scholarships.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM)
scholarships.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are high-level, integrated transnational study programmes at master's level designed and delivered by international partnerships of higher education institutions. An EMJM involves at least three higher education institutions from at least three different countries, and includes periods of study, research, traineeship, thesis preparation and defence. Each edition runs 1 to 2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits) and awards either a joint degree or multiple degrees. A new batch of selected Erasmus Mundus Masters is added to the list each year, and students apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme.
scholarships.deadline: Varies by consortium/programme - typically Dec-Feb for a Sept/Oct intake; no single central deadline
scholarships.deadline_display: Varies by consortium/programme - typically Dec-Feb for a Sept/Oct intake; no single central deadline
eligibility: Bachelor's degree (first degree) completed, or the candidate is in the final year of a bachelor's programme
Graduation before the master's programme starts
Officially recognised bachelor-equivalent level of learning (recognised under the legislation and practices of the degree-awarding country) is also accepted
benefits: Full tuition, approx. EUR 1,400/month stipend, travel allowance, installation allowance (exact figures vary slightly by consortium)
requirements: Bachelor's degree or final year of bachelor studies, with graduation before the programme starts
Full-time enrolment for the entire duration of the Master programme

Compulsory physical mobility: minimum two study periods in two countries, at least one an EU Member State or third country associated to the Programme, both different from the student's country of residence at enrolment, each at least one academic semester (30 ECTS; 20 ECTS exceptionally for 60-ECTS programmes)
Completion within 1 to 2 academic years, i.e. 60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits
No previous EMJM scholarship held
scholarships.duration: 1 to 2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits)
scholarships.application_period: Varies by consortium/programme - typically Dec-Feb for a Sept/Oct intake; no single central deadline
scholarships.selection_notes: Highly competitive. Selection depends on academic background, motivation, recommendation letters and programme-specific requirements.
scholarships.program_type: Joint Master Programme

scholarships.title: ICCR Scholarship (Suborno Jayanti Scheme)
scholarships.description: The Suborno Jayanti Scholarship Scheme is the ICCR scheme for nationals of Bangladesh, subsuming the earlier Bangladesh schemes previously offered by ICCR. Under it, the Government of India through ICCR provides scholarship at UG, PG and Ph.D level in Indian universities. Applications are made online on the ICCR A2A Scholarship Portal and must be submitted through the Indian Mission in the applicant's country, which then forwards them to empanelled Indian State and Central Universities. Registration for the 2026-27 academic year is closed and the portal currently lists 2026-27 as the only registration year.

scholarships.title: DAAD Scholarship
scholarships.degree: Mostly Master's/PhD (a few UG-eligible programmes exist but are rare)
scholarships.description: The DAAD scholarship database is the German Academic Exchange Service's official listing of its own funding programmes for international students and researchers, together with offers from other selected funding organisations. At the time of verification it returned 150 scholarship options, searchable by country, applicant type, scholarship purpose, subject and programme title. Applications are submitted to the specific programme rather than to a single central DAAD form, and each programme sets its own eligibility, deadline and award conditions. The database also links to the external funding guide www.funding-guide.de.

scholarships.title: MEXT (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship
scholarships.degree: UG/PG/PhD - separate application tracks: Undergraduate, Research Student (leads to Master's/PhD), Teacher Training, Japanese Studies, College of Technology
scholarships.description: The Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship is MEXT's scholarship programme for international students, offered in seven types: Research students, Teacher training students, Undergraduate students, Japanese studies students, College of technology students, Specialized training college students and Young Leaders Program students. There are two application routes: a recommendation from a Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission, or a recommendation from a Japanese university. The scholarship pays a monthly stipend, exempts tuition and provides a round-trip travel allowance (airfare), and in most tracks includes Japanese language training before or during study.

scholarships.title: France Excellence Charpak Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: France Excellence Charpak is the French government scholarship programme in India, divided into four sub-programmes that allow Indian students to study at undergraduate or postgraduate level in public and private institutions in France. The Master track is designed for one to two years of study at Master's level across all streams and fields, and awardees receive the status of Boursier du Government Français. The Master track pays a monthly living allowance of EUR 860 and covers visa and Campus France procedure fee exemption, student social security and complementary health insurance, accommodation assistance through Campus France in France, and reduced university restaurant meals at EUR 1. The scholarship does not cover travel expenses from India to France or within France, or any other expenses related to the awardee's stay.

scholarships.title: MOPGA Visiting Fellowship Program
scholarships.description: Since 2018 the Make Our Planet Great Again (MOPGA) initiative has been a flagship programme for postdoctoral mobility in France and one of the leading fellowship programmes of the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs. The 2027 call is the tenth edition, funded by MEAE in partnership with MESRE and implemented by Campus France, and enables young international researchers to carry out a research project in France. Each fellowship runs for 12 months and provides a monthly allowance of EUR 2,500, a EUR 500 settling-in allowance and health coverage including health insurance, civil liability insurance and repatriation assistance. Successful applicants receive the status of French Government Scholarship holder (BGF) and the fellowship is paid directly by Campus France.

scholarships.title: Deutschlandstipendium (Germany Scholarship)
scholarships.description: The Deutschlandstipendium is funded by the German Foreign Office with around 900 scholarships for excellent international students each year. It pays EUR 300 per month for 12 months, extendable to 24 months for master's students, plus insurance contributions. Applications are made directly to the university, which publishes its own application period, forms and subject-specific criteria, and either selects the scholars itself or forwards candidates for the DAI to decide. Eligibility requires being admitted to a German university and migrating to Germany to study.

scholarships.title: POSCO TJ Park Foundation Global Scholarship
scholarships.description: The POSCO Global Scholarship in Korea is the inbound component of the POSCO Global Scholarship operated by the POSCO TJ Park Foundation, and it is described by the Foundation as 'The Global Future Leaders Scholarship Program'. It funds non-Korean nationals admitted to Master's or doctoral programmes at designated Korean graduate schools, who must be recommended by their admitting institution. Master's students receive full tuition for four semesters plus living expenses of KRW 1,000,000 per month for 22 months, while doctoral and integrated master's-doctoral students receive full tuition for six semesters plus the same monthly living allowance for 36 months. A one-off KRW 1,000,000 settlement fee, National Health Insurance premiums and Korean language and cultural programmes are also provided.

Approximately 60 ESOP scholarships are assigned for the 2027/28 academic year, and the exact number depends on the availability of funds.

scholarships.title: Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Postdoctoral Fellowships
scholarships.description: MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships support researchers holding a PhD who wish to carry out their research activities abroad, acquire new skills and develop their careers. There are two types: European Postdoctoral Fellowships, lasting 12 to 24 months in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country and open to any nationality; and Global Postdoctoral Fellowships, lasting an outgoing phase of 12 to 24 months in a non-associated Third Country followed by a mandatory 12-month return phase, open only to nationals or long-term residents of EU Member States or Horizon Europe Associated Countries. The researcher is recruited by a host organisation, which submits the proposal through the EU Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal, and receives a living allowance, a mobility allowance and, where applicable, family, long-term leave and special needs allowances. The 2026 call closed on 9 September 2026 and the 2027 call opens on 7 April 2027 with a deadline of 8 September 2027, both indicative.

scholarships.title: Erasmus+ Student Exchange (Studying Abroad)
scholarships.description: Erasmus+ helps organise student and doctoral candidate exchanges within countries fully part of the Erasmus+ programme and to and from countries associated to Erasmus+. It is open to short-cycle, Bachelor's and Master's students and to doctoral candidates registered at a participating higher education institution and enrolled in studies leading to a recognised degree. There is no central application form: students apply through the international or Erasmus+ office of their own institution, which selects applicants fairly and transparently. The grant contributes to travel and daily living costs with amounts varying by destination and demand, and Erasmus+ students are exempt from tuition, registration, examination and laboratory or library fees at the receiving institution. Mobilities run from 2 to 12 months for long-term study, or 5 to 30 days for short-term blended mobility, with up to 12 months in total per study cycle.

scholarships.title: France Excellence Major Scholarship
scholarships.description: France Excellence-Major is a French government scholarship run by AEFE for the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs that supports the best non-French baccalaureat holders from the network of French schools abroad to continue their higher education in France. Around 800 foreign students are supported at any one time over five years of study, and about 200 new holders join each year. Applications require pre-selection by the head of the French school abroad and online entry on the dedicated Cascade application, followed by assessment by the French embassy's cultural cooperation service and a selection commission convened by AEFE each May. Selection weighs school results, a coherent orientation project, involvement in school life and extracurricular activity, and motivation for demanding French higher education. Holders receive a family-need-rated monthly allowance of EUR 280 or EUR 860, complementary health cover, and, at the higher rates, round-trip travel and CROUS housing.

scholarships.title: Humboldt Research Fellowship
scholarships.description: The Humboldt Research Fellowship sponsors researchers with above-average qualifications from across the globe to conduct their own research at a German host institution. For postdocs the monthly fellowship amount is €3,000 and for experienced researchers €3,600, plus additional benefits. On top of the fellowship amount the Foundation provides family benefits for children and partners, subsidies for private full health insurance, and travel expense allowances, as well as personal support throughout the sponsorship. The host institute generally receives an allowance for research costs of €800 per month for natural sciences and engineering, or €500 for humanities and social sciences.

scholarships.deadline_display: Three calls annually: March 15, July 15, November 15 (2026 schedule)
eligibility: Postdocs: did you complete your doctorate - or equivalent academic qualification - during the last four years?
Experienced researchers: did you complete your doctorate - or equivalent academic qualification - during the last twelve years?
Postdocs: have you been published in academic journals and by publishing houses that are reviewed according to international standards?

Experienced researchers: is your academic profile substantiated by an extensive list of publications including important papers in which you acted as thematic lead, and do you hold a leadership role commensurate with your career level (for example assistant professor, lecturer, head of an independent research group or higher)?

If a doctorate in your field or country of origin is not possible or uncommon, you can still apply up to 16 years after completing your master's or other postgraduate degree provided you have a publication record commensurate with your career level.

You are not a German national. If you are a German national, or if you obtained your university entrance qualification and university degree, or your university degree and your doctorate, in Germany, you can apply if you have lived and worked abroad for more than ten years and intend to continue doing so long-term. Have you lived and worked abroad for more than five years? You can still apply if there is a strong connection to your current country of residence (permanent employment, additional citizenship etc.).
For your application to be successful, you may not have lived in Germany for longer than a total of 90 days within the 18-month period prior to submitting your application.

A researcher from an academic institution of your choice in Germany will provide you with a mentoring agreement and written confirmation that research facilities are available, and will compile a detailed review for you.

You can provide two expert reviews. For postdocs: your doctoral supervisor and one other researcher - outside of your institute, if possible. For experienced researchers: important collaborative partners and/or researchers at your own institute as well as other institutes - outside your country of origin, if possible.

Natural sciences and engineering: you must have a good knowledge of German or English. Humanities, social sciences and medicine: you must have a good knowledge of German if this is necessary for conducting your research successfully; otherwise good knowledge of English will suffice.
You may not apply for the Humboldt Research Fellowship if you have already received sponsorship directly from the Humboldt Foundation (research fellowship or award).
benefits: Monthly fellowship amount EUR 3,000 (postdocs) or EUR 3,600 (experienced researchers)
Travel allowance

requirements: Submit the necessary documents to the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation online only

Applications are academically evaluated by a peer review process based on: academic career and academic record to date (mobility, determination, thematic scope, academic productivity); quality of the key publications named in the application; originality and innovative potential of your proposed research; your future potential; and your independent research profile (for experienced researchers). The assessment also considers the individual life journey and educational background in terms of equal opportunities and accessibility. The Foundation expects 20-25% of the applications received to be approved.

scholarships.title: Australia Awards Fellowships
scholarships.description: Australia Awards Fellowships is a DFAT competitive grants programme in which an Australian organisation - never an individual - applies for funding to host a Fellow nominated by an overseas counterpart organisation in an eligible developing country. The grant is up to $34,500 per Fellow for a single Fellowship of 2 to 52 weeks, and the Australian Host Organisation must add a mandatory cash and/or in-kind co-contribution; DFAT publishes no tuition component, no living-cost rate and no separate airfare figure. Every application must first clear a mandatory compliance gate - correct format, current ABN, no more than six applications per organisation, no more than 15 DFAT-funded Fellows, at least two weeks in Australia, in-partner country activity, and alignment with one of six development priority areas - or it is never assessed. The Fellow must travel without family, cannot hold or be seeking Australian permanent residency, and must be a citizen of and resident in one of DFAT's listed eligible countries; Round 21 closed on 16 January 2026 and Round 22 is expected to open in the final quarter of 2026 with no date published.

scholarships.title: Australian Government Research Training Program (RTP)
scholarships.degree: Research Doctorate, Research Master's (Higher Degree by Research)
scholarships.description: The Research Training Program is Australian Government funding that flows to eligible universities as block grants, which those universities then use to offer scholarships to students doing a research doctorate or research masters. A scholarship may comprise one or more of three published components - a tuition fees offset, a stipend for general living costs, and allowances for the ancillary costs of a higher degree by research - and it is the university, not the Department, that decides the mix, applies, selects and sets the deadline. Stipend rates are indexed annually and published as a base and a maximum (2027: $35,550 base, $55,537 maximum), so the amount you receive depends on your provider and your stipend level rather than on a national figure. Support runs 3 to 4 years full-time for a research doctorate, or up to 2 years full-time for a research masters, and from 3 December 2025 recipients must acknowledge the Commonwealth's contribution using the RTP's own DOI and add it to any ORCID profile they hold.
eligibility: Enrolled or commencing an accredited research doctorate or research master's at an eligible Australian university.
Meet university-specific application and selection criteria.
International students: universities may award up to 10% of RTP funding to overseas students.
benefits: RTP Stipend: base rate AUD 34,315/year (2026); max AUD 53,608/year (2026). Universities may offer any rate within this range.
RTP Fees Offset: 100% tuition fee exemption for standard program duration.
RTP Allowance: relocation and thesis allowance.
Part-time stipend rate is 50% of full-time rate.
requirements: Contact the chosen eligible higher education provider directly; RTP scholarship applications cannot be made through the Department of Education
Apply through that provider's own application process and meet its selection criteria and deadline
Be undertaking, or intending to undertake, a research doctorate or research masters degree (HDR) at an eligible provider
Study at the student load the scholarship is awarded for, since the published period-of-support bands differ between full-time and part-time loads
From 3 December 2025, acknowledge the Commonwealth's contribution in material relating to the HDR project, using the published form of words with the RTP DOI
If you hold an ORCID profile, include the RTP DOI in that profile; there is no requirement to create an ORCID profile if you do not already have one
Agree the period of support with the provider - it is not extended for paid recreation leave or approved personal leave, only for approved suspension and additional approved paid leave

For the industry internship weighting, have the written internship agreement in place between the student, the HEP and the research end-user within 18 months of commencement (full-time) or 36 months (part-time), with an eligible research end-user at the time the agreement is made
scholarships.duration: Research doctorate: a minimum of 3 years and up to a maximum of 4 years at the discretion of the higher education provider for a full-time student load, and a minimum of 6 years up to a maximum of 8 years for a part-time student load. Research masters: up to 2 years full-time and up to 4 years part-time. A student's period of support is not increased for periods of paid recreation leave or personal leave approved by the provider; it is increased by the length of any approved RTP suspension, or any additional approved paid personal leave, paid parental leave, paid partner leave, or paid family and domestic violence leave.
scholarships.selection_notes:
No selection criteria are published by the Department of Education. Each HEP runs its own application and selection process and publishes its own criteria; the Department page contains no ranking, weighting, pass mark or assessment panel.
The published scheme-level constraints that shape any selection are: the degree must be a research doctorate or research masters; the provider must be eligible for research block grants; the period of support must sit inside the published band for the degree and student load; and the scholarship may comprise one or more of the three published components.
Published incentive rule that affects provider behaviour: an additional weighting of 2.0 within the RTP funding allocation formula is applied to each research doctorate student reported from 2022 as completing their course having undertaken an eligible industry internship.
Published allocation rule that affects how generous a provider can be: 2026 RTP grant amounts are allocated on a formula reflecting each provider's relative performance in attracting research income and supporting students to complete HDRs.

scholarships.title: Brandeis University Wien International Scholarship
scholarships.description: The Wien International Scholarship Program, established at Brandeis University in 1958, brings undergraduate students from around the world to campus. It is awarded to exceptional international applicants who show strong academic achievement and extracurricular or community involvement, and it meets the full demonstrated financial need of each recipient based on a complete review of financial documentation. There is no separate application: candidates apply to Brandeis through the Common Application or Coalition Application and are considered automatically, with the award notice included in the admission decision. International applicants file the CSS Profile and any additional documentation by Nov. 2 (Early Decision I / Early Action) or Jan. 15 (Early Decision II / Regular Decision), and scholars renew annually with a March 1 renewal filing.

scholarships.title: University of Minnesota Global Excellence Scholarship
scholarships.description: The Global Excellence Scholarship (GES) is a competitive, merit-based award for international freshmen and transfer students at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities. All admitted freshmen studying on an F-1 visa who complete their admission application by the published deadlines are automatically reviewed, and admitted transfer students on an F-1 visa who complete by the priority deadline are automatically considered; there is no separate scholarship application. The award is partial - the University states it does not offer a full tuition waiver or scholarship - and the University's International Undergraduate Fact Book states the value as up to $15,000 each year for up to four years. Deadlines follow admission: Early Action I November 1, Early Action II December 1, Regular January 1. Applicants on temporary visas must also complete the Certification of Finances form.

scholarships.title: Clark University Global Scholars Program
scholarships.description: This record covers Clark University's institutional undergraduate scholarship portfolio rather than a single named award. The headline award is the Presidential Scholarship, which covers the full cost of tuition plus on-campus housing and meals for the four years of undergraduate study, with recipients still responsible for additional costs of roughly $12,000 to $15,000 per year; a second named award, the Davis United World College Scholars Program, is a need-based grant of up to $15,000 per year. There is no separate scholarship application: scholarships are decided inside the admissions process, bundled with the admission decision and made more generous in the binding Early Decision rounds, which publish decisions before Thanksgiving alongside more scholarship funding and a higher admission rate. Underneath the named awards sit institutional need-based aid that Clark reports as reaching 99% of first-year students with 98% of aid in the form of non-repayable grants, while international students are reported as typically paying around $40,000 per year after aid against a total cost of attendance of approximately $85,000.

scholarships.title: Michigan State University International Merit Scholarships

The main award is the MSU Non-resident Scholarship, granted at six levels from $3,000 to $18,000 per year on academic performance, with decisions released by mid-February. Additional awards include the Red Cedar Scholarship for alumni dependants and grandchildren, the Presidential Study Abroad Scholarship, and three Honors College awards including the $13,000 Excellence Scholarship and a research Professorial Assistantship. MSU warns that only a limited number of students considered receive offers and that meeting the criteria does not guarantee one; applying by the 1 November early action deadline guarantees a decision by 15 January.

scholarships.title: Clarendon Fund Scholarships
scholarships.description: The Clarendon Fund offers over 200 new fully-funded scholarships each year to outstanding graduate scholars at the University of Oxford, covering course fees in full and paying a grant for living expenses. There is no separate scholarship application: candidates are considered automatically if they apply for a new full-time or part-time Master's or DPhil by the December or January admissions deadline for their course, and departments nominate to their division for divisional ranking. Selection criteria are academic record, future potential and aptitude, and student motivation, and successful candidates are usually notified by the end of April.
scholarships.deadline: There is no separate Clarendon deadline: you must apply to your Oxford course by the December or January admissions deadline, whichever is relevant to your course. scholarships.description: The Nanyang President's Graduate Scholarship (NPGS) is a competitive and prestigious scholarship scheme offered by Nanyang Technological University to encourage outstanding graduates or final-year students to take their first step towards a leading research career by studying full-time for a PhD at NTU. It is described as the premier scholarship granted by NTU's President, recognising PhD students who exemplify exceptional academic, research and leadership qualities. Open to all nationalities, it requires an Honours (Highest Distinction) or equivalent at Bachelor's level, or official documentation confirming the candidate is on track to achieve it. Monthly stipends revised with effect from January 2026 are S$5,300 for Singapore Citizens, S$4,800 for Singapore Permanent Residents and S$4,300 for international students, with CPF contributions on top for Citizens. The award also covers the annual tuition fee and provides an overseas conference allowance of up to S$5,000 per financial year, an annual book allowance of S$500, a one-off IT allowance of S$1,500, a one-off thesis allowance of S$600 and priority for campus accommodation. There is no bond attached to the scholarship, though international students must perform teaching or laboratory supervision duties under the Graduate Assistantship Programme.

scholarships.description: The Lee Kong Chian Scholars' Programme is one of Singapore Management University's most prestigious undergraduate scholarships, made possible by a gift from the Lee Foundation, with up to 60 scholarships funded. It is open to full-time SMU first-year undergraduates of any nationality taking a single or double degree programme, and requires a second major or an equivalent breadth requirement, demonstrated leadership and communications skills, and a substantial record of co-curricular activity or community service. Benefits comprise a waiver of annual subsidised tuition fees for regular terms for up to four years, a S$16,000 Global Opportunities grant funding overseas exchange, community service or competitions, a S$5,000 annual living allowance, a S$1,800 one-time computer allowance, and development opportunities from SMU's Student Success Centre. scholarships.description: The Griffin Financial Aid Office at Harvard College provides need-based aid that allows Harvard to bring the best students regardless of their ability to pay. Financial aid is available to foreign students on exactly the same basis as for American students; because international students are not eligible for federal funding, the College applies its own job and scholarship money. Families with income up to $200,000 receive free tuition plus aid for additional costs. Aid is need-blind with respect to admission.

Need is calculated as cost of attendance minus family contribution, with direct expenses of tuition, fees, food and housing and indirect expenses such as travel, books, supplies and laundry. Families with total annual income below $125,000 with typical assets can expect no parent contribution, while families earning between $125,000 and $175,000 with typical assets can expect a scholarship or grants covering the full cost of tuition. International applicants file the CSS Profile with school code 3351, or the International Student Financial Aid Application if the CSS fee is a serious hardship. Financial aid deadlines are November 1 for Early Decision and February 1 for Regular Decision.

scholarships.title: Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme (AKF ISP) - Next Cycle, Opening Early 2027
scholarships.description: The Aga Khan Foundation's International Scholarship Programme (AKF ISP), established in 1969 by Prince Karim Aga Khan IV, is an opportunity for outstanding scholars from selected countries who have no other means of financing their studies to pursue postgraduate education. It has supported more than 1,500 students. Awards are structured as half grant and half loan, so 50 percent of the award must be repaid, and they cover tuition and student living expenses. Priority goes to Master's programmes; PhD students receive funding for the first two years only. The 2026-2027 cycle is closed and the next cycle opens in early 2027.
scholarships.deadline: The 2026-2027 application cycle is now closed. The next cycle will open in early 2027.

demonstrate a thoughtful, reliable, multi-source funding plan that covers all years of study;
be admitted to a reputable postgraduate institution;
be starting the first year of the programme; and
have strong leadership potential, professional experience, extracurricular and/or entrepreneurial achievements, and volunteer contributions.
Note: preference is given to young professionals under 30 years of age.

The programme is available in Afghanistan, Australia, Bangladesh, Egypt, India, Kenya, Kyrgyz Republic, Madagascar, Mozambique, New Zealand, Pakistan, Syria, Tajikistan, Tanzania, and Uganda. In countries such as Canada, Portugal and the USA, applications are accepted from those who are originally from one of the countries listed above. At this time, AKF ISP is not available to students who wish to study in the United Kingdom or Russia.

For PhD students, the first two years of study

requirements: Awards are provided according to need, but the AKF ISP should be considered a resource of last resort; applicants should secure multiple sources of funding to reduce the amount requested.

Applications for part-time programmes and short-term courses are not considered.

Repayment of the loan component, which includes a service charge, begins six months after the first of the following events: a) graduation, b) termination of studies, or c) withdrawal of support following failure to meet the academic standards expected of ISP students.
To maintain an AKF ISP award, the award holder must demonstrate good academic standing as well as ongoing financial need during the course of the postgraduate programme.

scholarships.title: Rotary Peace Fellowship
scholarships.description: The Rotary Peace Fellowship is funded by The Rotary Foundation and awards up to 170 fellowships a year for leaders with work experience in peace and development to study at one of eight Rotary Peace Centers. Each year up to 50 fellowships fund master's degrees and up to 120 fund professional development certificate studies at partner universities. Fellowships cover tuition and fees, room and board, round-trip transportation, and internship and field-study expenses. Master's programmes run 15 to 24 months and include a self-designed two- to three-month field study, while the certificate programme is a one-year blended learning course for working professionals that includes field studies and a social change initiative. Fellowships cannot be used for doctoral study. Applications open in February and the global deadline is 15 May; the 2027-28 cycle is closed and the 2028-29 cycle opens in February 2027.

scholarships.title: International Talents @unibo — Scholarships for International Students Enrolling in Second Cycle Degree Programmes
scholarships.description: The University of Bologna awards 30 International Talents @unibo study grants each year to international students who matriculate for the first time in the first year of a Second Cycle (Laurea Magistrale) degree programme. Each grant is worth EUR 6,500 gross per academic year and is awarded for two academic years, and successful applicants also receive a full tuition fee waiver, paying only EUR 157.04 in regional taxes, stamp duty and insurance premium. scholarships.title: MOFA Taiwan Scholarship (Taiwan Scholarship Program)
scholarships.degree: Bachelor's, Master's, PhD, plus pre-degree Mandarin Language Enrichment Program (LEP)
scholarships.description: The Taiwan Scholarship Program of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of China (Taiwan), funds international students for degree programmes or a pre-degree Mandarin Language Enrichment Program at Mandarin-teaching institutions affiliated with MOE-accredited universities. Recipients receive a monthly stipend of NT$33,000 for degree programmes or NT$28,000 for the LEP, plus one-way economy-class air tickets for direct flights to and from Taiwan, and must cover all other expenses themselves. The award period is one year for the LEP, up to four years for undergraduate and doctoral study and two years for a master's, with a five-year total cap. Applications are accepted from 1 February to 31 March each year, and the programme is open to students of any country except mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau, in principle prioritising Taiwan's diplomatic partners.
scholarships.deadline: from February 1 to March 31
scholarships.deadline_display: from February 1 to March 31
eligibility: Is a high school graduate or above with an excellent academic record, of good moral character and has no criminal record.
Is not a national of the Republic of China (Taiwan).
Is not an overseas compatriot student.
Has never attended an educational institution in Taiwan at the same level of degree or LEP that he/she intends to apply for.
Is not an exchange student through any cooperation agreement between a foreign university/college and an educational institute in Taiwan while receiving the Scholarship.
Has not previously had a Scholarship revoked by an ROC government agency or other relevant institution.
In principle, holds citizenship of a country that has diplomatic relations with Taiwan; special consideration may be given to students from other countries.
The programme is not applicable to students from mainland China, Hong Kong or Macau.
benefits: NT$33,000 per month stipend for degree programmes.
NT$28,000 per month stipend for the pre-degree LEP.
One-way economy-class air tickets for direct flights to and from Taiwan.
Possible university-level tuition and miscellaneous fee reductions, at each institution's discretion.
requirements: High school graduate or above with an excellent academic record and good moral character.
No criminal record.
Not a national of the Republic of China (Taiwan) and not an overseas compatriot student.
No prior study in Taiwan at the level being applied for.
Not simultaneously an exchange student under a university cooperation agreement while holding the Scholarship.
No previous Scholarship revocation by an ROC government agency or other relevant institution.
scholarships.duration: Pre-degree LEP: one year. Degree programmes: undergraduate maximum four years, master's maximum two years, doctoral maximum four years. Award periods must be continuous with no breaks and cannot exceed five years in total.
scholarships.application_period: Annual window from 1 February to 31 March, applying to the Taiwan Scholarship cycle for the following academic year. The February-March 2026 window has closed; the next is expected 1 February to 31 March 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: The Scholarship is in principle granted to students from countries that have diplomatic relations with Taiwan; special consideration may also be given to students from other countries. Selection follows the programme guidelines published by MOFA and administered for applicants through the Taiwan Scholarships portal.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship (Taiwan Scholarship Program of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
scholarships.name: MOFA Taiwan Scholarship (Taiwan Scholarship Program)

scholarships.title: Huayu Enrichment Scholarship (HES), Ministry of Education, Republic of China (Taiwan)
scholarships.description: The Ministry of Education of the Republic of China (Taiwan) established the Huayu Enrichment Scholarship to encourage international students to study Mandarin Chinese in Taiwan. The award funds a 2-month summer course or a 3-month, 6-month, 9-month or one-year course, and pays a monthly stipend of NT$28,000. Applicants must be foreign nationals aged 18 or over with an excellent academic record and good moral character, must already have applied to a Chinese language centre, and must submit their documents to the ROC overseas office for their country of nationality. MOE publishes no single deadline date, noting only that applications are made 'before the deadline specified in the scholarship guidelines issued by that authorized overseas office (usually in January or February each year)'.
scholarships.deadline: Applicants must apply to the authorized overseas office for their country of nationality 'before the deadline specified in the scholarship guidelines issued by that authorized overseas office (usually in January or February each year)'. MOE publishes no single fixed date, so no ISO deadline date can be recorded.
scholarships.deadline_display: Applicants must apply to the authorized overseas office for their country of nationality 'before the deadline specified in the scholarship guidelines issued by that authorized overseas office (usually in January or February each year)'. MOE publishes no single fixed date, so no ISO deadline date can be recorded.
eligibility: A foreign person (not an ROC passport holder and not an overseas compatriot student).
At least 18 years old.
Has graduated from secondary school or has studied at post-secondary level.
Has an excellent academic record.
Is of good moral character.
Excluded: a person currently studying Chinese in Taiwan, or who has previously undertaken a degree programme in Taiwan.
Excluded: a person who has previously received a Huayu Enrichment Scholarship, a TUSA Global Ambassador Scholarship, or a Taiwan Scholarship.
Excluded: an exchange student currently studying or researching in Taiwan under an academic cooperation agreement between a Taiwan university/college and an overseas institution.
Excluded: a person currently studying or researching in Taiwan who is receiving a scholarship or financial assistance from any Taiwan government agency or any educational institution in Taiwan.

Exception: the graduation and academic records of a foreign national recommended or selected by a foreign government, institution or educational institution under an education cooperation agreement are not subject to the preceding exclusion.
benefits: Monthly stipend of NT$28,000 for the duration of the awarded course (2-month summer course, or 3, 6, 9 or 12 months).
requirements: Meet the five published eligibility conditions and avoid all five published exclusions.
Be at least 18 years old.
Have graduated from secondary school or studied at post-secondary level with an excellent academic record.
Be of good moral character.
Have already applied to a Chinese language center, and supply proof of that application.
Submit all five required document types listed by MOE.
Apply before the deadline set by the relevant ROC overseas mission.
scholarships.duration: A 2-month summer course, or a 3-month, 6-month, 9-month or one-year course.
scholarships.application_period: Annual, with the deadline set by each applicant's own ROC overseas mission or representative office, which MOE says is 'usually in January or February each year'. The round for the current cycle has closed as of 2026-10-04; the next nominations are expected in January or February 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: The scholarships are awarded through Republic of China (Taiwan) embassies and overseas missions (Representative Offices) on the basis of merit, using the guidelines each office issues for its own jurisdiction.
scholarships.program_type: Government non-degree language scholarship (Ministry of Education Huayu Enrichment Scholarship, awarded through ROC overseas missions on merit)
scholarships.name: Huayu Enrichment Scholarship (HES), Ministry of Education, Republic of China (Taiwan)

scholarships.title: Taiwan International Graduate Program (TIGP) - Ph.D. Scholarship and Stipend, Academia Sinica
scholarships.description: The Taiwan International Graduate Program (TIGP), administered by Academia Sinica with partner universities, admits international students to fourteen English-taught Ph.D. programmes and pays a tax-free stipend of NT$40,000 per month for the first year, extendable for one further year for students who perform well. Academia Sinica also subsidises the difference between international and domestic tuition fees for five consecutive years, but students still pay the domestic tuition rate, stated as roughly NT$28,000-31,000 per semester for the first four semesters and NT$16,000-20,000 per semester for the remainder. Applications are submitted online between 1 November and 1 February (GMT+8) with no application fee, and admission results are usually announced in late June or early July for enrolment the following fall.
scholarships.deadline: The TIGP Admission Office receives online applications 'from November 1st to February 1st every year' (GMT+8). The most recent cycle, for fall 2026 entry, closed at 1 February 2026 and admissions results were announced on 20 July 2026. No application announcement for the next cycle had been posted as of 2026-10-04, so no exact calendar date is recorded.
scholarships.deadline_display: The TIGP Admission Office receives online applications 'from November 1st to February 1st every year' (GMT+8). The most recent cycle, for fall 2026 entry, closed at 1 February 2026 and admissions results were announced on 20 July 2026. No application announcement for the next cycle had been posted as of 2026-10-04, so no exact calendar date is recorded.
eligibility: International applicant seeking admission to one of the fourteen TIGP Ph.D. programmes.
Must satisfy the general and programme-specific admission requirements published on the TIGP site for the chosen programme.
Must not already hold the degree level to which they are applying, per TIGP's general admission requirements.
No application fee is required.
benefits: Tax-free monthly stipend of NT$40,000 (NT$34,000 + NT$6,000) for the first year.
Stipend extended for one additional year for students who perform well.
International tuition surcharge fully subsidised for five consecutive years, leaving students at the domestic tuition rate.
Eligibility to apply separately for the Presidential Fellowship, Research Performance Fellowship, Rising Star Fellowship, PhD Supplemental Stipend Program and Travel Grants.
requirements: Apply online through the TIGP application system between 1 November and 1 February (GMT+8).
Meet the general admission requirements and the specific requirements of the chosen Ph.D. programme.
Select a thesis advisor before the end of the first year of study.
Uphold the academic integrity standards of Academia Sinica and the partner university.
Confirm tuition arrangements with the programme secretary, since the domestic tuition rate varies by partner university.
scholarships.duration: PhD programme of three years. The stipend is paid for the first year and, for students who perform well, extended for one more year; after the scholarship/stipend allowance period, further financial support depends on the individual thesis advisor.
scholarships.application_period: Annual, 1 November to 1 February (GMT+8). TIGP posts a 'TIGP Application Announcement' each November (the 2026 one was published 2025-11-01). Admission results are usually announced in late June or early July, and admitted applicants enrol in the following fall semester.
scholarships.selection_notes: Admission is decided per Ph.D. programme. TIGP states that admission results are usually announced in late June or early July, and each programme publishes its own admission criteria and evaluation. A research proposal and interview requirements are set at programme level.
scholarships.program_type: Research-based doctoral scholarship programme administered by a research institute (Academia Sinica) with partner universities
scholarships.name: Taiwan International Graduate Program (TIGP) - Ph.D. Scholarship and Stipend, Academia Sinica

scholarships.title: International Industrial Talents Education Special Program (INTENSE Program)
scholarships.description: The International Industrial Talents Education Special Program (INTENSE Program) is a Ministry of Education initiative, run with the National Development Council, participating universities and partner companies to recruit international students into industry-linked degree programmes in key fields such as STEM, finance and semiconductors. Admitted students receive full tuition and credit waivers for up to two years, a one-way flight ticket to Taiwan, initial administrative expense support and a monthly living allowance of at least NT$10,000 paid by the partner company, plus paid internships, in exchange for an obligation to work in Taiwan after graduation. Applications are made to individual participating universities, which publish their own deadlines for each Spring and Fall intake, so there is no single programme-wide application date.
scholarships.deadline: There is no single INTENSE deadline. Each participating university sets its own application window and nomination deadline per intake, and the two intakes do not coincide. Windows published by partner universities for 2027 Spring include 10 September to 12 October 2026 (NCHU), 1 to 22 October 2026 (NCU) and 21 September to 23 October 2026 (KMU), all GMT+8; for 2027 Fall, NTUT publishes a student nomination deadline of 10 March 2027. Applications for several 2027 Spring intakes are open as of 2026-10-04.
scholarships.deadline_display: There is no single INTENSE deadline. Each participating university sets its own application window and nomination deadline per intake, and the two intakes do not coincide. Windows published by partner universities for 2027 Spring include 10 September to 12 October 2026 (NCHU), 1 to 22 October 2026 (NCU) and 21 September to 23 October 2026 (KMU), all GMT+8; for 2027 Fall, NTUT publishes a student nomination deadline of 10 March 2027. Applications for several 2027 Spring intakes are open as of 2026-10-04.
eligibility: Must meet the MOE Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan.
Must apply to a specific approved INTENSE programme at a participating university, in one of the key industry fields (commonly STEM, finance and semiconductors).
English-taught programmes: CEFR B1 English proficiency required at admission, and TOCFL Level A2 (Listening and Reading) by the end of the first semester of the second academic year.
Chinese-taught programmes: TOCFL Level B1 (Listening and Reading) required.
Some programmes restrict eligible nationalities, for example Vietnam, Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand; others accept students of all nationalities.
Must satisfy the participating university's own programme requirements, including academic performance within the top 50% of the class and a conduct score of not lower than 80 points.
benefits: Full tuition and credit waiver for up to two years.
One-way flight ticket to Taiwan plus initial administrative expense support.
Monthly stipend of at least NT$10,000 for up to two years, paid by the partner company.
Paid summer internships, with allowances not lower than the minimum wage under a bilingual contract.
Priority employment in Taiwan after graduation with a partner company.
requirements: Meet the MOE Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan.
Meet the participating university's programme-specific academic and language requirements.
Maintain grades in the top 50% of the class and a conduct score of not lower than 80 points, or equivalent to Grade A.
Accept the mandatory internship stage and the employment obligation in Taiwan.
For students already studying in Taiwan at junior or senior undergraduate level, academic performance within the top 50% of the class and a conduct grade of at least 80 or Grade A.
scholarships.duration: Typically a two-year degree programme of study plus internship, followed by employment in Taiwan.
scholarships.application_period: Two intakes a year. Spring intake first round runs from early October to late December and second round from early April to late June; the Fall intake mirrors those two rounds. Each participating university publishes its own exact dates, so no single application period applies.
scholarships.selection_notes: The university's proposal must pass joint review by the Ministry of Education and the relevant ministries before the programme can run, and participating universities must sign contracts with companies to provide student living allowances and internships. Admission is therefore per programme and per intake, with results typically announced in the middle of the year for a September start and in mid-January for a February start.
scholarships.program_type: Industry-academia collaboration degree programme (MOE specialised class) with a compulsory employment obligation in Taiwan after graduation
scholarships.name: International Industrial Talents Education Special Program (INTENSE Program)

scholarships.title: NTU International Outstanding Graduate Student Scholarship
scholarships.description: The NTU International Outstanding Graduate Student Scholarship supports current international graduate students at National Taiwan University through a matching-fund structure: NTU waives the student's tuition, while the student's thesis or dissertation supervisor pays a monthly research-assistant salary, with published minimums of TWD 6,000 per month for two years for master's students and TWD 8,000 per month for three years for PhD students, before tax. Applicants must first secure a professor willing to sponsor them and sign the university's word form, and must pass an annual review to keep the award. The published application period is 23 April to 15 May, through NTU's International Degree Current Student System, and roughly half of applicants are awarded.
scholarships.deadline: The published application period on NTU's International Student Services scholarships page is April 23, 2026 - May 15, 2026, submitted through the International Degree Current Student System. The 2026 window has closed; the same window is expected for the next cycle.
scholarships.deadline_display: The published application period on NTU's International Student Services scholarships page is April 23, 2026 - May 15, 2026, submitted through the International Degree Current Student System. The 2026 window has closed; the same window is expected for the next cycle.
eligibility: Must be a current international graduate student at NTU.
Overseas Chinese students and Mainland Chinese students are excluded.
Must have a thesis or dissertation supervisor willing to sponsor the award and sign the university's word form.
Must pass the annual review to continue receiving the scholarship.
benefits: NTU tuition waiver.
Supervisor-paid monthly research-assistant salary, minimum TWD 6,000 per month for master's students (two years) and TWD 8,000 per month for PhD students (three years), before tax.
Renewal for up to two years for master's students and three years for PhD students, subject to annual review.
requirements: Be a current international graduate student at NTU (overseas Chinese and Mainland Chinese students are excluded).
Secure a sponsoring thesis or dissertation supervisor who will sign the word form and pay the research-assistant salary.
Submit past years' transcripts or an Advisor Evaluation Form.
Submit a recommendation letter for the Outstanding International Graduate Student Scholarship and a curriculum vitae.
Pass the annual review to retain the award.
scholarships.duration: Minimum monthly support for two years for master's students and three years for PhD students, subject to passing an annual review.
scholarships.application_period: Annual, with a published application period of 23 April to 15 May for existing international degree students at NTU, applying through the International Degree Current Student System.
scholarships.selection_notes: Decision on NTU scholarships is made by the professors of the department to which the applicant belongs. NTU's scholarship FAQ states that about half of applicants receive scholarships. Renewal requires passing review each year.
scholarships.program_type: University merit scholarship with a matching-fund structure (university tuition waiver plus a thesis supervisor's research-assistant salary)
scholarships.name: NTU International Outstanding Graduate Student Scholarship

scholarships.title: NYCU Elite Ph.D. Scholarship for New Students
scholarships.description: The NYCU Elite Ph.D. Scholarship for New Students awards a monthly stipend of NT$33,000 together with a tuition waiver for two years to new doctoral students at National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University who have outstanding grades and hold no other scholarship or grant from the Taiwan government. It is not open to direct application: NYCU states that the award is made on the basis of recommendations from the college and a review by the scholarship committee. Recipients must submit semester transcripts and tuition payment receipts before a per-semester deadline to remain eligible, and the stipend is in principle deposited on the 10th of each month. The tuition waiver covers basic tuition only, with dormitory, insurance and campus facility fees remaining payable.
eligibility: Must be a new Ph.D. student at National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University.
Must have outstanding grades.
Must not have received any scholarship or grant from the Taiwan government.
Must be nominated by the candidate's college and selected by the scholarship committee; students cannot apply directly.
benefits: Monthly stipend of NT$33,000.
Full tuition waiver for two years.
In principle, the monthly stipend is deposited on the 10th of each month.
requirements: Be a new Ph.D. student at NYCU with outstanding grades.
Not hold any scholarship or grant from the Taiwan government.
Be nominated by the college and selected by the scholarship committee.
As a recipient, submit transcripts and tuition payment receipts every semester before the specified deadline.
Renew during the application period announced by the OIA.
scholarships.duration: Two years of monthly stipend plus tuition waiver, per NYCU's published 'Scholarship Content and Duration'.
scholarships.application_period: Not student-applied. New Ph.D. places are nominated by the candidate's college and reviewed by the scholarship committee within NYCU's doctoral admission cycle. Existing recipients must submit transcripts and tuition payment receipts each semester before a per-semester deadline to remain eligible in the following semester, and renewals are handled in the application period announced by the OIA.
scholarships.selection_notes: The award is based on recommendations from the college and a review by the scholarship committee, not on a student application. Full terms are set out in NYCU's scholarship regulations.
scholarships.program_type: University nomination-based doctoral scholarship (college recommendation and scholarship committee review, not a direct student application)

scholarships.name: NYCU Elite Ph.D. Scholarship for New Students

scholarships.title: MOE Elite Scholarship Program for Lecturers from South and Southeast Asian and African Countries
scholarships.description: The MOE Elite Scholarship Program was created by the Ministry of Education of the Republic of China (Taiwan) under its New Southbound Policy to encourage university lecturers from South and Southeast Asian and African countries to pursue graduate degrees in Taiwan, with priority given to doctoral study. Awardees receive a total monthly award of NT$25,000 for up to two years of a master's programme or three years of a doctorate, reviewed annually; participating universities deduct tuition and credit fees from that total and pay the remainder to the student as a monthly stipend, which at Taipei Tech works out at around NT$14,000 per month in years one to three and NT$12,000 in year four. Applicants must currently hold a lecturer or more senior post at a university in an eligible country with that position on hold, must supply an up-to-date English Lecturer Certificate, and apply through the participating university, which submits the case for MOE review. Around 100 places are awarded per academic year across a three-year cycle.
scholarships.deadline: No central deadline is published. The scholarship site publishes guidelines, forms and comparison tables, and directs every applicant to their local Taiwan Representative Office, which owns the application timing.
scholarships.deadline_display: No central deadline is published. The scholarship site publishes guidelines, forms and comparison tables, and directs every applicant to their local Taiwan Representative Office, which owns the application timing.
eligibility: Must be a university lecturer, assistant professor or professor currently employed at a public or private higher education institution in an eligible country.

Eligible Southeast and South Asian countries: Indonesia, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, India, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, Myanmar, Cambodia, Laos, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Bhutan.

African route: applicants from any African country who are either current university lecturers or professors with an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate in English, or have at least three years of university researcher experience in an African country with research publications or papers.
Must be a citizen of the country where they hold the teaching position.
The teaching position must be on hold because of the studies.
Must provide an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate in English; the African researcher route requires an employment certificate in English plus research publications.
Must not hold Taiwan (R.O.C.) nationality or overseas Chinese student status.

Must not be enrolled in, or hold a retained admission at, a university in Taiwan. This restriction does not apply to a student on course to graduate who is pursuing a next degree, provided they are still a lecturer from a South or Southeast Asian country.
Must not previously have studied in Taiwan for a degree at the same level.
Must not be an exchange or dual-degree student under a partnership agreement with an overseas institution.
Must not have received stipends through this programme for more than three years.
Must not be a recipient of any other scholarship or financial assistance from a Taiwan government agency or a foreign government.
Must satisfy the participating university's own admission and English-taught programme requirements.
benefits: NT$25,000 per month total award from MOE, of which tuition and credit fees are deducted first.
Full tuition fee subsidy out of the award; Taipei Tech states tuition and fees are subsidised for up to 4 years.

Post-tuition monthly stipend. At Taipei Tech this works out at around NT$14,000 per month in years 1 to 3 and NT$12,000 per month in year 4, because the full tuition is deducted from the total MOE award.
Annual review, with enrolment procedures to be completed every semester to keep the scholarship continuous.
requirements: Hold a current university lecturer, assistant professor or professor post at an institution in an eligible country.
Provide an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate in English.
Have the teaching position on hold because of the studies.
Apply to a participating university and, where required, choose a full English-taught programme.
Submit the MOE-Elite form and documents by the deadline stated in the university's post-admission email.
Complete enrolment procedures every semester to keep the two or three-year scholarship continuous.
Apply for renewal each year, subject to review.
scholarships.duration: Up to 2 years for a master's programme and up to 3 years for a doctoral programme under the standard MOE terms, reviewed annually. Some participating universities extend this, and Taipei Tech runs the award for up to 4 years.
scholarships.application_period: Tied to each participating university's admission cycle, with published Fall application windows running from around mid-December to mid-March, followed by a post-admission document submission stage with its own email-stated deadline. MOE announces recipient lists around late October for Fall and late April for the African Spring intake. The AY2026/27 Fall window closed in mid-March 2026; the next is expected to open around mid-December 2026 for 2027 Fall entry.
scholarships.selection_notes: The programme is administered under the MOE Elite Scholarship Program Action Plan and was created in accordance with the New Southbound Policy Work Plan announced by the Executive Yuan in December 2016, under the MOE New Southbound Policy Talent Development Program. Priority is given to doctoral programmes. The university evaluates the admission application by department, and the MOE then reviews and determines the scholarship award. Published quota: one hundred students per academic year over three academic years, for a total of three hundred students. MOE allocates the quota, so entry is limited to new PhD students in the relevant intakes and can involve a waitlist.
scholarships.program_type: Government graduate scholarship for university lecturers from South, Southeast Asia and Africa to study in Taiwan (Ministry of Education, New Southbound Policy talent development)
scholarships.image_alt_text: National Cheng Kung University Office of International Affairs
scholarships.name: MOE Elite Scholarship Program for Lecturers from South and Southeast Asian and African Countries

scholarships.title: Unil Master's Scholarship
scholarships.description: The University of Lausanne awards around ten excellence scholarships each year, exclusively to students who have graduated from a foreign university and whose academic results are of a very high standard. The scholarship is paid for the minimum statutory period of the Master's programme at CHF 1,600 per month, and recipients are exempt from the standard course registration fees, with only the CHF 80 semester fees remaining payable. UNIL states explicitly that the amount does not constitute full funding, since about CHF 2,000 per month is needed to live in Lausanne. Applications for the 2027/2028 academic year are open until 1 November 2026.
scholarships.deadline: The online application for the academic year 2027/2028 is open. The deadline is 1 November 2026.
scholarships.deadline_display: The online application for the academic year 2027/2028 is open. The deadline is 1 November 2026.
eligibility: Hold a foreign university degree recognised as equivalent to a Swiss university bachelor's degree (180 ECTS credits) before starting the Master's programme at UNIL
Have achieved outstanding academic results during those studies
Hold a minimum C1 level in French for programmes taught in French, or in English for programmes taught in English
Not be currently enrolled at UNIL
Have paid the non-refundable administrative fee of CHF 200
Not have already begun a Master's programme at UNIL, and not be in the preparatory year
Applicants who already hold a foreign master's degree may apply, but priority is given to applicants holding only a bachelor's degree
benefits: CHF 1,600 per month for the minimum statutory period of the Master's programme
Exemption from the standard course registration fees; only the CHF 80 semester fees remain payable
UNIL guarantees holders accommodation with the Student Housing Foundation of Lausanne (rent paid by the student)
Possibility to recognise European health insurance (EU/EFTA) or buy cheaper Swiss student health insurance
requirements: One single PDF file, downloaded and uploaded during online registration
Two recommendation letters sent by e-mail from a professional (not private) address, naming the candidate in full, and only accepted if sent after the online registration
Certified true copies by post where the degree comes from a non-Lisbon-ratified state; candidates from ratifying states must not send them
CHF 200 administrative fee paid by bank transfer with proof of payment included in the PDF
Incomplete applications are not taken into account
scholarships.duration: The minimum statutory period of the chosen Master's programme
scholarships.application_period: Online application open now for the academic year 2027/2028; all parts of the file (online registration, recommendation letters, certified copies by post where required) must be completed by 1 November.
scholarships.selection_notes: Around ten excellence scholarships are awarded each year. The SASME checks completeness, the Admissions Office (SII) decides formal eligibility, the faculty decides admission to the chosen master's, and finally the Selection Board for the Master's Scholarship selects the scholarship holders in March, with applicants notified in early April. Decisions may not be appealed.
scholarships.program_type: University excellence scholarship for international master's admission
scholarships.name: Unil Master's Scholarship

scholarships.title: Excellence Scholarship for Bachelor Students (University of St.Gallen)
scholarships.description: The University of St.Gallen awards Excellence Scholarships to students enrolled in a Bachelor's degree on the basis of merit. The scholarship amount corresponds to the current tuition fees at the Bachelor level for a total of six semesters. It is not open to self-application: the Advice Center for Study Funding identifies enrolled students with an outstanding academic performance in the HSG Assessment Year and invites them to apply. The University of St.Gallen and the Monique Dornonville de la Cour - Stiftung currently fund these Bachelor-level excellence scholarships.
scholarships.deadline: There is no public application deadline. The Advice Center for Study Funding identifies students with an outstanding academic performance in the HSG Assessment Year and invites them to apply; an application without an invitation is not possible.
scholarships.deadline_display: There is no public application deadline. The Advice Center for Study Funding identifies students with an outstanding academic performance in the HSG Assessment Year and invites them to apply; an application without an invitation is not possible.
eligibility: Enrolled at the University of St.Gallen in a Bachelor's degree programme
Outstanding academic performance in the HSG Assessment Year
Identified and invited by the Advice Center for Study Funding; an application without an invitation is not possible
Additional selection criteria may be applied depending on the funding source
benefits: Full Bachelor-level tuition fees for six semesters
Award decided by the relevant committee, in cooperation with the funding foundation
requirements: Wait for and hold an invitation from the University of St.Gallen to apply
Submit the study funding application form with the required enclosures by the published deadline
For study funding applications generally, the Advice Center for Study Funding first checks the completeness of the application and then contacts the applicant to coordinate a personal interview
scholarships.duration: Six semesters of Bachelor-level tuition fees (three years)
scholarships.application_period: Invitation-driven. Invitations are issued by the Advice Center for Study Funding to enrolled students with outstanding Assessment Year performance, and applications are submitted by those invitees only.

Corporate Services

scholarships.program_type: Merit-based university excellence scholarship, invitation only
scholarships.name: Excellence Scholarship for Bachelor Students (University of St.Gallen)

scholarships.title: Starr International Foundation Scholarship (University of St.Gallen)
scholarships.description: The Starr International Foundation promotes education in Switzerland and abroad, and the HSG Starr International Foundation Fund supports excellence scholarships of the HSG Best Talents Programme. The Best Talents Programme gives financial support, including coverage of tuition fees and contributions to living expenses, alongside a personal development programme for outstanding and engaged bachelor's graduates from EU/EFTA countries or holders of a Swiss C permit who are admitted to a master's at HSG. Applications for the 2026 cohort closed on 12 June 2026 and the portal reopens in November 2026 for the 2027 cohort.
scholarships.deadline: Applications for the 2026 Best Talents cohort were accepted until June 12, 2026. The application portal will reopen in November 2026 for the 2027 cohort application cycle.
scholarships.deadline_display: Applications for the 2026 Best Talents cohort were accepted until June 12, 2026. The application portal will reopen in November 2026 for the 2027 cohort application cycle.
eligibility: EU/EFTA national or holder of a Swiss C permit
Admitted to a Master's programme at the University of St.Gallen
Completed a bachelor's degree
Excellent grades
Demonstrated engagement beyond studies
A proven sense of responsibility towards society, the economy and the environment, and a diversity of perspectives

scholarships.title: CERN Doctoral Student Programme
scholarships.description: The CERN Doctoral Student Programme is a PhD-level employment contract in which doctoral students carry out cutting-edge research at CERN in collaboration with their university, in fields spanning physics, engineering, applied physics, electronics, electrical engineering, information technologies, chemical and process engineering, civil engineering, mechanical engineering, data science and AI, and technology transfer. The programme pays a monthly net allowance of CHF 3,907 together with CERN health insurance, a possible family supplement, possible travel to Geneva on joining, and 30 days of paid leave plus two weeks of annual closure. Contracts run six months and are renewable up to three years, with the possibility of spreading the total over a maximum of four consecutive years. Eligibility is limited to nationals of CERN Member or Associate Member States, and applicants from Pakistan, Lithuania, Latvia, Cyprus, Croatia and Turkey are currently excluded because the Article II.5 ceiling has been reached.

scholarships.title: CERN Research Fellowship
scholarships.description: The CERN Research Fellowship Programme, part of CERN's broader Graduate Programme, is an opportunity for recent PhD graduates in physics and engineering to conduct advanced research in science, technology, engineering and mathematics at CERN. It pays a monthly net stipend of either CHF 7,004 or CHF 7,425 depending on the degree and years of post-graduation experience, together with CERN health insurance for the fellow, their partner and children, a contribution to the CERN Pension Fund, and depending on individual circumstances an installation grant, family, child and infant allowances and travel to Geneva on joining. Fellows receive 30 days of paid leave per year plus two weeks of CERN's annual closure, and on-the-job and formal training including language classes. Contracts run 6 to 24 months with the possibility of extension up to 36 months. Applicants must be nationals of a CERN Member or Associate Member State, must hold a PhD or obtain one within six months, must respect a research-experience cap of six years for Theoretical and Experimental Physics or three years for Applied Sciences and Engineering, and must never previously have held a CERN fellow or graduate contract.

scholarships.title: WIPO Fellowship Program
scholarships.description: WIPO's Fellowship Program places professionals in specialized disciplines at the World Intellectual Property Organization in Geneva, Switzerland, for 12 to 36 months. Fellows are classified into four categories: translation fellows in the PCT Translation and Terminology Fellowship Program, legal case manager fellows in the WIPO Domain Name Fellowship Program, visiting and research fellows in the Research and Visiting Fellowship Program, and other specialized fellows. Applicants must hold at least a first-level university degree, with additional requirements such as professional experience, an advanced degree or specific competencies depending on the category. Fellows receive a monthly stipend of CHF 3,000 to CHF 8,000 depending on academic background and relevant experience, comprehensive medical and professional accident insurance largely paid by WIPO, relocation assistance covering travel at the start and end of the fellowship, assistance with visa formalities, 10 official holidays plus 2.5 days of annual leave per full month, and access to WIPO Academy training with up to six study leave days a year. Positions are advertised through calls for expressions of interest on WIPO's career website and LinkedIn.

scholarships.title: Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship
scholarships.description: The Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship programme awards 18 full scholarships each academic year, including a tuition fee waiver and a monthly stipend, to highly talented students from outside the EU who have been admitted to a Maastricht University master's programme. It combines the High Potential Scholarship, funded by the Maastricht University Scholarship Fund, with the ministry-funded NL Scholarship. For the 2027-2028 intake, scholarship applications run from 1 October 2026 to 1 February 2027 (23:59 CET), the participating master's application must be complete through Studielink before 10 December 2026, and applicants must be non-EU/EEA (also excluding Switzerland and Surinam), aged 35 or under on 1 September 2027, with a GPA of at least 7.5 out of 10 and no previous degree-seeking study in the Netherlands. Recipients receive a living-expense stipend of EUR 20,150 over 13 months or EUR 38,750 over 25 months, tuition fees, visa costs and EUR 700 of health and liability insurance paid at cost, a mandatory UM room until 16 July 2028 and a two-week Pre-Academic Training programme. Only about 2% of applicants are awarded.

scholarships.title: University of Twente Scholarship (UTS)
scholarships.description: The University of Twente Scholarship is a scholarship for excellent students from non-EU/EEA countries applying for an English-taught master's programme at the University of Twente. Its value ranges from EUR 3,000 to EUR 22,000 for one year and is intended as compensation for study-related costs, with no costs such as tuition fees paid on the student's behalf; for two-year programmes a second-year award of an equal amount is possible if the student obtains an average grade of 7 out of 10 and at least 50 percent of the European Credits at the end of the third quartile of the first year. Applicants must first obtain an academic admission letter for a qualifying 2027/2028 master's programme, hold a UT student number, meet English requirements of IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 90 with 6.0 in speaking, not be eligible for a Dutch study loan, and belong to the top 5 to 10 percent of their graduating class. The application form opens on 15 October 2026 and closes on 1 April 2027 at 16:00 CET, with results in the first week of May 2027.

scholarships.title: Melbourne Research Scholarship (MRS)
scholarships.description: The Melbourne Research Scholarship is offered to high-achieving domestic and international students enrolling in, or already enrolled in, a graduate research degree at the University of Melbourne. It exists in three forms: a Fee Offset award, a Stipend award, and a combined Stipend and Fee Offset award. The Stipend award combines a full fee offset with a fortnightly stipend of $41,100 per year pro rata (2027 full-time rate), a one-off relocation allowance and OSHC Single Membership for international students who need a student visa. No separate application is required: applicants who apply for a graduate research course by that course's closing date are assessed automatically. Around 350 scholarships are available, and selection is by ranking on academic results for previous study and research potential.
