scholarships.title: One World Scholarship (Afro-Asian Institute Salzburg)
scholarships.description: The One World Scholarship of the Afro-Asian Institute Salzburg is a partial scholarship of EUR 500 per month during the semester (October through June) for students from Africa, Asia, the Near and Middle East, Oceania, the Caribbean and Latin America who study in Salzburg. Applicants must already be enrolled in Austria or admitted to a regular degree programme, hold a student residence permit or visa, and be admitted to a regular Master's or PhD programme in Salzburg. Selection is a multi-stage process - online form until 12 July, verification of formal criteria, full application until 15 July, online interview, then acceptance or rejection - and the Institute states that applying does not guarantee a scholarship place because positions are very limited. Successful applicants are expected to show financial need, good study progress, interest in development-related issues and a willingness to attend monthly meetings and actively contribute to the programme. Regarding equally qualified individuals, priority is given to female students.

ISTA charges no tuition fees and no application fee for its PhD, internship and scholarship programmes. Published gross salaries for 2026 range from EUR 3,053 to EUR 3,673 per month depending on whether the student holds a Bachelor's or Master's degree at admission, are paid 14 times a year, and rise once the Qualifying Exam is passed. All students receive five-year employment contracts and typically complete the programme in 4.5 to 6 years. For the 2027 intake the call opens in late October 2026 with an application deadline of 8 January 2027.

scholarships.title: Helmut Veith Stipend for Female Master's Students in Computer Science
scholarships.description: The Helmut Veith Stipend is an annually awarded grant for women pursuing a Master's programme in Computer Science at TU Wien taught in English, created in memory of Professor Helmut Veith (1971-2016). TU Wien states the benefits as "EUR 7000 per year" plus a "Waiver of tuition fees at TU Wien". The fund is set up by TU Wien, the Wolfgang Pauli Institute and the colleagues and friends of the late Prof. Veith. Applications are submitted electronically through the TU Wien job portal and are due by 30 November each year.

scholarships.title: FWF ESPRIT (Early-Stage Program: Research - Innovation - Training)
scholarships.description: ESPRIT (Early-Stage Program: Research - Innovation - Training) is an Austrian Science Fund career programme that lets highly qualified postdoc-level researchers lead an independent research project at an Austrian research institution. The FWF states a funding period of 36 months, paying the principal investigator's salary at the current senior postdoc rate plus project-specific costs of EUR 45,000 as a flat rate, or up to EUR 75,000 with justification. Submissions are accepted on a rolling basis through the elane online application portal, and decisions are taken at five Scientific Board approval meetings per year.

scholarships.title: Mannagetta Fellowships (Johann Wilhelm Ritter von Mannagetta Foundation at the Austrian Academy of Sciences)
scholarships.description: The Mannagetta Fellowships are financed from the funds of the Johann Wilhelm Ritter von Mannagetta Foundation held at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and support doctoral candidates at Austrian universities in completing a doctoral thesis in the humanities, cultural and social sciences. Applicants must have started their doctoral studies at a university in Austria no more than three years before the submission deadline and need no more than another twelve months to finish. Each fellowship is worth EUR 25,000 for twelve months, and one or two fellowships are granted per year. Applications for the next round close on 20 October 2026 at 2 p.m. CEST.

scholarships.title: DAAD Research Grants in Germany (for doctoral candidates and early postdocs)
scholarships.description: The DAAD Research Grants in Germany fund a research project at a state or state-recognised university or non-university research institute in Germany, carried out with a German scientific supervisor. Doctoral candidates may be funded for 2 to 12 months and early postdocs for 2 to 6 months; the grant cannot be extended and cannot be split within the funding period. The current DAAD announcement sets a monthly scholarship payment of EUR 1,400 plus insurance cover, a travel allowance, and for stays over six months a research allowance of EUR 460, a monthly rent subsidy and a monthly family allowance. Applications are submitted online through the DAAD Portal and are open annually, with deadlines updated in the second quarter of each year; on 2026-10-04 the DAAD stated that applications for the 2027 funding period were closed.

The committee also gives due consideration to equal opportunities.

scholarships.title: DAAD University Summer Courses offered in Germany for Foreign Students and Graduates (HSK)
scholarships.description: The DAAD University Summer Courses programme funds four-week German language, cultural studies and technical language courses at German universities and affiliated language schools for students and graduates from eligible countries. The scholarship covers the cost of the language course, provides accommodation in a single room through the course provider for the duration of the course, pays a one-time allowance of EUR 475, a country-specific travel allowance, and health, accident and personal liability insurance. Applications are accepted each year from 1 September to 30 October at 23:59 Central European Time, and courses run between June and September.

scholarships.title: DAAD Helmut-Schmidt-Programme (Master's Scholarships for Public Policy and Good Governance - PPGG)
scholarships.description: The DAAD Helmut-Schmidt-Programme, also known as Public Policy and Good Governance, is funded by the German Federal Foreign Office and supports future leaders from developing and emerging countries who want to promote democracy and social justice in their home regions. It funds places on selected English-taught master's courses in public policy, good governance, international relations, public management, public administration, civil society, geo-governance, peace and conflict studies, and development and socio-economic policy at seven German higher education institutions. Applications go directly to the participating universities rather than to the DAAD, and the published application window is 1 June to 31 July each year, with the 2027-intake round closed on 31 July 2026.

scholarships.title: Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship of the Heinrich Böll Foundation for international students who have completed their first degree abroad and intend to start a Master's degree in Germany, and for international PhD candidates who completed their graduate degree abroad. Applications are accepted in two rounds a year. Master's students funded by the Federal Foreign Office receive a base scholarship of EUR 992 per month plus a health insurance allowance of up to EUR 100 and optional components; PhD candidates funded by the Federal Foreign Office receive EUR 1,500 per month plus health insurance of up to EUR 200 per month. The funds come from the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR) and the Federal Foreign Office (AA).
scholarships.deadline: Two rounds per year. Spring 2027: 15 January 2027 until 1 March 2027 (online portal opens 15 January 2027 and closes 1 March 2027). Fall 2027: 15 July 2027 until 1 September 2027.
scholarships.deadline_display: Two rounds per year. Spring 2027: 15 January 2027 until 1 March 2027 (online portal opens 15 January 2027 and closes 1 March 2027). Fall 2027: 15 July 2027 until 1 September 2027.
eligibility: First degree completed abroad (Bildungsauslaender) before starting a Master's programme in Germany
Graduate degree completed abroad before starting a PhD in Germany
Priority for applicants from DAC countries who have not yet taken up residence in Germany at the time of application
AA-funded track requires a nationality from outside the EU; BMFTR track is aimed at German nationals, Bildungsauslaender educated in Germany and EU nationals
benefits: Health insurance allowance
Reimbursement of German tuition fees up to EUR 10,000 per year (AA track)
German language course tuition fees
Fixed fringe benefits of EUR 38 per month
Family allowance and child allowances
Ideational support, events and alumni network offered by the foundation
requirements: Applications are accepted only online; the portal opens about six weeks before the deadline
The application deadline is 1 March and 1 September; the portal opens around 15 January and 15 July respectively
Parts of the degree programme may be completed abroad if academically necessary, but with no additional funding for studies abroad
Any additional income must be offset against the scholarship payment
scholarships.duration: Funding is granted for the length of the study programme, up to a maximum of three years for master's students and five years for doctoral students.
scholarships.application_period: 15 January 2027 to 1 March 2027, and 15 July 2027 to 1 September 2027
scholarships.selection_notes: From the time of application (1 March or 1 September) the three-stage application process takes four to five months. Funding usually starts at the beginning of the winter term (applying by 1 March) or at the beginning of the summer semester (applying by 1 September), or somewhat earlier for PhD students.
scholarships.program_type: Master's degree and PhD scholarship
scholarships.name: Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarship

scholarships.title: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for Undergraduate Students (Embassy Recommendation)
scholarships.description: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for students from abroad who want to study as undergraduate students at Japanese national universities, selected through the recommendation of a Japanese embassy or consulate general. Applicants first pass a First Screening (documents, written academic examinations and interview) at the diplomatic mission in their country, are recommended to MEXT, and then pass MEXT's Second Screening. The scholarship pays a monthly allowance of JPY 117,000, waives entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees, and provides an economy-class airline ticket to Japan and, on return, back to the grantee's home country. The scholarship period is five years from April 2027 to March 2032 including one year of preparatory Japanese language education, or seven years for medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine and six-year pharmacy courses.
scholarships.deadline: No single central date: applicants must submit to the Japanese diplomatic mission in the country of their nationality by the deadline that mission sets, and that date is not published by MEXT. MEXT states applicants are informed of the final selection result by their diplomatic mission after February 2027, and that grantees must in principle arrive in Japan between 1 April 2027 and 7 April 2027.
scholarships.deadline_display: No single central date: applicants must submit to the Japanese diplomatic mission in the country of their nationality by the deadline that mission sets, and that date is not published by MEXT. MEXT states applicants are informed of the final selection result by their diplomatic mission after February 2027, and that grantees must in principle arrive in Japan between 1 April 2027 and 7 April 2027.
eligibility: Nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan; Japanese nationals are not eligible, with a limited exception for dual nationals resident outside Japan who renounce Japanese nationality on arrival
One of the listed academic-background conditions, normally 12 years of schooling completed outside Japan by March 2027
Applicants must be willing to learn Japanese and be interested in Japan
In principle, applicants must be willing to carry out their academic studies in Japan in Japanese
Age limit in principle, as set out in section 5 of the application guidelines
Able in principle to arrive in Japan between 1 April 2027 and 7 April 2027, with departure from the home residence on or after 1 April 2027
benefits: Monthly scholarship allowance of JPY 117,000
Supplemental regional allowance in specially designated regions
Full waiver of entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees
Economy-class airline ticket to Japan and back to the home country
One year of preparatory Japanese language education where applicable
requirements: Applications must be submitted to the Japanese diplomatic mission in the country of the applicant's nationality by that mission's designated deadline
Applicants must submit two application packets: one complete set of original documents and one complete set of copies
Document numbers 1 to 9 must be written in the upper right-hand corner of the first page of each document
Submitted documents are not returned
Applicants must sit the First Screening written examinations and interview at the diplomatic mission
scholarships.duration: Five years from April 2027 to March 2032 including one year of preparatory Japanese language education; seven years for medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine or a six-year pharmacy course; four years for grantees placed directly at a university
scholarships.application_period: Annually; the 2027 cycle guidelines were published by MEXT in April 2026 and applications were made to Japanese diplomatic missions during the first half of the year
scholarships.selection_notes: The Japanese diplomatic mission conducts the First Screening through examination of submitted documents, written academic examinations and interviews; MEXT then conducts the Second Screening of the recommended applicants and selects candidates from each course. Written examination subjects depend on the chosen field: Social Sciences and Humanities applicants take Japanese, English and Mathematics; Natural Sciences applicants take Japanese, English, Mathematics and either Chemistry or Physics. Reasons for screening results are not disclosed and objections to the decision on university placement are not accepted.
scholarships.program_type: Undergraduate scholarship (embassy recommendation)
scholarships.name: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for Undergraduate Students (Embassy Recommendation)

scholarships.title: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for Research Students (University Recommendation)
scholarships.description: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for students from abroad who wish to pursue research study at a Japanese university under the university-recommendation route, meaning the accepting university nominates the student to MEXT. The monthly allowance depends on the course enrolled in: JPY 117,000 for regular students in bachelor degree courses, JPY 144,000 for master's or professional degree courses and JPY 145,000 for doctoral courses, with a supplemental regional allowance of JPY 2,000 or JPY 3,000 per month in specially designated regions. Entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees must be paid by the accepting university, and MEXT stipulates the travel route and provides an economy-class airline ticket. The scholarship period is the necessary period for completion of the relevant regular course.
scholarships.deadline: No applicant-facing deadline is published. Under the university-recommendation route the accepting university nominates the student to MEXT, so the application timetable is set between MEXT and each university and is not announced publicly.
scholarships.deadline_display: No applicant-facing deadline is published. Under the university-recommendation route the accepting university nominates the student to MEXT, so the application timetable is set between MEXT and each university and is not announced publicly.
eligibility: Nominated by a Japanese accepting university under the university-recommendation route
Enrolled in a regular course corresponding to the level for which the scholarship is awarded (master's or professional degree course, or doctoral course)
Meets the nationality, age and academic-background conditions set out in the application guidelines
Able to arrive in Japan within the period designated by MEXT for the intake year

Applications for extension of the scholarship period due to advanced study are not acceptable for bachelor degree courses, preparatory education and bachelor degree courses, master's courses (doctoral course first phase), or professional degree courses
benefits: Monthly scholarship allowance up to JPY 145,000 for doctoral students
Supplemental regional allowance in specially designated regions
Entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees covered by the accepting university
Economy-class airline ticket to Japan and back on completion of the course
requirements: The student must be nominated by the accepting university; individual applicants cannot apply directly to MEXT under this route
Applications for extension of the scholarship period due to advanced study must be submitted; they are not automatic
MEXT stipulates the travel schedule and route; the airline ticket cannot be changed afterwards
MEXT will not provide an airline ticket for domestic recommenders
The grantee bears domestic travel to the nearest international airport, airport taxes, travel within Japan, travel insurance and baggage costs
scholarships.duration: The necessary period for the completion of the respective regular course; the guidelines note that for adopted five-year doctoral courses the first two years count as a master's course and years three to five as a doctoral course, so students must apply for extension when advancing to the third year
scholarships.application_period: Annual. MEXT publishes the guidelines for the coming year and calls universities for nominations; students apply through their prospective or current Japanese university rather than directly to MEXT
scholarships.selection_notes: MEXT's stated aim is to foster human resources who will become bridges of friendship between the grantee's country and Japan through study in Japan and who will contribute to the development of both countries and the wider world. Under the university-recommendation route the academic assessment is effectively the university's, with MEXT confirming the nominated candidates.
scholarships.program_type: Research student scholarship (university recommendation)
scholarships.name: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for Research Students (University Recommendation)

scholarships.title: Young Leaders Program (YLP) Students - Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship
scholarships.description: Young Leaders Program (YLP) Students is the seventh type of the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship. It funds a one-year master's course at a Japanese graduate school for university or college graduates with practical work experience and for young public administrators who are expected to play an active role in Asia and other countries. The scholarship pays JPY 242,000 per month, the tuition is exempted, and round-trip airfare to and from Japan is provided. Unlike the other six MEXT scholarship types, YLP is neither embassy-recommended nor university-recommended: recruitment is conducted by the embassies of Japan in target countries upon the recommendation of official overseas recommending organisations, the initial selection is by document screening, interview and essay writing, and the final selection is made by the YLP Committee set in MEXT.
scholarships.deadline: No central MEXT or portal deadline is published. Recruitment is conducted through the embassies of Japan in target countries upon the recommendation of official overseas recommending organisations, so the timetable is set country by country and by the recommending organisation. Applicants must check the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their own country.
scholarships.deadline_display: No central MEXT or portal deadline is published. Recruitment is conducted through the embassies of Japan in target countries upon the recommendation of official overseas recommending organisations, so the timetable is set country by country and by the recommending organisation. Applicants must check the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their own country.
eligibility: Under 40 years of age in principle
University or college graduate with practical work experience
Young public administrator or similar early-career leader expected to play an active role in Asia and other countries
Nominated through an official overseas recommending organisation to the embassy of Japan in a target country
Admitted to, or placed in, a master's course at a Japanese graduate school
benefits: Monthly scholarship allowance of JPY 242,000, the highest of the seven MEXT scholarship types
Full tuition exemption
Round-trip airfare to and from Japan
One year of postgraduate study at a Japanese graduate school
requirements: Candidates are recruited through the embassies of Japan in target countries upon the recommendation of official overseas recommending organisations; this is neither the embassy-recommendation nor the university-recommendation route
The initial selection consists of document screening, an interview and essay writing
The second selection is done by the YLP Committee set in MEXT, and MEXT makes the final decision
The type and field of application can differ from country to country; applicants should check with the embassy whether there is an opening in the type and field they wish to apply for
The latest edition of the application guidelines governs where its contents differ from the portal's summary
scholarships.duration: 1 year
scholarships.application_period: Not published centrally. Recruitment runs through the embassies of Japan in target countries upon the recommendation of official overseas recommending organisations, at timings that differ by country and region.
scholarships.selection_notes: The initial selection is by the embassy through document screening, interview and essay writing; the subjects of any written component vary by country and region. Candidates who pass are recommended to MEXT, and the second selection is made by the YLP Committee set in MEXT, which makes the final decision.
scholarships.program_type: Master's course scholarship (YLP)
scholarships.name: Young Leaders Program (YLP) Students - Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship

scholarships.title: JASSO Reservation Program for Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students by Pre-arrival Admission
scholarships.degree: Bachelor's, Master's, PhD, Other (junior college, college of technology 3rd year or above, specialized training college course)
scholarships.description: JASSO's reservation programme for the Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students, for students who have already received pre-arrival admission to a Japanese institution and face financial difficulties. It pays a monthly stipend of JPY 48,000 for 12 months if the student enrols in April, or for 6 months if the student enrols in September or October. Applications are not made to JASSO directly; the applicant must apply through the school they plan to enrol in. There are three reservation categories: graduate level, EJU exam, and English courses.
scholarships.deadline: No JASSO deadline is published. Applications are handled entirely through the school the applicant plans to enrol in, so the deadline is the school's own pre-arrival admission and scholarship nomination deadline.
scholarships.deadline_display: No JASSO deadline is published. Applications are handled entirely through the school the applicant plans to enrol in, so the deadline is the school's own pre-arrival admission and scholarship nomination deadline.
eligibility: Privately-financed international student (not a Japanese Government MEXT Scholarship holder)
Has received pre-arrival admission to an eligible school listed by JASSO for the relevant reservation category
Plans to enrol as a full-time student; research students, trainees, non-degree students, advanced course students, special course students, auditing students and special students are excluded
Graduate level reservation: enrolling in a graduate school in Japan in April, or September/October for autumn enrolment

EJU exam or English courses reservation: enrolling in an undergraduate school, junior college, college of technology (3rd grade or upper) or specialized course in a specialized training college in Japan in April, or September/October for autumn enrolment
Faces financial difficulties and has an excellent academic and character record
benefits: Monthly stipend of JPY 48,000
12 months of support for April enrollees
6 months of support for September or October enrollees
requirements: JASSO does not accept applications directly from students; the procedure must be completed through the school
The school must be on the eligible list for the relevant reservation category for that enrolment cycle

For the EJU exam category JASSO uses the registered-school list as of 1 October 2025 for spring enrolment and as of 1 April 2026 for September or October enrolment, which may differ from the list published on the web page
The student must enrol as a full-time student; research students, trainees, non-degree students, advanced course students, special course students, auditing students and special students are excluded
scholarships.duration: 12 months for students enrolled in April (April of the year of enrolment to the following March); 6 months for students enrolled in September or October (October of the year of enrolment to the following March)
scholarships.application_period: School-by-school, twice a year, matching the Japanese enrolment cycles: spring enrolment (April) and autumn enrolment (September or October). JASSO publishes the eligible school and department lists for each cycle; for 2026 the autumn lists were published in June 2026 and the spring lists in January 2026.
scholarships.selection_notes: JASSO's stated objectives for the reservation programme are to ease students' financial concerns about arrival and studies in Japan, promote pre-arrival admission and improve the level of learning. The award targets privately-financed international students with excellent academic and character records who face financial difficulties, and the practical selection is carried out through the school.
scholarships.program_type: Reservation programme for the MEXT Honors Scholarship, by pre-arrival admission
scholarships.name: JASSO Reservation Program for Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students by Pre-arrival Admission

scholarships.title: Kyushu University International Scholarship
scholarships.description: Kyushu University does not operate a single named international scholarship for master's and PhD students. Instead, it publishes an annual scholarship information list in which more than 65 awards from external foundations are available to enrolled international students, each with its own stipend amount, duration, deadline and application route. Some awards are made through on-campus selection by the International Student Exchange Division and others require direct application to the foundation. Amounts published for the 2027 cycle range from JPY 50,000 per month to JPY 200,000 per month, plus tuition subsidies in some cases.
scholarships.deadline: Varies (check Kyushu University admissions)
scholarships.deadline_display: Varies (check Kyushu University admissions)
eligibility: The base requirement for the scholarship list is enrolment as an international student at Kyushu University; the page states it provides information on scholarships for international students enrolled at Kyushu University

Each award adds its own conditions, for example the KDDI award requires applicants under 35 as of 1 April 2027 with research related to information technology, and the Rotary Yoneyama award restricts eligibility to specific years of study

Some awards require Japanese language ability; the Honjo award requires the research plan to be written in Japanese and daily conversational ability, and the ITO award requires the ability to communicate and write in Japanese
For on-campus selection, the applicant must already be enrolled and hold a residence card whose period of stay is on or after 1 April 2027
benefits: Tuition fee waiver
Monthly stipend (amount varies)
Admission fee exemption
requirements: For on-campus selection, submission of the prescribed on-campus selection application form and transcript before the award's deadline
For foundation applications, the applicant applies directly and provides the foundation's own documents
Some awards require an interview; the Rotary Yoneyama award requires a face-to-face interview and written examination between early December and late January, with no rescheduling if absent
Where an award is a direct application, scholarship recommendation forms must be requested from the student affairs office of the department or graduate school
Several awards are mutually exclusive; the INPEX awards state that university scholarships are not subject to adjustment
scholarships.duration: Award-specific. Published durations include 6 or 12 months from 1 April 2027, 1-2 years, from April 2027 to the minimum term of study, and from the start of study abroad to the end of study abroad with the monthly scholarship for up to two years and eight months including the research student period.
scholarships.selection_notes:
Where the award states selection criteria, they include academic performance and, for the INPEX awards, a privately financed international student aspiring to pursue a master's programme in STEM fields in the 2027 academic year
The KDDI award states that only one international student per faculty advisor may be recommended, and that adjustments are made so combined assistance from other institutions and the foundation does not exceed JPY 100,000
scholarships.program_type: University-administered external foundation scholarship list
scholarships.name: Kyushu University International Scholarship

scholarships.title: MOFCOM Scholarship - CSC Program (Ministry of Commerce of China and China Scholarship Council Joint Program)
scholarships.description: The MOFCOM Scholarship is an aid programme hosted by the Ministry of Commerce of the People's Republic of China that offers postgraduate study in China to applicants from developing countries. It runs in two tracks: the MOFCOM-40 direct-admission track of 40 MOFCOM-led projects, and the MOFCOM-CSC joint track operated with the China Scholarship Council. Through the Chinese Embassy in Sierra Leone, applicants register on the CSC portal under institution code 00010, select three target universities and majors, and email the full document set to the embassy. The official programme PDF states free on-campus accommodation and annual stipends of RMB 36,000 for master's and RMB 42,000 for PhD students. Admission is decided by the receiving university.
scholarships.deadline: Applicants for MOFCOM-CSC must email their PDF materials and Appendix 3 to sl@mofcom.gov.cn by May 12, 2026; shortlisted applicants are notified in late May 2026 and results are announced around July-August 2026.
scholarships.deadline_display: Applicants for MOFCOM-CSC must email their PDF materials and Appendix 3 to sl@mofcom.gov.cn by May 12, 2026; shortlisted applicants are notified in late May 2026 and results are announced around July-August 2026.
eligibility: Senior officials of the Sierra Leonean government, university faculty or corporate executives
Age 45 or under
At least 3 years of work experience
Bachelor's degree for master's applicants; master's degree for doctoral applicants
Minimum average GPA of 3.25 on a 4-point scale, or 4.0 on a 5-point scale
Good health; physical examination at the 34th Military Hospital or Jui Hospital with the form signed and verified by a Chinese doctor
HSK Level 3 or higher is a priority (not mandatory)

Not eligible if any type of Chinese Government Scholarship funding was received in the past three years; students scheduled to graduate from a Chinese university in 2026 are barred, and those who graduated in 2023 or earlier with prior Chinese Government funding are eligible
Degree certificates and transcripts must be stamped by the Ministry of Technical and Higher Education and authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
benefits: Free on-campus accommodation
Stipend of RMB 36,000 per year for master's students
Stipend of RMB 42,000 per year for PhD students
Visa assistance for successful applicants
requirements: Register on the CSC portal at https://studyinchina.csc.edu.cn/#/login and select 3 target universities/majors using institution code 00010
Complete the relevant university-specific application portal as well
Email all PDF materials plus Appendix 3 to sl@mofcom.gov.cn with the prescribed subject line
Keep the original paper copies, as submission is by email and online system only
Attend the embassy interview if invited; uninvited applicants are automatically disqualified
scholarships.duration: Postgraduate degree programme (master's or doctoral); the notice does not publish a fixed duration.
scholarships.application_period: The 2026 recruitment notice was issued 3 April 2026, materials were due 12 May 2026, interviews were expected in late May 2026 and admission results were expected July-August 2026. The programme is recruited annually.
scholarships.selection_notes: Incomplete or overdue applications are rejected. The embassy recommends candidates and the final admission decision rests with the university's admission committee. Applicants are urged to act with integrity; in previous years degrees were revoked over falsified transcripts.
scholarships.program_type: Postgraduate scholarship programme run by the Ministry of Commerce of China in two tracks - the MOFCOM-40 direct-admission track and the MOFCOM-CSC joint track operated with the China Scholarship Council

scholarships.title: Chinese Government Scholarship - Tsinghua University Program (Type B)
scholarships.description: The Chinese Government Scholarship (CGS) is funded by the Chinese government and administered by the China Scholarship Council, which is entrusted by the Ministry of Education with admission, enrolment and administration of recipients. Tsinghua University hosts the Category Type B route, in which the university nominates candidates under the CGS-Chinese University Program, and the page also explains that Type A programmes are handled by other authorities such as the bilateral, EU and AUN programmes. This record covers the Type B route for graduate study at Tsinghua. Full CGS covers tuition, university accommodation or an accommodation subsidy, a stipend and comprehensive medical insurance, for one to three years of master's study or four to five years of doctoral study.
scholarships.deadline: Applicants are highly recommended to apply before Mid-December, 2025; the exact date is set by each school or department of Tsinghua University, so there is no single university-wide deadline.
scholarships.deadline_display: Applicants are highly recommended to apply before Mid-December, 2025; the exact date is set by each school or department of Tsinghua University, so there is no single university-wide deadline.
eligibility: Citizen of a country other than the People's Republic of China and in good health both mentally and physically
Bachelor's degree holder under the age of 35 when applying for master's programs
Master's degree holder under the age of 40 when applying for doctoral programs

HSK Level 4 for Chinese-taught master's or doctoral programs; holders of a degree from a Chinese university taught in Chinese must instead provide proof of Chinese-taught instruction from the previous degree-awarding institution
Pre-admitted by Tsinghua University and recommended for CGS by the admitting school or department - otherwise the application is not considered
Must not have been offered other scholarships for prospective graduate study at Tsinghua or nominated as a CGS candidate by another university
Must meet other Type B programme requirements such as applicable programmes, majors and nationalities
benefits: Full CGS: tuition fees
Free university dormitory or accommodation subsidy
Monthly stipend
Comprehensive medical insurance
Partial CGS variants include one or some items from the full coverage
requirements: Submit the Tsinghua pre-admission online application at https://yzbm.tsinghua.edu.cn/intlLogin
Obtain a recommendation from the admitting school or department
Complete the CSC online application in the Chinese Government Scholarship Information System when instructed by the department
Submit documents online; CGS applicants do not need to mail hard copies to Tsinghua University
scholarships.duration: Master's degree: 1-3 years. Doctoral degree: 4-5 years.
scholarships.application_period: The 2026 cycle page was published in November 2025 with pre-admission applications recommended before mid-December 2025. Tsinghua's 2027 international graduate admission round was announced on 5 September 2026, so the 2027 CGS Type B cycle is expected to open in the same period as the 2026 one.
scholarships.selection_notes: Tsinghua states that applying for CGS through Tsinghua is highly competitive and that it usually selects candidates from pre-admitted applicants of remarkable merit. Applicants who cannot be reached or who fail to complete the CGS online application in time are treated as renouncing the candidacy. All CGS holders must pass a strict annual review covering academic performance, learning attitude, attendance, student conduct, rewards and punishments; the scholarship is suspended or terminated if the review is failed.
scholarships.program_type: Chinese Government Scholarship Category Type B (CGS-Chinese University Program) nominated by Tsinghua University to the China Scholarship Council
scholarships.name: Chinese Government Scholarship - Tsinghua University Program (Type B)

scholarships.title: Confucius Institute Scholarship
scholarships.degree: Chinese Language Studies, Teaching Chinese as Foreign Language
scholarships.description: Established by the Center for Language Education and Cooperation of the Ministry of Education to meet growing global demand for Chinese-education professionals, promote Chinese-language education worldwide and support the growth of international Chinese-education talent, the scholarship - formerly the Confucius Institute Scholarship - focuses on cultivating qualified overseas Chinese-language teachers. Authorised recommending institutions nominate outstanding students and in-service Chinese-language teachers to study International Chinese Language Education and related programmes at 236 designated Chinese receiving universities.
scholarships.deadline: 31 October 2026 (Beijing time), for March 2027 entry
scholarships.deadline_display: 31 October 2026 (Beijing time), for March 2027 entry
eligibility: Non-Chinese citizens; applicants of Chinese origin (naturalised former Chinese citizens and their foreign-national children) must pass a nationality pre-screening at the admission stage
Friendly toward China, with no criminal record, and willing to abide by Chinese laws, regulations and institutional rules
Physically and mentally healthy, of excellent character and academic standing
Committed to pursuing Chinese-language education, teaching or related work
Aged 16-35 (reckoned at 1 September of the entry year); in-service Chinese-language teachers up to 45; undergraduate applicants generally not over 25
benefits: Full tuition
Free accommodation
Monthly stipend: CNY 2,500-3,000
Basic health insurance
One-time CNY 1,500 settlement allowance

MA in International Chinese Language Education (2 years, September entry): bachelor's degree; HSK Level 5 score 210 plus HSKK Intermediate 60
BA in Chinese Language and Literature / International Chinese Language Education (4 years, September entry): high-school diploma; HSK Level 4 score 210 plus HSKK Intermediate 60

Central expert-panel review commissioned by the centre, based on HSK and HSKK levels and scores with consideration of country balance
Priority for applicants presenting a post-graduation teaching work agreement or related proof
In-service Chinese-language teachers are prioritised under equal conditions
One-semester and one-academic-year programmes generally exclude applicants who received the same scholarship within the previous three years
An applicant may hold only one Chinese government-institution scholarship at a time; duplicate applications are void

scholarships.name: Confucius Institute Scholarship

scholarships.title: UCD Global Excellence Scholarships (100% and 50% Tuition Fee)
scholarships.description: UCD Global Excellence Scholarships offer a limited number of 100% and 50% tuition fee scholarships to outstanding international students who are classed as non-EU for tuition fee purposes and are applying to undergraduate or graduate taught programmes that appear on UCD's eligible-programmes list. Students must first secure an offer or conditional offer on an eligible course. Application deadlines are regional - 1 February 2026 for North American undergraduates, 28 February 2026 for undergraduate and graduate taught applicants from the Middle East, Africa and Pakistan and graduate taught applicants from South Asia, and 31 March 2026 for all other regions. Results are published via SISWeb about seven weeks after each regional deadline. The award is a tuition fee reduction only, is not automatically renewable, and is reassessed for continuing students between late September and October.
scholarships.deadline: Regional deadlines for 2026/27: 1 February 2026 (undergraduate applicants from North America); 28 February 2026 (undergraduate and graduate taught applicants from the Middle East, Africa and Pakistan, and graduate taught applicants from South Asia); 31 March 2026 (all other applicants, undergraduate and graduate taught).
scholarships.deadline_display: Regional deadlines for 2026/27: 1 February 2026 (undergraduate applicants from North America); 28 February 2026 (undergraduate and graduate taught applicants from the Middle East, Africa and Pakistan, and graduate taught applicants from South Asia); 31 March 2026 (all other applicants, undergraduate and graduate taught).
eligibility: Must be an incoming student who is classed as non-EU for tuition fee purposes (for information regarding fee classification, UCD directs applicants to its fees page)
Must apply to an undergraduate or graduate taught programme only
The programme must be listed in UCD's Eligible Programmes 2026 document
Must first have received an offer or a conditional offer to study on an eligible UCD course
Awards are not automatically renewed for continuing students; each is reassessed in line with the original award terms, with outcomes notified between late September and October

scholarships.title: University of Otago Global Scholarships
scholarships.description: The University of Otago Global Scholarships provide NZD $15,000 towards tuition fees to new international Bachelor degree students who hold a passport from one of twelve nominated countries — Bangladesh, China, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Macau, Malaysia, Singapore, South Korea, Sri Lanka, Taiwan, Thailand or Vietnam. scholarships.description: Since the 2026 intake the University of Turku no longer offers a scholarship that covers the first year of tuition. Instead it offers an automatic EUR 2,000 Early Bird discount to newly admitted master's students who accept the offer and pay within 28 days of the admission decision, and the University of Turku Merit Scholarship, which covers 50% of the tuition fee for the following study year. The merit scholarship is based on studies completed at the University of Turku and requires 55 ECTS in the first study year, an average score of at least 3.0, and at least 4 ECTS of Finnish, with a separate application opened in spring.

scholarships.title: LUT Scholarship and Early Bird Discount (master's studies)
scholarships.description: LUT University reduces tuition for fee-paying students of its two-year master's programmes in two automatic steps. In the first academic year every tuition-liable student who accepts the study place and pays the remaining EUR 10,000 of the first-year fee within 21 days of the official admission email receives an early bird discount of EUR 5,000. In the second academic year every tuition-liable student who has completed at least 60 ECTS credits in accordance with their personal study plan, with those credits recorded on the Transcript of Records by 31 July, and who pays the second-year fee on time receives a LUT scholarship of EUR 5,000. Neither award requires a separate application and neither covers living costs.
scholarships.deadline: No scholarship application deadline exists: the awards are automatic. The early bird discount requires that you 'accept your study place and pay the remaining first-year tuition fee of EUR 10,000 within 21 days of your official admission email'. The LUT scholarship requires 60 ECTS recorded on your Transcript of Records by 31 July. LUT's own homepage states applications to English-language master's programmes are open until 31 March 2027 under rolling admission.

scholarships.title: Danish Government Scholarship for Non-EU/EEA Full-Degree Students
scholarships.description: Danish universities receive a limited number of government scholarships each year to fund highly qualified full-degree students from countries outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland. Applicants must be citizens of a non-EU/EEA/non-Swiss country, enrolled in a full degree programme and hold a time-limited residence permit for education, and they are excluded if they seek admission to an artistic higher education institution, have a legal claim to Danish citizens' rights, or are eligible for SU. The scholarship consists of two parts and may be a full or partial tuition fee waiver, a grant towards living costs, or both. The individual university administers the award and selects the students.
scholarships.deadline: The ministry publishes no deadline: 'The scholarships are administered by the Danish universities, who each select the students, who are awarded with a scholarship. For further information about the government scholarship, please consult the admission details of the higher education institution of your choice.' The deadline is therefore the admission deadline of the individual university.
scholarships.deadline_display: The ministry publishes no deadline: 'The scholarships are administered by the Danish universities, who each select the students, who are awarded with a scholarship. For further information about the government scholarship, please consult the admission details of the higher education institution of your choice.' The deadline is therefore the admission deadline of the individual university.

Enrolled in a full degree higher education programme
Granted a time-limited residence permit in Denmark due to education
Not applying to an Artistic Higher Education Institution

Not eligible for a grant under Danish State Education Fund (SU) rules
Not holding a residence permit under Aliens Consolidations Act section 9c(1) as a child of a section 9m permit holder who is a non-EU/EEA national

scholarships.selection_notes: The scholarship is highly competitive because the ministry states universities receive only a limited number each year; selection is entirely in the hands of each university.

scholarships.title: DTU Tuition Fee Waiver for International non-EU/EEA MSc Students
scholarships.description: DTU awards a very limited number of tuition fee waivers to new international non-EU/EEA MSc students applying for the autumn intake, allocating them to students with excellent academic performance. A waiver covers the tuition fee for two years. To be considered, applicants must apply by the 15 January deadline and submit a separate personal statement with the application that focuses on academic achievements at bachelor's level; applications without that statement are not considered. Waivers are offered only for the autumn intake, are decided in parallel with admissions, and are granted after the applicant accepts an admission offer.

All eligible non-EU/EEA applicants to the university's MA/MSc programmes are considered automatically as part of the admission process, so no individual application exists. The award is granted as a full or partial tuition fee waiver and/or an amount covering basic living expenses, depending on faculty, and is decided on academic achievement alone.
scholarships.deadline: No scholarship deadline is published, because there is no separate scholarship application. The operative date is the master's admission deadline, and tuition payment terms are emailed around mid-May.

scholarships.funding: Tuition Fee Waiver (full or part; some faculties add a monthly living-expense grant)
scholarships.description: Aarhus University administers a limited number of Danish state scholarships for non-EU/EEA applicants liable to pay tuition fees. The award takes the form of a full or partial tuition waiver; the Faculty of Arts and Aarhus BSS add a monthly grant towards living expenses, while the Faculty of Natural Sciences and the Faculty of Technical Sciences offer tuition waivers only. No separate scholarship application exists: applicants are assessed automatically when they apply for admission to a Master's programme by 15 January (summer admission) or 15 September (winter admission). The scholarship is tied to the specific Master's programme and cannot be transferred to another AU degree programme.

scholarships.title: University of Southern Denmark (SDU) Danish Government Scholarship
scholarships.description: The University of Southern Denmark awards a limited number of Danish government scholarships to highly qualified non-EU/EEA citizens. Eligibility is restricted to seven specific programmes: MSc in Engineering in Electronics/Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering and Mechatronics at the Sønderborg campus, and BSc in Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, Interactive Technology Engineering and Software Engineering at the Vejle campus. The award is a full tuition fee waiver covering two years for MSc and three years for BSc programmes, limited to 30 ECTS per semester, and it does not cover living costs. Applicants need no separate scholarship application; the admission application is submitted by 1 February for master's and 15 March for bachelor's programmes, followed by an online interview for shortlisted candidates.

scholarships.title: NTNU PhD Positions (Salaried Employment)
scholarships.funding: Fully Funded (salaried employment as a PhD research fellow / stipendiat)
scholarships.description: NTNU's PhD positions are salaried employment rather than scholarships: Norwegian PhD candidates are not treated as students and are normally employees of the institution that funds them. Most PhD candidates at NTNU are employed as PhD research fellows (stipendiat) at NTNU or a university college, with individual positions advertised on NTNU's vacancy pages and on jobbnorge.no. Admission requires at least five years of higher education including a master's degree, a weighted average of at least B over the last two master's years on NTNU's scale, and a funding plan for the whole PhD period. Acceptance is done continuously throughout the academic year rather than at fixed deadlines, and the standard PhD is three years full-time, sometimes extended by a fourth year of teaching duties.
scholarships.deadline: Positions are advertised individually and applications are assessed continuously: 'Acceptance to a PhD-programme at NTNU is done continuously throughout the academic year and is not restricted to the beginning of term.' Each vacancy carries its own application deadline.

For the 2026-2027 academic year one scholarship was available, awarded to an outstanding applicant to any eligible KU Leuven master's or advanced master's programme. Holders receive a full tuition fee waiver, pay only an annual administration fee of circa EUR 140, and receive an allowance of EUR 13,200 per academic year for a maximum of two academic years. scholarships.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Degrees (EMJMD/EMJM) Scholarships
scholarships.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degrees are integrated international master's programmes jointly delivered by at least three higher education institutions from at least three different countries, at least two of which are EU Member States or Programme-associated third countries. The European Commission funds the programmes and offers EU scholarships to the best-ranked students worldwide at EUR 1,400 per month for a maximum of 24 months. Students apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme, usually between October and January for entry the following academic year.

scholarships.title: Visegrad Scholarship Programme
scholarships.description: The International Visegrad Fund's Visegrad Scholarship Programme supports master's and post-master's students and researchers for up to two semesters at institutions in Central and Eastern Europe, awarded for a period of 1 or 2 semesters; within the In-Coming scheme, master's applicants can be awarded 1- to 4-semester scholarships. It is open to citizens of Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine, and all applicants must have completed at least four semesters of university studies. Because it is a mobility scholarship, the host country varies with the chosen institution rather than being a single destination. The Fund's own site shows the next application round opening on 1 January 2027; no closing date for that round is published yet, and the funding amounts are not stated on the pages read, so funding_type and funding_amount are left unresolved rather than guessed.

scholarships.title: Jagiellonian University Rector's Scholarship (stypendium rektora)
scholarships.description: Jagiellonian University's Rector's Scholarship is a merit-based cash benefit from the university Scholarship Fund for first-cycle (bachelor), second-cycle (master) and long-cycle master's students, awarded on request for outstanding academic performance, scientific, artistic or sports achievements. In the first year of first-cycle or long-cycle master's studies it goes to students admitted in the year of the matura exam who won an international olympiad or were laureates/finalists of a central-level olympiad, or who medalled in at least a Polish Championship competition; in higher years it is capped at 10% of students in a given programme. Foreign students admitted from the 2019/2020 academic year onward may apply regardless of citizenship. The award runs for nine months (October to June), paid monthly into a Polish zloty (PLN) bank account held at a bank in Poland.

scholarships.title: Scholarships of the Government of the Czech Republic for Students from Developing Countries
scholarships.description: Scholarships of the Government of the Czech Republic for students from developing countries let nationals of designated partner states study at Czech public universities within the Czech foreign development cooperation programme. DZS states that "the Czech Republic offers scholarships to foreigners for a standard period of study in accredited university study programmes provided at public universities, and for courses in the Czech language and vocational preparation". Awards cover a master's study programme in Czech preceded by a one-year Czech language and professional training course, or study in master's and doctoral study programmes conducted in English. Applications are made through an electronic form, then the file passes through the applicant's Czech embassy, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and MŠMT.

scholarships.title: Charles University Doctoral Study Income (full-time doctoral students)
scholarships.description: Charles University guarantees every full-time doctoral student a doctoral study income of at least 1.2 times the Czech minimum wage for the standard length of the doctorate (four years). The income may take the form of a doctoral scholarship, a salary or wage for creative work directly related to preparing the dissertation, or a combination of both, and is often supplemented by research-project awards and teaching remuneration. For bachelor's and master's students the university publishes no general scholarship: its page routes applicants to Czech Ministry of Education scholarship schemes (developing-country, general international and International Visegrad Fund), the Vaclav Havel Bursary, the Institute for Language and Preparatory Studies, and faculty-level awards whose amounts are set by each faculty's own regulations.

scholarships.title: International Visegrad Fund Fellowships and Scholarships (V4 mobility)
scholarships.description: The International Visegrad Fund runs regional mobility programmes for Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Ukraine. The Visegrad Fellowship Program funds individual short-term in-person stays of 2 to 10 weeks for full-time doctoral students and PhD holders to conduct a research project, give lectures or seminars, or study archival material at an institution in a V4 country other than their country of citizenship and residence; it pays a lump-sum scholarship of EUR 500 per week in two instalments (80% and 20%). The separate Visegrad Scholarship Program supports Master's and post-Master's students and researchers for up to two semesters at institutions in Central and Eastern Europe and its next cycle opens on 1 January 2027. Other Fund programmes include the Visegrad-Taiwan Scholarships for doctoral and post-doctoral researchers, the Western Balkans-Visegrad Fellowships, research grants at the Historical Archives of the EU, and a scholarship at the Open Society Archives in Budapest.

scholarships.title: Ontario Graduate Scholarship (OGS) - University of Toronto
scholarships.description: The Ontario Graduate Scholarship program encourages excellence in graduate studies at publicly-assisted universities in Ontario and has provided merit-based scholarships to Ontario's best graduate students in all disciplines since 1975. At the University of Toronto the program is jointly funded by the Province of Ontario and the University of Toronto, and the Province allocates OGS awards to universities specifying how many each may offer annually. The OGS is worth $5,000 per session at U of T, and the awarding graduate unit contributes one-third of the total award cost. Deadlines and application dates are set by each graduate unit, with results in mid-July.

scholarships.description: The Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development - Phase 2 (SEED-2) program is offered by Global Affairs Canada as a key initiative under Canada's Indo-Pacific Strategy, funded under that strategy. It expands the Canada-ASEAN Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development (SEED) programme to students from ASEAN Member States, Pacific Island Countries and Mongolia, who conduct short-term study or research at Canadian post-secondary institutions in areas contributing to the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Four award components are offered, from $10,200 to $15,900, with durations of four to eight months.

scholarships.description: The Václav Havel Bursary is Charles University's own financial support for international students whose studies are hindered or prevented by repression under totalitarian, authoritarian or other non-democratic regimes anywhere in the world. Students from countries where humanitarian organisations report violated human rights and freedoms and where discriminatory measures restrict access to education may apply, provided they have already been admitted and enrolled in a degree programme at a Charles University faculty through the standard admissions procedure. scholarships.description: The Visegrad Scholarship Program supports full-time Master's and post-Master's students and researchers in all disciplines and in any language for one to two semesters at more than 190 accredited higher-education institutions across Central and Eastern Europe. scholarships.title: CTU Scholarship for Foreign Students - Czech Technical University in Prague
scholarships.description: CTU awards a scholarship to foreign students who wish to take a Master study programme at the Czech Technical University in Prague and display qualities that entitle them to the award, and to foreign doctoral students capable of doing scientific work who study on a doctoral programme in English at CTU in Prague. The Master's award is a contribution towards the costs of a stay in the Czech Republic of up to CZK 10,000 per month for one to two semesters; the doctoral award covers the basic doctoral-study scholarship plus living costs of up to CZK 16,000 per month for six to twelve months. scholarships.title: Aalto University Excellence Scholarship (100% tuition fee waiver)
scholarships.description: The Aalto University Excellence Scholarship is a merit-based, competitive tuition fee waiver awarded to non-EU/non-EEA applicants who are liable to pay Aalto tuition fees. It covers the full tuition fee for the target time of the degree programme - three years for a bachelor's degree and two years for a master's degree. Applications are made as part of the normal admission process, and only a very limited number of scholarships are awarded, with some programmes awarding none. The scholarship does not cover living costs in Finland, which students must fund themselves.

Continued for the second academic year (third for a bachelor's) subject to satisfactory study progress

Agree to the terms of the scholarship by the given deadline after the scholarship decision.

scholarships.selection_notes:
Aalto University Excellence Scholarships are merit-based and are granted on a competitive basis to the highest-achieving applicants based on the programme's evaluation criteria.
Each study option evaluates and ranks applications that are complete and meet the general eligibility criteria, based on its own selection criteria, which may include the relevance of previous studies, academic performance, motivation and, in the fields of art, design and architecture, a portfolio.
The applications are compared to each other, and the highest-ranked applicants are admitted; since the number of study places is restricted, not all eligible applicants will receive an offer of admission, and study options are not required to fill all available places.
There is a very limited number of scholarships available, and programmes may also decide not to grant any scholarships.
For the bachelor's-to-master's continuation route: completion of the bachelor's degree within the target time period and a weighted average grade of at least 3.50, calculated from the completed degree in its entirety.

scholarships.description: The Embassy of France in South Africa invites citizens of South Africa, Lesotho and Malawi to apply for Master's or PhD study at French higher education institutions in the 2027/28 academic year under the France Excellence scheme. scholarships.title: ANRF Ramanujan Fellowship
scholarships.description: The Ramanujan Fellowship, operated by the Anusandhan National Research Foundation, is a reverse brain drain scheme that brings brilliant Indian and Indian-origin scientists and engineers from abroad to take up scientific research positions in India. It is scientist-specific and highly selective, restricted to candidates below 40 years of age who hold a higher degree such as a PhD in science or engineering, a master's in engineering or technology, or an MD, with adequate professional experience and a proven track record evidenced by publications and recognition. Fellows must not already hold any permanent, tenure-track or contractual position in an Indian institution or university, and must be working abroad at the time of nomination. The fellowship pays Rs 1,35,000 per month consolidated including HRA, plus a research grant of Rs 7.00 lakh per annum and Rs 60,000 per annum in overhead charges to the host institute.
scholarships.deadline: No fixed application deadline is published; nominations are submitted year-round through the ANRF online portal and selections are made periodically by an empowered Selection Committee.
scholarships.deadline_display: No fixed application deadline is published; nominations are submitted year-round through the ANRF online portal and selections are made periodically by an empowered Selection Committee.

Be below 40 years of age
Hold a higher degree or equivalent, such as a PhD in Science or Engineering, a Master's in Engineering or Technology, or an MD in Medicine, and have adequate professional experience
Have a proven outstanding track record evidenced by research publications and recognitions
Be working abroad at the time of nomination
Not hold any permanent, tenure-track or contractual position in any Indian institute or university
Not already hold a Ramanujan Fellowship
benefits: Consolidated monthly fellowship of Rs 1,35,000 including HRA
Annual research grant of Rs 7.00 lakh to the host institute
Annual overhead charges of Rs 60,000 to the host institute
One international travel per year
Eligibility to apply for regular extramural research grants through Government of India S&T agencies
Travel and daily allowance entitlement equivalent to Scientist-D for TA/DA

Nominations from the candidate's PhD supervisors or from the institute where the PhD was pursued will not be considered
Upload the research proposal as a single PDF of no more than 5 pages
Join the host institute within six months of the selection intimation letter, or the award is cancelled
scholarships.duration: Five years, not extendable
scholarships.application_period: Continuous. Nominees register on the ANRF portal, fill the Ramanujan Fellowship nomination form and send it to their nominator at the host institution, who verifies and submits it to ANRF. Selection is made periodically by an empowered Selection Committee.
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection is made periodically by an empowered Selection Committee specially appointed for the purpose. Candidates approach the institution of their choice for hosting and the institution forwards the nomination to ANRF.

scholarships.title: Government of Ireland Postgraduate Scholarship Programme
scholarships.description: The Government of Ireland Postgraduate Scholarship Programme awards individual, prestigious research scholarships to excellent postgraduate researchers in Ireland. The award is worth up to €34,000 per annum for 1-4 years, made up of a €25,000 stipend, a fee contribution of up to €5,750 and €3,250 of eligible direct costs. scholarships.title: University of Bologna Study Grants and Subsidies

MEXT publishes the terms in the FY2027 Application Guidelines and the application is made through a Japanese embassy or consulate general, or through a university recommendation. The award pays a monthly scholarship, exempts tuition at the accepting university and provides round-trip airfare. Under embassy recommendation the scholarship runs for five years including one year of Japanese language training.

scholarships.title: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2026 (Japanese Studies Students)
scholarships.description: The Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2026 (Japanese Studies Students) funds international undergraduates who major in Japanese language or Japanese culture to study for one year at designated Japanese universities. Applicants must already have studied Japanese studies for at least one year and must remain enrolled at their home institution on return. MEXT states that it "offers scholarships to international students who wish to study for a period of one year at designated Japanese universities as Japanese Studies Students". The award pays a monthly scholarship, exempts tuition and provides round-trip airfare.
scholarships.deadline: "Recruitment for those arriving in Japan next October is made between December of the previous year and the following February. The first screening is conducted between January and February by the Japanese embassies or consulates general."
scholarships.deadline_display: "Recruitment for those arriving in Japan next October is made between December of the previous year and the following February. The first screening is conducted between January and February by the Japanese embassies or consulates general."

Nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan; Japanese nationals are not eligible
Undergraduate at a foreign (non-Japanese) university at the time of arriving in and leaving Japan, and still enrolled there on return
Majoring in a field related to the Japanese language and/or Japanese culture
Has studied Japanese studies at university for a total of one year or more as of 1 September 2026
Japanese language ability sufficient to receive education at a Japanese university in Japan
Physician-signed health certificate confirming no condition hindering study in Japan
benefits: JPY 117,000 per month scholarship
Tuition exemption for the one-year course
One year of Japanese Studies Program study at a designated Japanese university
Round-trip airfare between the home country and Japan

scholarships.degree: Undergraduate, Master's, PhD, Junior College, College of Technology, Specialized Training College, University Preparatory Course, Japanese Language Institute
scholarships.description: The JASSO Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students is a stipend for privately financed international students in Japan with excellent academic and character records who face financial difficulties. It is not open for direct application: each educational institution nominates candidates to JASSO, and the number of candidates depends on the institution's international enrolment. The stipend is JPY 48,000 per month at graduate and undergraduate level and JPY 30,000 per month at Japanese language institutes, for 12 or 6 months.

scholarships.title: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan - Standard Program (Open Call)
scholarships.description: The JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan (Standard Program) let excellent postdoctoral researchers from other countries conduct cooperative research in Japan with a Japanese host researcher. JSPS runs two open-call rounds a year and awarded 120 fellowships in each FY2027 round. The fellowship pays a maintenance allowance of JPY 362,000 per month, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance of JPY 200,000 and overseas travel insurance. Applications are submitted by the host researcher through the JSPS Electronic Application System, not by candidates directly.

scholarships.description: The Short-term Program (PE) of the JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan lets young PhD holders and PhD researchers conduct collaborative research in Japan for between 1 and 12 months. It is restricted to candidates from the United States, Canada, EU member states, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Norway and Russia, who hold a doctoral degree obtained within the previous six years or are currently enrolled in a doctoral course abroad. JSPS runs three open-call rounds a year and awards 20 fellowships per round. The maintenance allowance is JPY 362,000 per month for PhD holders and JPY 200,000 for non-PhD holders, on top of a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance and overseas travel insurance.

scholarships.title: JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan - Short-term (FY2027, 2nd Recruitment)
scholarships.description: The JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan invite mid-career and senior overseas researchers to Japan for lectures, discussions and exchange activities hosted by a Japanese researcher. The short-term option runs 14 to 60 days and covers a round-trip economy air ticket, a maintenance allowance of JPY 18,000 per day, overseas travel insurance and a host-applied research support allowance of up to JPY 150,000. The candidate does not apply directly: a host researcher in Japan submits the application through the head of their institution.
scholarships.deadline: FY2027 2nd Recruitment (Short-term): Application deadline (from host institution to JSPS) April 23, 2027 (by 5 p.m. (JST)). The first FY2027 recruitment deadline was August 28, 2026. Note that host institutions set their own internal deadlines, which 'depending on the institution, it may have its own deadline more than one month before the application deadline set by JSPS'.
scholarships.deadline_display: FY2027 2nd Recruitment (Short-term): Application deadline (from host institution to JSPS) April 23, 2027 (by 5 p.m. (JST)). The first FY2027 recruitment deadline was August 28, 2026. Note that host institutions set their own internal deadlines, which 'depending on the institution, it may have its own deadline more than one month before the application deadline set by JSPS'.
eligibility: Candidate eligibility (both conditions must be satisfied at the time of application, at the time of selection, and during the fellowship period): (1) Be a citizen or permanent resident of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan. (Taiwan and Palestine are treated in this manner.) Persons of Japanese nationality are eligible to apply if they have resided at the time of application in a foreign country for 10 years or longer and are judged at a host research institution to have played an active role in that country's scientific community. (2) Be a full-time researcher or person with full-time researcher status at a university or research institution in a foreign country and have a position equivalent to a professor, associate professor or assistant professor in Japan (including positions such as professor emeritus). Researchers of other status may apply if it has been six years or longer since they obtained their doctoral degree and the host research institution judges them to have continuously conducted research at a foreign university or research institution.

Host researcher (applicant) eligibility: be affiliated with a research institution specified in Article 2 of the Procedure for the Handling of Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research (KAKENHI) issued by MEXT, be eligible to apply for a KAKENHI grant, and wish to host an overseas researcher.

Host researcher eligibility: be a full-time researcher. However, researchers who are not employed full time may be eligible if the host institution judges them able to execute their responsibility to carrying out the program uninterruptedly throughout the Fellow's tenure including providing them a suitable research environment (e.g. laboratory, space, facilities and personnel) in the same way that a full-time researcher would be able to do.
Selection policy requires that the applicant (host researcher) and candidate have established contact in advance and created a concrete activity plan.
benefits: JSPS provides fellows with useful information on living in Japan, opportunities to foster interactions among researchers, and avenues for conducting outreach activities.
JSPS supports the Science Dialogue Program, enabling fellows to give lectures in English on their research work at high schools in the vicinity of their Japanese host institutes.
Access to the JSPS Fellows Plaza network and alumni follow-up activities after the fellowship.
requirements: Applications must be submitted to JSPS by a host researcher in Japan via the head of their university or institution.
The host researcher must choose the review section in which the application will be screened from the FY2027 Review Section Table, referring to the FY2027 Review Section Set.

The host institution's application must be sent to the president of JSPS by the application deadline for the programme, verified as approved by the head of the institution and confirmed that the stated requirements will be carried out if approved.
Before sending the application, the institution must check the 'List of Applications' on the JSPS Electronic Application System to verify that the registered information is correct.
A Research Proposal Document (S-2) must be completed jointly by the applicant (host researcher) and the candidate.
A Fellow's Curriculum Vitae (S-3) must be completed by the candidate.
scholarships.duration: 14 to 60 days
scholarships.application_period: FY2027 2nd recruitment: host-institution submissions to JSPS by 5 p.m. JST on 23 April 2027; selection results published in early August 2027; periods for arrival in Japan 1 October 2027 - 31 March 2028. The JSPS Electronic Application System becomes available approximately two months before each JSPS deadline.
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection of the applicant (host researcher) and the candidate (invited overseas researcher) is done by the JSPS International Program Committee, made up of Japan's frontline researchers. Selection is carried out through a document review in the first stage and a panel review in the second. Reviewers with a potential conflict of interest are removed, and all Review Committee Members must comply with confidentiality and non-disclosure agreements. Document reviews are conducted by three examiners per application, using a graduated 1-5 scale (5 superlative, 4 excellent, 3 good, 2 fair, 1 poor), taking into account research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity and future potential; the averaged document-review score is the primary screening criterion for panel review. Two selection judgements are made: Selected and Not-selected.

scholarships.title: NL Scholarship (formerly Holland Scholarship)
scholarships.description: The NL Scholarship is the Dutch national scholarship programme for bachelor and master students from outside the European Economic Area. It is financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science together with Dutch research universities and universities of applied sciences. Study in NL states the scholarship amounts to € 5,000 and is paid in the first year of studies, and explicitly notes that it is not a full-tuition scholarship. Institutions set their own application deadlines and their own amount tiers, so the value and the deadline both depend on the institution you apply to.

requirements: Apply for an NL Scholarship-eligible programme at a participating institution and meet that institution's admission and scholarship requirements.
