scholarships.selection_notes: Utrecht University assesses applications on the academic background shown in the master's programme application, the motivation explaining the relevance of the time in the Netherlands and at Utrecht University to future goals, and the quality and feasibility of the financial plan. Radboud University assesses on academic excellence (outstanding study results, relevance of the previous degree to the programme, ranking of the university where previous degrees were obtained) and ambition (quality and relevance of the motivation letter, promise shown by achievements, life experience and extracurricular activities such as internships or volunteering), with each faculty considering its own applicants individually. Admission to the programme and selection for the scholarship are two separate processes.

scholarships.title: Eric Bleumink Fellowship
scholarships.description: The Eric Bleumink Fellowship is a University of Groningen grant for nationals of a listed group of countries who hold provisional or unconditional admission to a one or two year master's programme starting in September. The grant covers tuition fee, international travel, subsistence, books and health insurance. It is nomination-based: the University of Groningen's Admission Office decides which admitted applicants are nominated, so there is no direct scholarship application. The University of Groningen states that a considerable number of students apply each year while it can issue only a limited number of grants.
scholarships.deadline: There is no scholarship application deadline: "It is not possible to actively apply for an Eric Bleumink Fellowship Scholarship. Suitable candidates will be informed about a nomination." Applicants must hold a provisional or unconditional admission offer for a master programme received before February, and their master's application "should be completed by the applicant before 1st of December".

scholarships.title: KITLV Visiting Fellowship
scholarships.description: The KITLV Visiting Fellowship is a three month funded research stay at the Royal Netherlands Institute of Southeast Asian and Caribbean Studies (KITLV) in Leiden for researchers who hold a PhD in the social sciences and/or humanities and are not tax residents of the Netherlands. Fellows work on a publication or research project of their own choice in Southeast Asian or Caribbean Studies and do not need a university or research institute affiliation. The offer covers a return economy air or train fare, reimbursement of accommodation costs in Leiden up to EUR 2,000 per month against proof of payment, and a case-by-case monthly compensation for higher living costs. It is explicitly not a salaried position and fellows are expected to have a steady income during the stay.

scholarships.title: Tilburg University Waiver
scholarships.description: The Tilburg University Waiver halves the institutional tuition fee for up to 21 non-EEA international applicants each year, as part of the university's Diversity, Equity and Inclusion commitment. It applies to all regular one-year Master's programmes starting in September 2027, with the two-year Master in Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence as an explicit exception; Research Master's and Pre-Master's students are not eligible. Applicants must have completed their most recent degree in a designated country and must not already hold any other tuition-fee waiver. If more eligible applicants apply than there are waivers, recipients are chosen by random lottery, and outcomes are notified by 1 June 2027.
scholarships.deadline: Both the Master's programme application and the waiver webform must be completed by the same date: "Submit your application for a Tilburg University Master's program by April 1, 2027" and "Complete the Tilburg University Waiver application form before April 1, 2027". Outcomes are notified by June 1, 2027.

Outcomes are notified by June 1, 2027.

Submit a complete application for a regular one-year Master's program starting in September 2027 by April 1, 2027

scholarships.title: Radboud Scholarship Programme
scholarships.description: The Radboud Scholarship Programme is a highly selective Radboud University scheme for talented, highly motivated non-EU/non-EEA students with outstanding study results, covering English-taught Master's programmes. A scholarship reduces the tuition fee to EUR 2,771 (the university notes the amount is to be confirmed) instead of an illustrative EUR 19,000, and additionally covers visa, residence permit, health insurance and liability insurance costs. Costs of living and studying in the Netherlands are not covered. A maximum of 26 scholarships are available for 2027/2028, allocated across six faculties, and selection is based on academic excellence, ambition and the quality of two reference letters.
scholarships.deadline: Two official deadlines: "You must have submitted your application in the online OSIRIS Application system on 31 January 2027 23:59 CET at the latest", after which the application must be complete "by 14 February 2027 23:59 CET at the latest" and "incomplete applications will not be considered for the scholarship selection". Final decisions are notified before mid-April 2027.

Final decisions are notified before mid-April 2027.

scholarships.title: University of Amsterdam Scholarships
scholarships.description: The University of Amsterdam runs several scholarship programmes for talented and motivated international students, published from one official Fees and funding hub. The flagship is the Amsterdam Merit Scholarship for outstanding students from outside the EU/EEA planning a Master's programme at the UvA. Each faculty also runs its own scholarships for international Master's students, covering Economics and Business, Humanities, Law, Science and Social and Behavioural Sciences, and a separate set of Bachelor's scholarships exists. The Amsterdam Merit Scholarship equals the tuition fee but the UvA states it cannot be used as a partial tuition waiver, so the recipient still pays the full tuition, payable in monthly instalments. Amounts are set annually and are published by each faculty.

scholarships.title: New Zealand Space Scholarship
scholarships.description: The New Zealand Space Scholarship gives postgraduate STEM students a fully supported three-month internship at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California, working alongside scientists and engineers on space missions and research. Applications for the 2027 scholarship opened on 1 October 2026 and the internship runs from July to September 2027. The scholarship covers return economy flights to the United States, accommodation, a daily living allowance and reasonable travel-related expenses including insurance support where applicable. Applicants must be New Zealand citizens aged 18 or over, enrolled in a postgraduate STEM qualification at a New Zealand tertiary institution in a field relevant to NASA's mission priorities, and hold at least a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale.

Be available to undertake the internship in person from July to September 2027 (dates subject to change)
Be willing to undergo any required health and security checks for travel to the United States and entry into US federal facilities
Be eligible for a J1 or F1 visa and understand the applicable visa conditions
Be able to obtain appropriate travel and medical insurance
Not currently hold, and never have held, citizenship in a country listed on NASA's Designated Countries List

scholarships.selection_notes: The scholarship is highly competitive. Candidates are assessed on academic excellence, relevance of experience to JPL projects, personal qualities and self-management, and commitment to contributing to JPL and New Zealand's space sector. Final shortlisted candidates are submitted to JPL for final selection, so MBIE's assessment is not the final word.

scholarships.title: Rhodes Scholarship for New Zealand
scholarships.description: The Rhodes Scholarship for New Zealand is a partnership between the Rhodes Trust and the Robertson Foundation, administered in New Zealand by Universities New Zealand – Te Pōkai Tara. It supports outstanding all-round students to undertake postgraduate study at the University of Oxford, United Kingdom. Up to three scholars are elected from New Zealand each year, and the Scholarship covers fees, accommodation and living costs for up to three years. Applicants must be New Zealand citizens or hold a New Zealand Permanent Resident Visa and must meet an age and undergraduate GPA requirement.

scholarships.title: Ngarimu VC and 28th (Māori) Battalion Memorial Scholarships
scholarships.description: The Ngarimu VC and 28th (Māori) Battalion Memorial Scholarships are annual awards funded by the Ngarimu VC and 28th (Māori) Battalion Memorial Scholarship Fund Board, established in 1945, and administered through the Ministry of Education. They are awarded to exceptional Māori students for vocational or tertiary study who demonstrate values aligned with those of the 28th (Māori) Battalion. Following a $100,000 per year increase from the 2026-27 Budget, 14 scholarships are awarded each year across five schemes: 5 VET, 4 undergraduate, 3 master's, 1 Master of Education research and 1 doctoral. Applicants must be of Māori descent or whakapapa to a recognised Māori iwi and be enrolling in or continuing full-time tertiary study.

scholarships.title: Walczak NAWA Programme
scholarships.degree: Doctoral (PhD students and doctoral-school participants); also doctors and academic teachers
scholarships.description: The Walczak NAWA Programme funds international mobility for researchers in medical, pharmaceutical and health sciences connected with Polish institutions, letting them carry out research and work alongside leading specialists in the best medical centres worldwide. Participants choose a teaching, research or clinical track for a stay of one to six months. Eligible applicants are PhD students and doctoral-school participants, doctors with at least a doctorate working in hospitals and other medical institutions, and academic teachers in the medical, pharmaceutical and health sciences. The support, described by NAWA as covering a stipend, living and accommodation costs and travel expenses, amounts to up to PLN 32,000 for each month of stay, with a one-off PLN 20,000 for doctoral students and researchers on the scientific path whose stay exceeds three months. NAWA's call page still shows the December 2024 edition as the most recent announcement.

scholarships.description: The Temasek Undergraduate Local Scholarship is a merit-based award for talented students pursuing a full-time STEM undergraduate degree programme at the Singapore Institute of Technology, offered to polytechnic graduates. Each scholarship is valued at up to S$18,030 per annum, including an annual stipend of S$7,200, with a one-time S$2,000 laptop allowance in the first year of study and a possible one-time S$10,000 Global Mobility Grant for an eligible global exposure programme. scholarships.title: SUTD Undergraduate Merit Scholarship
scholarships.description: The SUTD Undergraduate Merit Scholarship is an academic merit award for applicants to SUTD bachelor's degree programmes. It pays the subsidised tuition fees, after the Tuition Grant, for the normal duration of the programme, up to four years. It carries no bond, but the recipient must take up the Singapore Government's Tuition Grant Scheme to enjoy subsidised fees. Recipients must maintain good academic standing, reviewed every term, and complete at least 20 hours of service to the University. Applications are made as part of the SUTD admission application.

scholarships.title: African Research Universities Alliance (ARUA) Scholarship
scholarships.description: Lund University runs the ARUA Scholarship as part of its global scholarship programme for high-achieving African students who have demonstrated academic excellence at an ARUA member university. The award is selective and merit-based and covers a percentage of tuition fees up to a maximum of 90%, depending on the budget of the programme or faculty concerned; living costs are not covered. Applicants must first apply for an international degree programme at Lund University with Lund as first choice, then apply through a separate Lund scholarship portal that opens by email invitation in early February each year.

Citizens of countries in the Pacific and Asia, including Russia (East-West Center publishes country lists for the Pacific Region, Southeast Asia, South Asia and East Asia)
Minimum grade point average of 3.0 (4.0=A scale) or the equivalent in the last four semesters or six quarters of the undergraduate record and in all post-baccalaureate work
A 4-year bachelor's degree or equivalent from an accredited US college or university, or a recognized institution of higher learning abroad, obtained before the award starts

scholarships.title: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP) 2027 - Application Window #1 (Developing Country Nationals)
scholarships.description: The JJ/WBGSP is a fully funded master's scholarship for mid-career professionals from listed World Bank developing countries who are already admitted to one of a fixed set of participating development-related master's programmes. For the 2027 cycle the World Bank states that a scholarship provides tuition, a monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus, economy class round-trip airfare, basic medical insurance obtained through the university, and a US$600 travel allowance for each trip. The amount of the monthly subsistence allowance varies depending on the host country and is not published on the programme page. The Government of Japan solely funds the scholarship on an annual basis, and scholars commit to return to their home country after earning their degree.
scholarships.deadline: Application Window #1 from January 18 to February 26, 2027. The programme also runs Application Window #2 from March 29 to May 21, 2027. The link to the JJ/WBGSP application form is only communicated to candidates admitted unconditionally (except for funding) to a participating master's programme and shortlisted as eligible by that university.
scholarships.deadline_display: Application Window #1 from January 18 to February 26, 2027. The programme also runs Application Window #2 from March 29 to May 21, 2027. The link to the JJ/WBGSP application form is only communicated to candidates admitted unconditionally (except for funding) to a participating master's programme and shortlisted as eligible by that university.
eligibility: Be a national of a World Bank member developing country on the published 2027 eligible list
Not hold dual citizenship of any developed country
Be in good health
Hold a bachelor's (or equivalent) degree earned at least 3 years prior to the Application Deadline date

Be employed in development-related work in a paid full-time position at the time of submitting the scholarship application, with at least 3 years of paid development-related employment since earning a bachelor's degree (or equivalent university degree) and acquired within the past 6 years from the date of the application deadline

On or before the scholarship application deadline date, be admitted unconditionally (except for funding) for the upcoming academic year to at least one of the JJ/WBGSP participating master's programs located outside of the applicant's country of citizenship and country of residence listed at the time the call for scholarship applications opens; the letter of admission must be uploaded before submitting the scholarship application

Not be an Executive Director, his/her alternate, and/or staff of any type of appointment of the World Bank Group, and not be a close relative of any of the aforementioned by blood or adoption (close relative defined as Mother, Father, Sister, Half-sister, Brother, Half-brother, Son, Daughter, Aunt, Uncle, Niece, or Nephew)
Individuals who have previously been offered a JJ/WBGSP scholarship but declined it, or who previously received a JJ/WBGSP scholarship but did not graduate, are not eligible to apply again
Exception: applicants from a country on the list of Fragile and Conflict States in Annex 3 of the Application Guidelines may have their limited employment opportunities taken into consideration
benefits: The scholarship covers the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less
Participation in the JJ/WBGSP alumni community of more than 7,000 mid-career professionals from 160 developing countries and Japan
requirements: Must already hold an unconditional admission letter (except for funding) from a JJ/WBGSP participating master's program, located outside the applicant's country of citizenship and country of residence as listed when the call opened
The letter of admission must be uploaded before submitting the scholarship application

The link to the JJ/WBGSP application form is only communicated to candidates who are admitted unconditionally (except for finance) to a participating master's program and shortlisted as eligible JJ/WBGSP applicants by the participating university
All eligibility criteria are strictly adhered to with no exceptions; they will not change during an open call for applications
scholarships.duration: The duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less
scholarships.application_period: Two application rounds per cycle, organised to match the academic calendars of the participating programmes. For the 2027 cycle: Application Window #1 January 18 - February 26, 2027; Application Window #2 March 29 - May 21, 2027. Each participating university sets its own admission deadlines, which fall before the JJ/WBGSP window closes.
scholarships.selection_notes: Two qualified assessors independently review each eligible application and score it from 1 to 10 on four factors: quality of professional experience (30% weight), quality of professional recommendations (30% weight), quality of commitment to the applicant's home country (30% weight), and quality of education background (10% weight). The Secretariat uses the average of the two assessors plus a reasonably wide geographical distribution of awards, a reasonable distribution across gender, unusual circumstances or hardships, and giving scholarships to applicants who otherwise have limited access to financial resources for graduate studies abroad. Finalists go to the JJ/WBGSP Steering Committee, composed of members of the World Bank Board of Directors and World Bank management, for approval.

scholarships.title: Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: The Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship Program is a program of the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs that provides up to $5,000 in merit-based scholarships to outstanding American undergraduate students with high financial need to pursue credit-bearing academic studies and career-oriented internships abroad. It is congressionally funded, established by the U.S. Congress in 2001, and administered by the Institute of International Education since its inception. Applicants must be receiving a Federal Pell Grant during the time of application or be able to prove they will receive one during their term abroad. The programme has funded American students to study and intern abroad in more than 170 countries, with recipients from all 50 U.S. states and D.C.
scholarships.deadline: Fall 2026 application cycle: deadline October 1, 2026 at 11:59PM PT, now closed. Next cycle, Spring 2027: student deadline February 25, 2027 at 11:59pm Pacific Time, with the advisor certification deadline March 4, 2027 and the application cycle opening mid-January 2027.

Next cycle, Spring 2027: student deadline February 25, 2027 at 11:59pm Pacific Time, with the advisor certification deadline March 4, 2027 and the application cycle opening mid-January 2027.
eligibility: Be an American undergraduate student
Have high financial need
Be receiving a Federal Pell Grant at the time of application, or be able to provide proof that a Pell Grant will be received during the term of the study abroad program or internship
Apply for the correct scholarship term matching the student's programme dates
benefits: Up to USD 5,000 merit-based scholarship for study abroad or an international internship
Access to the Gilman alumni network of more than 50,000 American students and professionals
requirements: Federal Pell Grant eligibility
Advisor certification of the submitted application
Submission in Pacific Time; late applications are not accepted
Application for the correct scholarship term according to programme dates
scholarships.duration: Duration of study abroad program
scholarships.application_period: Rolling annual cycles by study-abroad term. The application cycle opens mid-January 2027 for the Spring 2027 term; all applicants are notified of their status by email in May 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications move through a published process: the cycle opens, students submit, advisors certify, the Gilman Program screens eligibility, selection panelists recommend eligible applications, the U.S. Department of State reviews and approves, and the Gilman Program sends award notifications to all applicants. 72% of Gilman scholars come from small towns or rural communities.

scholarships.title: Boren Awards (Boren Scholarships and Boren Fellowships)
scholarships.description: The Boren Awards fund intensive overseas language study for U.S. undergraduate students (Boren Scholarships) and research or language study for U.S. graduate students (Boren Fellowships). They pay a fixed grant of $8,000, $12,500 or $25,000 depending on the duration of overseas study, and the programme states plainly that the award "is not all-inclusive" and is designed to cover only the majority of an awardee's overseas expenses. In exchange, recipients commit to at least one year of federal service in support of U.S. national security after graduation.
scholarships.deadline: National deadlines for the 2027 Boren Awards: Boren Fellowships January 20, 2027; Boren Scholarships January 27, 2027 - both 5pm Eastern time.
scholarships.deadline_display: National deadlines for the 2027 Boren Awards: Boren Fellowships January 20, 2027; Boren Scholarships January 27, 2027 - both 5pm Eastern time.
eligibility: U.S. citizens at the time of the national application deadline
A high school graduate, or have earned a GED
At least 18 years of age or older by the time the application is submitted
Planning an overseas program in an overseas destination outside of Western Europe, Canada, Australia, or New Zealand
Planning to study in an overseas destination of which they are not a citizen

Matriculated for the duration of their Boren Awards-funded program in an undergraduate or graduate degree program located within the United States and accredited by a body recognized by the U.S. Department of Education
For ROTC cadets, midshipmen and members of the military Reserves or National Guard: in inactive, non-drilling status for the duration of their Boren Awards-funded program

Boren Scholarships applicants must be matriculated in an associate's or bachelor's degree program at the time of application and must remain matriculated in an undergraduate degree program; they may not graduate until the scholarship is complete

Boren Fellowships applicants may be matriculated in or applying to a graduate degree program, but Boren Fellows must be matriculated in a graduate degree program by the start date of the fellowship and may not graduate until the fellowship is complete

Eligible graduate degree programs include master's (MA, MS, MBA, LLM and others), juris doctor (JD), or doctoral (PhD, MD and others) programs; non-degree certificate programs are not eligible by themselves
benefits: NSEP Service Team support, including resume reviews, career fairs, a mentorship program and advocacy on behalf of award recipients to human resources and hiring officials at U.S. government agencies
Access to NSEPnet, which features job listings and positions for federal government agencies exclusive to awardees
Non-competitive eligibility: until they fulfill the federal service requirement in full, Boren award recipients are eligible for non-competitive appointments to many federal positions
An annual Federal Employment Seminar in Washington, DC with training on the federal hiring process and networking with senior officials from federal agencies and contractors
Access to the NSEP Alumni Association
requirements: Two letters of recommendation for Boren Scholarships (a third letter is optional); three letters of recommendation for Boren Fellowships, with at least one from a research advisor at the U.S. institution if a research component is proposed
Recommenders may be academic or professional contacts who know the applicant well; they may not be family or friends
Essay 1 - National Security, maximum 800 words, single-spaced
Essay 2 - Motivation and Public Service Careers, maximum 800 words for Boren Scholarships and 1000 words for Boren Fellowships, single-spaced
Study Plan Summary: maximum 250 words for each segment of the proposed overseas program, plus descriptions of alternate overseas destination programs
Weekly contact hours of formal language acquisition - the Boren Awards requires overseas programs contain at least 15-20 weekly language hours

An alternate study abroad program is required for applicants choosing an overseas destination marked with an asterisk (blue on the map) or for the languages Arabic, Mandarin or Russian; it is not required for Mandarin in Taiwan, Arabic in Morocco, or Language Flagship capstone applicants
Employment History: up to three jobs, each described in 50 to 100 words
Activities: up to three extracurricular activities, each described in 50 to 100 words
Language Self-Assessment in the online application, plus up to four additional languages studied or spoken
Up to three non-U.S. countries where you have lived, traveled or studied; up to five relevant honours and awards; optional list of up to five other scholarships applied for
Applicants must agree to the policies in the Submission Information section in order to actually submit
Boren Scholars whose airfare is funded by Boren must comply with the Fly America Act and send a photocopy of the passenger receipt page(s) to their airline to show compliance
All Boren-funded programs must include language study within a classroom as a core element for the duration of the grant
scholarships.duration: 8 to 52 weeks of overseas study; 25-52 weeks preferred; minimum 12 weeks for most applicants (8 weeks minimum for undergraduate STEM summer programmes).
scholarships.application_period: The 2027-2028 Boren Scholarship and Boren Fellowship application cycle is open as of 2026-10-01. National deadlines are January 20, 2027 (Fellowships) and January 27, 2027 (Scholarships), 5pm Eastern time. Selected applicants are notified in mid-to-late April. Campus representatives may set earlier campus deadlines that applicants are asked to respect.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are evaluated by IIE-organized regional merit review panels made up of faculty members and administrators from colleges and universities across the United States, representing a wide array of fields of study. The panels make recommendations on each submitted, eligible application, with final decision-making authority held by the program's federal sponsor, DLNSEO. There is no semi-finalist or interview phase, so everything an applicant would want the selection committee to know must be stated in the essays and other application materials. Selection preference is given to veterans when other factors are equivalent.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship
scholarships.name: Boren Awards (Boren Scholarships and Boren Fellowships)

scholarships.title: Phi Kappa Phi Fellowship
scholarships.description: The Honor Society of Phi Kappa Phi awards 40 Fellowships of $8,500 each, six at $15,000 each, and two at $35,000 each to members entering the first year of graduate or professional study. Established in 1932, the Fellowship Program annually provides funding to first-year graduate students pursuing post-baccalaureate degrees across all academic disciplines. Each active chapter may select one candidate from among its local applicants to compete for the Society-wide awards, and endorsed Phi Kappa Phi Fellows go on to study at some of the nation's top graduate schools. The 2027 cycle opens its application portal on December 15, 2026 and closes at the national deadline of April 15, 2027.
scholarships.deadline: April 15, 2027: National deadline. The application portal opens December 15, 2026, and applicants must apply through their local chapter by the chapter deadline, which varies but is typically two weeks prior to the national deadline. Recipients are notified in summer 2027.
scholarships.deadline_display: April 15, 2027: National deadline. The application portal opens December 15, 2026, and applicants must apply through their local chapter by the chapter deadline, which varies but is typically two weeks prior to the national deadline. Recipients are notified in summer 2027.
eligibility: Must be an active (dues paid) member through April 15, 2027, or have accepted the invitation to join and be initiated by June 30, 2027
Seeking full-time enrollment status in a graduate/professional school program to begin between May 1, 2027, and February 1, 2028
Have not completed more than 9 hours of semester credits of graduate study in any field at the application deadline
Not be a sitting Phi Kappa Phi board member, divisional vice president, member of the Fellowship Award committee or Society employee at the time of application
Be endorsed by and apply through a local active Phi Kappa Phi chapter, which selects one nominee for the Society-wide competition
benefits: 40 Fellowships of $8,500 each
6 Fellowships of $15,000 each
2 Fellowships of $35,000 each
requirements: Active dues-paid membership through April 15, 2027, or accepted invitation with initiation by June 30, 2027
No more than 9 hours of graduate semester credits completed at the application deadline; applicants who completed 10 or more graduate credits on or before April 15 are not eligible
Full-time enrolment in a graduate or professional programme beginning between May 1, 2027 and February 1, 2028
Endorsement and submission through the local chapter by the chapter's own deadline
scholarships.duration: 1 year
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle. The online application portal opens December 15, 2026; applicants submit to their local chapter in late March or early April 2027; the national deadline is April 15, 2027; recipients are notified in summer 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection is based on the applicant's promise of success in graduate or professional study, as evidenced by academic achievement including transcripts, honors and awards, relevant research experience and samples of creative work; service and leadership experience on and off campus; letters of recommendation; a personal statement and career goals; a work sample; and acceptance or application to an approved graduate or professional program.

scholarships.title: NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program (NSF GRFP)
scholarships.description: The NSF GRFP funds full-time graduate students pursuing research-based master's or doctoral degrees in NSF-supported STEM fields at accredited, nonprofit U.S. institutions. Each fellowship provides three years of financial support over a five-year fellowship period: a $37,000 annual stipend paid to the fellow and a $16,000 annual cost-of-education allowance paid to the institution in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees, so there is no tuition or mandatory-fee cost to the student. There is no post-graduate study service requirement, and fellows may transfer to a different institution after completion of the first fellowship year. Estimated 1,500 awards for the 2027 solicitation (NSF 26-526), pending availability of funds.
scholarships.deadline: Reference letters due October 16, 2026 by 8:00 p.m. Eastern time. Application deadlines: October 19, 2026 (Life Sciences); October 20, 2026 (Computer and Information Science and Engineering; Materials Research; Psychology; Social Sciences); October 22, 2026 (Engineering); October 23, 2026 (Chemistry; Geosciences; Mathematical Sciences; Physics and Astronomy). All applications must be received by 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time on the deadline date for the Major Field of Study selected. November 15, 2026 is the last day to withdraw an application without it counting towards the number of times an individual may apply.
scholarships.deadline_display: Reference letters due October 16, 2026 by 8:00 p.m. Eastern time. Application deadlines: October 19, 2026 (Life Sciences); October 20, 2026 (Computer and Information Science and Engineering; Materials Research; Psychology; Social Sciences); October 22, 2026 (Engineering); October 23, 2026 (Chemistry; Geosciences; Mathematical Sciences; Physics and Astronomy). All applications must be received by 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time on the deadline date for the Major Field of Study selected. November 15, 2026 is the last day to withdraw an application without it counting towards the number of times an individual may apply.
eligibility: At the time of submission, must be a U.S. citizen, national, or a permanent resident ("green-card" holder).
Must intend to enroll or be enrolled full-time in an eligible research-based master's or doctoral degree program in an eligible field of study in STEM.
Must never have previously accepted an NSF Graduate Research Fellowship.
Must have declined any previously offered NSF Graduate Research Fellowship by the deadline (if applicable).

Must have completed less than one academic year in a graduate degree program according to the institution's academic calendar; non-degree coursework must be clearly identified in the transcript and does not count toward this limit.
Must not be a current NSF employee.

Degree programs must be at a nonprofit institution of higher education accredited in, and having a campus located in, the United States, its territories, or possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.
An eligible applicant can submit only one application per annual competition.

Fellowships may only be used for an eligible graduate degree program at a nonprofit academic institution accredited in, and having a campus located in, the U.S., its territories, possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.
benefits: Five-year award with three years of financial support.
No post-graduate study service requirement.
Access to supplemental funding to sustain research while on medical leave.
Access to professional development opportunities and the NSF GRFP community.
The fellowship is portable and can be transferred to a different institution of higher education; fellows can transfer after completion of the first fellowship year.
requirements: Prepare and submit the application in the GRFP Application Module on Research.gov.
Create a Research.gov account to access the module.
Provide accurate personal information: full legal name, mailing address, permanent address, date of birth, high school location, and demographic information.
Select a level (Level 1 undergraduate, or Level 2 graduate) in the application.
Provide the list of institutions, enrollment status, enrollment dates and degree conferred (if applicable) for all degree-granting undergraduate and graduate institutions attended.
Provide significant academic honors, fellowships, scholarships, publications and presentations.
Select the Major Field of Study most closely aligned with the proposed graduate program and research plan; the Major Field of Study determines the application deadline and the reviewers.

Request reference letters in the GRFP Application Module and rank them in order of preference; three reference writer names and contact information are required, and two reference letters must be received by NSF.
Provide a Personal, Relevant Background, and Future Goals Statement of a maximum of three pages with headings for Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts.
Provide a Graduate Research Plan Statement of a maximum of two pages with headings for Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts.
Reference letters are due before the NSF GRFP application deadlines, by 8:00 p.m. Eastern time on the reference letter date in the Notice of Funding Opportunity.
All materials are submitted through the GRFP Application Module; emailed and/or physically mailed applications will not be accepted.
Applications are automatically checked by the GRFP Application Module for compliance with the format requirements; documents that are not compliant will not be accepted by the module.
scholarships.duration: Five-year fellowship period with three years of financial support
scholarships.application_period: The GRFP Application Module usually opens in July or August; applications for the 2027 competition close between October 19 and October 23, 2026 depending on Major Field of Study, with reference letters due October 16, 2026. The module opened in time for the 2026 application cycle; the 2027 application deadlines were published August 25, 2026.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are reviewed by disciplinary and interdisciplinary scientists, engineers and STEM experts selected by NSF Program Officers, with care taken to ensure no conflicts of interest. Applications are reviewed in broad areas of related disciplines based on the Major Field of Study selected by the applicant, using the two NSF Merit Review Criteria: Intellectual Merit (potential to advance knowledge) and Broader Impacts (potential to benefit society and contribute to specific, desired societal outcomes). Intellectual Merit factors include the ability to plan and conduct research, work independently, work as part of a team, interpret and communicate research, take initiative, think creatively, solve problems, persist and overcome challenges, and demonstrated intellectual ability as indicated by grades, coursework and awards. Broader Impacts factors include increasing participation in STEM, improving STEM education through outreach and mentoring, increasing public scientific literacy, increasing collaboration among academia and industry, improving educator development, improving societal well-being, developing a globally competitive STEM workforce, improving national security, increasing U.S. economic competitiveness, and enhancing research and education infrastructure. GRFP was established to recruit and support individuals who demonstrate the potential to make significant contributions in STEM.

scholarships.title: Harvard College Need-Based Financial Aid 2027-2028
scholarships.description: Harvard College states: "You can afford Harvard. We know that paying for college is a big concern for many families, and we're committed to making a Harvard education - and the opportunities that come with it - possible for more students than ever." Its stated goal is "to bring the most promising students to Harvard-period", and its financial aid officers "create a comprehensive financial aid package that accounts for the full cost of attendance". Need is assessed on family income, assets and overall circumstances; Harvard states "You'll never be required to take on loans" and that financial circumstances will not affect admission chances. For 2027-2028 the aid application consists of a CSS Profile for everyone, plus IDOC document submission, plus the FAFSA for US citizens, permanent residents and other eligible non-citizens. Harvard publishes three income bands: families at or below $100,000 with typical assets receive aid covering all billed expenses plus extras; at or below $200,000 receive Free Tuition Plus; above $200,000 receive tailored aid. Students are expected to cover $3,500 in personal expenses per academic year, usually through work-study hours.
scholarships.deadline: November 1 for Restrictive Early Action and QuestBridge Match; February 1 for Regular Decision; March 1 for Transfer
scholarships.deadline_display: November 1 for Restrictive Early Action and QuestBridge Match; February 1 for Regular Decision; March 1 for Transfer

US Citizens and Permanent Residents (and other eligible non-citizens) must also submit the FAFSA
All applicants must have an underlying admission application; financial aid is offered once you are admitted, assessed by the Financial Aid Committee
Financial aid packages are calculated from family income, assets and overall financial circumstances
benefits: "You'll never be required to take on loans"
"we typically don't factor in home equity or retirement savings when crafting your aid package"
"Most importantly, your financial situation will not affect your chances of admission to Harvard College"
"Harvard offers generous need-based financial aid for all students, regardless of nationality or citizenship"
Work-study hours available to help cover the $3,500 personal expense expectation
$2,000 start-up grant in the first year and $2,000 launch grant in the junior year (lowest band)
requirements: File the online 2027-2028 CSS Profile via the College Board, including Harvard as a recipient using code 3434
Complete the CSS Profile before IDOC becomes accessible: "you cannot access IDOC until you have completed the CSS Profile"
Submit the 2027-2028 FAFSA (US citizens, permanent residents and other eligible non-citizens), including Harvard's code E00468, filed online or via the mobile app
Submit all applicable tax and other documents through the College Board IDOC Service
If parents are married or living together, one CSS Profile is filed for the family; if separated or divorced, each parent files their own CSS Profile
Declare a Gross Monthly Household Income equivalent - the family income, assets and circumstances that drive the assessment

Family income

scholarships.title: Yale College Need-Based Financial Aid 2027-2028
scholarships.description: Yale College Need-Based Financial Aid is not a separate scholarship application: it is assessed as part of the Yale College admission application, with the applicable date being the admission plan deadline (Regular Decision February 15, 2027). The average annual need-based scholarship awarded to the class of 2029 was $75,220. For families with income below $100,000, a Yale Scholarship covers the full cost of tuition and fees, housing, food, and travel with no loans, and Yale also provides hospitalization insurance.

scholarships.deadline_display: Regular Decision: February 15, 2027

International students go through exactly the same need-based process as domestic students, and MIT states it is committed to meeting 100% of demonstrated financial need for international students, just as for domestic students. scholarships.title: University of Chicago International Student Financial Aid (Need-Based and Merit Scholarships for Undergraduates)
scholarships.description: The University of Chicago states that "Nearly $20 million in need-based financial aid has been offered to international students at UChicago over the past four years, and a recent gift of $35 million for international financial aid has strengthened the University's commitment to enrolling a diverse and talented student body from around the world." Its commitment is explicit: "We are committed to meeting 100% of your demonstrated need with a loan-free financial aid package if you are admitted and applied for funding." Packages "are based on an estimate of the full costs of enrolling at the University of Chicago, including tuition, housing, health insurance, a meal plan, and estimates for additional costs like books and personal expenses." International students must apply for funding during the admissions process; they are not eligible afterwards or during their four years in the College. Separately, UChicago offers partial-tuition merit scholarships - single lump-sum or renewable annual - which are considered independently of financial situation and for which all first-year applicants are automatically considered.

scholarships.description: UNU-WIDER and the South African National Treasury invite proposals under the third phase of the Southern Africa - Towards Inclusive Economic Development (SA-TIED) programme for research using South African tax administrative data. Accepted proposals are paid a research honorarium in the range of US$3,000-10,000 on delivery of a working paper of 10,000 words or fewer, and the resulting papers are published in the SA-TIED research paper series. This is research funding rather than a degree scholarship: the deliverable is a policy paper, and the honorarium is expected to cover all expenses of the research.

scholarships.title: Albert Einstein Distinguished Educator Fellowship (AEF) Program
scholarships.degree: Not a degree programme - professional fellowship for K-12 STEM educators
scholarships.description: The AEF Programme places accomplished K-12 STEM educators for eleven months in federal agencies or U.S. Congressional offices, working on national education programmes and policy. Each fellow receives a monthly living stipend of $8,200, a travel allowance of up to $5,000 for approved travel requested by the host agency, an education allowance of up to $1,000 for approved professional development expenses, relocation reimbursement of up to $3,500 for fellows relocating from outside the Washington, DC area, and a health insurance stipend of up to $550 per month on an individual plan or $1,300 per month on a family plan. The DOE sponsors up to five congressional office placements. The programme is a single eleven-month appointment; it is not a degree award and involves no tuition.
scholarships.deadline: Application deadline 8:00pm Eastern, November 5, 2026. Online application opened August 3, 2026. The application period typically opens in mid-August, with applications due in mid-November.
scholarships.deadline_display: Application deadline 8:00pm Eastern, November 5, 2026. Online application opened August 3, 2026. The application period typically opens in mid-August, with applications due in mid-November.
eligibility: Be a U.S. citizen at the time of applying (by the November 5, 2026 application deadline).

Have a minimum of five complete years of full-time classroom teaching experience prior to submitting the application; student teaching does not count toward this minimum full-time teaching requirement.

Have been teaching full-time in a public or private elementary or secondary school for at least five of the last seven years in a science, technology, engineering, or mathematics (STEM) discipline; current employment may be as an educator or district official.
Be currently employed full-time in a public or private elementary or secondary school or school district in the U.S.
Be able to provide a letter of recommendation from a school district official as one of their three required letters of recommendation.
Be able to obtain a leave of absence from teaching in order to participate in the program for the full eleven months.
benefits: Develops a professional development plan to guide individual professional development objectives outside host office responsibilities, with ongoing mentoring provided by the AEF Programme.
Access to a national network of education leaders and programmes.
Placement in a federal agency or U.S. Congressional office, with the DOE sponsoring up to five placements in congressional offices.
Up to ten personal days off per year and up to ten sick days off without reduction in the Fellow's stipend.
Fellows are connected with outgoing Fellows to help identify available housing in the Washington, DC area.
requirements: All applications must be completed online through the online application system.
Applicants must meet all eligibility requirements.
All applications, including recommendations, are due by the specified application deadline; only complete applications submitted by the deadline will be considered for evaluation and placement.
Materials uploaded into the application system provide the sole basis for evaluation.

Completion of all required fields, including contact information; education background (formal education and continuing education); teaching and professional experience; professional awards and recognition; citizenship status; interest in federal agency and/or Congressional office placement; and five essay questions.
Submission of three letters of recommendation online, including one recommendation letter from a school district official.
School district officials do not include department chairs, assistant principals, associate principals or vice-principals.

Applicants are responsible for ensuring their recommenders have the information needed to access the online Recommender form; requests can only be sent electronically through the online application system.
Provide proof of U.S. citizenship upon accepting a Fellowship offer.
Secure a leave of absence from teaching during the fellowship year.
Complete the eleven-month full-time appointment (mid-August through mid-July) in Washington, DC.
Meet the terms and conditions in the offer letter of appointment, including requirements for ethical conduct, and financial disclosure and conflict of interest.
Participate in the official professional development meetings, conferences and field trips organised for Fellows by the AEF Programme.
Have health care coverage during the fellowship appointment; Fellows are eligible to participate in the ORISE health insurance plan if they do not have other health insurance coverage.
Establish an individual Professional Development Plan for the year, which must be completed by early October.
Submit the requested written reports, presentations and surveys related to the Fellowship experience before the published deadlines.
Represent themselves as educators in a responsible and professional manner.
Only use the AEF Programme name or the Fellow's affiliation with the AEF Programme in an authorised manner.
In managing their responsibilities throughout the fellowship, give priority to the duties assigned to them by their host office.
scholarships.duration: Eleven months, mid-August through mid-July; the fellowship begins on the third Monday in August with the initial programme Orientation
scholarships.application_period: Online application opens August 3, 2026 and closes 8:00pm Eastern on November 5, 2026 for the 2027-2028 programme. Semi-finalist notifications with travel arrangements are made by February 24, 2027; interviews in Washington, DC February 27 - March 1, 2027; finalist notifications March 9, 2027; congressional fellows placement interviews mid-June 2027; fellows arrive in Washington, DC mid-August 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are first subject to an eligibility and compliance review conducted by the AEF Programme to verify applicant eligibility and ensure all required materials have been provided; only applications meeting all requirements are advanced for merit-based evaluation. Merit review is a thorough, consistent and objective examination by evaluators who must be independent of the applicants and of the sponsoring agencies, applying pre-established criteria in four areas: the applicant's teaching experience, professional accomplishments, demonstrated leadership qualities, and interests as they relate to participating in the AEF Programme. Sponsoring federal agencies then review the highly reviewed applications on overall professional experience and demonstrated leadership qualities, the applicant's interest in and preparedness for the fellowship, alignment of the applicant's experience and subject matter expertise with the interests of the host office, and quality of recommendations, and select the top candidates as semi-finalists to interview in Washington, DC. Semi-finalists are invited to Washington, DC for three days of individual interviews and information sessions. Following interviews, final selections are made at the discretion of the sponsoring federal agencies; finalists are contacted by ORISE regarding offers. DOE selects the finalists for Congressional office placements. Recruitment and selection is done without regard to race, gender, age, colour, religion, national origin, mental or physical disability, or status as a veteran.

scholarships.title: Office of Science Graduate Student Research (SCGSR) Program
scholarships.description: SCGSR provides supplemental awards to thesis-based doctoral students to conduct part of their dissertation research at a DOE national laboratory or facility, in collaboration with a DOE laboratory scientist, in a DOE Office of Science priority research area. Awardees receive a monthly living stipend of up to $3,600 while at the host laboratory, plus up to $3,000 total for inbound and outbound transportation if the host laboratory is more than 50 miles from their home graduate institution. The award does not pay tuition or fees, does not cover supplies and materials, and does not cover travel during the project; the student must remain enrolled full-time at their home institution and keep paying their own tuition. Successful applicants are considered guest scientists at the host laboratory, not employees.

eligibility: Applicants must be U.S. Citizens or Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR) at the time of application and be at least 18 years of age at the time of applying.
Applicants must be enrolled full-time in a Qualified Graduate Program with the Ph.D. as their degree objective.
At the time of application, applicants must have obtained the Ph.D. candidacy at their home institution, and must have established a defined graduate thesis project and graduate thesis advisor.
The applicant's primary graduate thesis advisor must provide a Letter of Support.

Applicants must be pursuing a Ph.D. in physics, chemistry, material sciences, biology (non-medical), mathematics, engineering, computer or computational sciences, or select areas of environmental sciences at an accredited college or university in the United States or its territories.
The Ph.D. degree program pursued must require a research thesis/dissertation, with an emphasis on fundamental experimental or theoretical research.

Applicants must demonstrate that their graduate thesis research is in an area of fundamental research aligned with the DOE Office of Science Priority Research Areas identified for the 2026 SCGSR Solicitation 2.
The applicant and their primary graduate thesis advisor are responsible for identifying a collaborating research scientist at a DOE laboratory and jointly developing the research proposal.
Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientists may be from any of the participating DOE national laboratories/facilities.
The duration of the proposed research to be conducted at the DOE laboratory/facility may range from 3 to 12 consecutive months.
For applications in BES priority research areas, eligibility depends also on proximity between the applicant's university and the host DOE national laboratory.
Applicants must remain enrolled as a full-time graduate student in a qualified graduate program during the duration of the proposed SCGSR research project period at the host DOE laboratory/facility.
benefits: Access to DOE national laboratory expertise, user facilities, instrumentation and leadership-class computing systems.
Professional network expansion and access to scientific user facilities not available at most universities.
The possible opportunity for a short international research visit of 6 weeks maximum to an institution such as CERN or RIKEN, applied for after the award is received.
Weekly virtual office hours and application assistance workshops offered by the SCGSR Program.
A running list of collaborating laboratory scientists who are ready to work with SCGSR awardees.
requirements: All applications must be completed through the online application system; only complete applications submitted by the deadline will be considered for review.
Materials uploaded into the online application system provide the sole basis for evaluation.

Complete all required fields: Contact Information; Academic Information including Current Graduate Program Information; Citizenship or Permanent Residency Status; Professional Information such as Scientific Publications and Awards; Graduate Thesis Advisor and Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientist Contact Information.

Submit the SCGSR research proposal, co-developed by the applicant and the collaborating DOE laboratory research scientist in consultation with the primary graduate thesis advisor, as a PDF through the online application.
Upload a PDF copy of current official graduate transcripts.
Provide official proof of Ph.D. candidacy as an official, signed letter from the Registrar's office or from the Chair, Head or Director of Graduate Studies of the applicant's academic department.
Submit two Letters of Support, one from the primary graduate thesis advisor and one from the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist, both completed through the online application system.
Indicate in the online application system which Office of Science priority research area the proposed project aligns with.
List citations of publications and awards, no more than 3 for each, in the appropriate section of the online application; do not submit supplemental materials.

The research proposal must address the stated aims in at least one of the SCGSR Priority Research Areas and must identify how the proposed research will take advantage of the DOE laboratory/facility's research capabilities and assets.

The proposed research must be an integral part of the applicant's overall doctoral thesis project and must be approved by the primary graduate thesis advisor, whose approval is made through the thesis advisor's Letter of Support.
Create an account on the SCGSR online application system well before the deadline and become familiar with the application information requested.
scholarships.duration: 3 to 12 consecutive months of research at a DOE laboratory/facility, within a project period bounded by published earliest and latest start dates
scholarships.application_period: 2026 Solicitation 2: online application opened August 12, 2026 and closes 5:00 PM ET on November 4, 2026. Offer notifications April 1 - 16, 2027. Proposed project periods may start as early as June 7, 2027 and must start no later than October 4, 2027. 2027 Solicitation 1 (tentative): application opens February 2027, applications due May 2027, offers September 2027, project periods starting November 2027 and ending no later than March 2028.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are first subject to an eligibility and compliance review. All eligible and compliant applications are then reviewed externally by subject matter experts in the field of the proposed research, using the DOE Office of Science's standard merit review processes. Two merit review criteria apply: (1) Scientific and/or Technical Merit of the Proposed Research, asking whether the research is well-conceived with a clear understanding of the scientific and technical challenges, whether the method and approach are appropriate, whether the graduate student is sufficiently well prepared, and whether DOE laboratory resources are adequate, including whether necessary access to a scientific user facility has been secured by the collaborating scientist; and (2) Relevance of the Proposed Research to Graduate Thesis Research and Training, asking whether the proposed research can make a significant contribution to the applicant's thesis project and whether it will enhance the applicant's graduate training and research skills. Applications are selected for award based on the results of peer review and other program policy factors, including availability of funds and balance of portfolio. The application materials received, including the research proposal, provide the sole basis for evaluation. Participation in other DOE programmes is collected for internal purposes only and does not affect selection.

scholarships.title: Chevening SIDS Scholarship
scholarships.description: The French Community of Belgium offers the government of Quebec a pool of 60 monthly scholarships per academic year, which the Quebec side may split into short, medium or long terms, for candidates from Quebec pursuing specialised Master's-level or postgraduate studies in the French-speaking Community of Belgium. Each award pays a monthly stipend of EUR 789.71 for second cycle or EUR 963.29 for third cycle programmes, university registration fees, a EUR 24.79 per month materials or travel allowance, and one-off thesis or dissertation printing payments on programme completion. Fields prioritised but not exclusive are life sciences, environmental sciences and new social issues.
scholarships.deadline: Applications for Chevening Scholarships are now open! Applications close at 11:00 UTC on 6 October 2026. 'The deadline for applications is 6 October 2026 at 11:00 UTC. You will not be able to access the online application system after this date.'
scholarships.deadline_display: Applications for Chevening Scholarships are now open! Applications close at 11:00 UTC on 6 October 2026. 'The deadline for applications is 6 October 2026 at 11:00 UTC. You will not be able to access the online application system after this date.'
eligibility: To be eligible for a Chevening SIDS Scholarship, you must meet the standard eligibility criteria for Chevening, and be a citizen from one of the participating countries shown on the map on the official page.
Be a citizen of a Chevening-eligible country or territory.

If applying for an award from an ODA-eligible country, be resident in an ODA-eligible country. This does not have to be the country of citizenship, but all applicants must show a clear intention to support their country of award.
Commit to returning to your home country (country of award) for at least two years after your scholarship ends.
Have at least two years' work experience, acquired after completing your undergraduate degree, equivalent to 2,800 hours.

Hold an undergraduate degree that qualifies you for a UK master's programme. You must have finished your undergraduate studies at least two years before the application deadline, even if you have not yet received your certificate; you will need the certificate by the time of your interview.
Apply to three different and eligible UK university courses, and receive an unconditional offer from at least one by the deadline listed on the application timeline.

Applicants are required to study on courses that help to address a national development priority or capacity shortage. This includes courses relating to: human rights, democracy and the rule of law; climate change and sustainability; economic recovery and growth; supportive societies that help people lead peaceful and productive lives.
benefits: Full tuition fees for a one-year UK master's degree at the university of the scholar's choice
A monthly stipend, stated in the Final Award Letter, which Chevening says is intended to cover all living costs including accommodation
Return flights between the nearest airport in the home country and the nearest airport to the UK university, booked by Chevening's designated travel agency, where confirmed in the Final Award Letter
Student visa application fee and Immigration Health Surcharge ('you don't need to pay the visa fee or the Immigration Health Surcharge')
Arrival allowance where confirmed in the Final Award Letter
Departure allowance for scholars on a full award
A travel grant
requirements: Applications must be submitted through the Chevening online application system reached from your own country/territory page.
Opt in to be considered for the Chevening SIDS Scholarship within the standard Chevening Scholarship application.
Choose three different eligible UK master's degree courses in order of preference; duplicate courses at the same university cannot be considered.
Courses must be full-time, taught master's courses (not research-focused MRes programmes), based in the UK, starting in the autumn term (usually September/October) and lasting nine to twelve months.
Courses cannot be part-time, distance learning, a PhD or DPhil, or include more than one month of study outside the UK.
Provide the names and contact details of two referees in the application.
If shortlisted, upload two reference letters and your undergraduate degree certificate to the online application system no later than seven working days before your interview.
If successful at interview, submit at least one unconditional UK university offer by 17:00 BST on 8 July 2027.
Apply for your own student visa; Chevening cannot apply on your behalf.
scholarships.duration: One-year master's degree in the UK
scholarships.application_period: Opened at 11:00 UTC on 4 August 2026 and closes at 11:00 UTC on 6 October 2026, for the 2027-28 Chevening Scholarship cycle. Studies begin in the UK in September/October 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are sifted against the eligibility criteria from October 2026, then independent reading committees assess all eligible applications from mid-October 2026 to January 2027. British embassies and high commissions produce shortlists and interview candidates in March to April 2027; results are announced from mid-June 2027. Applicants are assessed on leadership and influencing skills, the ability to build professional relationships to achieve positive outcomes, the reasons for the course and university choice (linked to UK priorities such as promoting growth and prosperity, building climate resilience, strengthening security and stability, and supporting development for more inclusive and effective societies), and a realistic short, mid and long-term career plan. Chevening states: 'The use of AI software to generate answers in Chevening applications is strictly prohibited.' The official page does not publish a separate SIDS selection weighting, so the SIDS element appears to be applied alongside the standard Chevening assessment.

scholarships.title: Chevening Europe Defence and Security Fellowship
scholarships.description: The Chevening Europe Defence and Security Fellowship, delivered by Cranfield University, is a six-week Chevening Fellowship for mid-career professionals who are citizens and residents of 35 listed European countries and who work in defence, security and related fields. The fellowship covers full programme fees, living expenses with pre-arranged accommodation close to Oxford, return economy airfare, a monthly personal living allowance and related allowances.
scholarships.deadline: Open for applications until 12 October 2026, at 11:00 (UTC)
scholarships.deadline_display: Open for applications until 12 October 2026, at 11:00 (UTC)
eligibility: In addition to meeting our standard eligibility criteria, you must be a citizen of and resident in one of the following countries at the point of application: Andorra, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Gibraltar, Greece, Holy See, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Monaco, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, San Marino, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, or Switzerland.
If you live in a European overseas territory, you may apply through the relevant Chevening award scheme for the European country of which you are a citizen.
Hold a postgraduate qualification (or equivalent professional training or experience in a relevant field).
Have at least five years' relevant professional experience.

Be a mid-career professional with responsibilities for national or international security, and employed within government, public or private sector, academia, defence, security, law enforcement, intelligence, civil protection, resilience, or an international organisation.
Be working in a role with the potential to influence organisational capability, policy, strategy, or operational effectiveness within their organisation and/or country.

Be able to demonstrate leadership potential and a commitment to applying the knowledge and networks gained through the fellowship within their organisation and/or country on completion of the programme.

General Chevening Fellowship criteria: be a citizen of a fellowship-eligible country or territory; demonstrate the potential to rise to a position of leadership and influence; demonstrate the personal, intellectual, and interpersonal attributes reflecting this potential; return to your country of citizenship (country of award) for at least one year after your fellowship ends; and meet all programme-specific fellowship eligibility requirements.

General work-experience rule for Chevening Fellowships: a minimum of five years' work experience in a relevant related field, which equals 7,200 hours, calculated by multiplying weeks worked by hours per week (a working week comprises 35-60 hours and a working year comprises 40-50 weeks). 'If you do not already have the level of work experience required for your chosen fellowship programme, you will be unable to submit your application.'
You do not need to meet the work experience requirement in one period of employment; applicants can submit up to fifteen different employment periods.
benefits: Full programme fees
Living expenses for the duration of the fellowship, including pre-arranged accommodation (the page states 'close to Oxford')
Return economy airfare
A monthly personal living allowance (stipend), confirmed in the Final Award Letter
Arrival allowance, paid on arrival in the UK
Departure allowance, where applicable to the fellowship type
A travel top-up allowance to attend events in London, for those in receipt of non-London stipends
A contribution of up to £75 for TB testing where this is required for the visa application
Reimbursement of the UK visa application fee for the fellow only
Reimbursement of the Immigration Health Surcharge, or a contribution towards travel insurance of up to £200

A research allowance as a contribution towards the cost of producing a thesis/dissertation where required for the course, or for conducting research associated with the programme, confirmed in the Final Award Letter
requirements: Meet the general Chevening Fellowship eligibility criteria and all programme-specific requirements.
Apply through the Chevening online application system reached from the relevant European country/territory page.
Demonstrate five years' (7,200 hours) of relevant professional experience, calculated automatically from the weeks and hours you enter.

Ensure the employing organisation will release you for the six-week programme: 'it is your responsibility to ensure that they will release you if you are selected for a Chevening Fellowship. The British embassy/high commission or the Chevening Secretariat cannot intervene in this.'
Secure and comply with the UK entry clearance (visa) requirements applicable to the fellowship, including medical clearance.
On return of the acceptance form, agree to abide by the Chevening Fellowship terms and conditions for the duration of the award.
scholarships.duration: Six weeks, in two cohorts: Cohort 1 25 January - 5 March 2027; Cohort 2 15 March - 23 April 2027
scholarships.application_period: Applications are open and close at 11:00 (UTC) on 12 October 2026. The programme itself runs in two cohorts in 2027: 25 January - 5 March 2027 and 15 March - 23 April 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: Chevening publishes the four general Fellowship objectives - supporting mid-career professionals in positions of leadership and influence, offering dynamic training/professional development/research relevant to professional interests and UK international strategic priorities, increasing the breadth and diversity of Chevening awards, and supporting FCDO foreign policy priorities by creating lasting relationships with future leaders, influencers and decision-makers. For this programme the assessment is against the general Chevening Fellowship criteria plus the published programme-specific requirements, and against the needs of a cohort drawn from the listed European countries. Chevening Fellowships are 'an important element of Britain's public diplomacy effort', and fellows are active in their field or subject. Chevening does not publish a separate scoring framework or interview format for this programme; applications for Chevening Scholarships follow the published sifting, reading committee, embassy shortlist and interview stages, while Chevening states that 'Application timelines for Chevening Fellowships vary.'

scholarships.title: Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation PhD Scholarship (2027 competition)
scholarships.description: This is not an award. It is an official swissuniversities information page that signposts to other funding opportunities. Its stated purpose: "swissuniversities occasionally receives information about various other funding opportunities from higher education institutions, research institutions or foundations abroad. Foreign higher education institutions often offer own scholarships for international students which are not announced worldwide. We therefore recommend advanced students, especially researchers, to contact the host university directly regarding financial aid." The page then lists, by country or region, links to external funding bodies, scholarship databases and search tools - including IEFA.org, Studyportals, GlobalScholarships.com, GOstralia!-GOmerica!, the Swiss Confederation's College of Europe scholarships, the Shanghai Municipal Government Scholarship for Foreign Students, the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme, the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, EURAXESS, the DAAD Stipendiendatenbank, UKCISA, the Berrow Foundation Scholarships at Lincoln College Oxford, and others - each with a stated 'Update' date. No award, amount, deadline, eligibility rule or application procedure is published on the page itself.
scholarships.deadline: November 6, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. ET (deadline to submit the complete application); October 2, 2026 (deadline to request eligibility confirmation); October 30, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET (deadline for receipt of all three references)
scholarships.deadline_display: November 6, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. ET (deadline to submit the complete application); October 2, 2026 (deadline to request eligibility confirmation); October 30, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET (deadline for receipt of all three references)
eligibility: At the time of application the applicant must be in the first year or the second year of a PhD program.
The field of study must be broadly related to the humanities or social sciences and address issues relevant to Canada's future.
The PhD research must align with at least one of the Foundation's four themes: Human Rights and Dignity; Responsible Citizenship; Canada and the World; People and their Natural Environment.

The applicant must be one of the following: a Canadian student enrolled at a Canadian university; a Canadian student enrolled at a university outside Canada; or an international student enrolled at a Canadian university.
Applicants must demonstrate outstanding academic achievement and a high level of intellectual ability, assessed across the whole application including transcripts and letters of recommendation.
Three letters of reference are required: one from the PhD supervisor, one from another academic referee, and one from a referee outside academia.
There is no age limit to apply.
There is no requirement to be fluent in both official languages; applicants must be able to communicate effectively in either French or English.
benefits: Annual stipend of up to $50,000 for three years to cover tuition and living expenses related to doctoral studies
Annual allowance of up to $20,000 for three years to support research, networking activities, and travel related to the doctoral work
Membership in the Foundation's community of Scholars, Fellows and Mentors
Lifelong membership in the Foundation's alumni network of more than 500 individuals
Mentorship and experiential learning: meetings, masterclasses, seminars and field experiences
requirements: Complete the eligibility screening form first; only applicants whose eligibility is confirmed gain access to the full application form
Applications that do not meet the eligibility criteria will not be reviewed
Provide exactly three letters of reference — thesis supervisor, another academic referee, and a non-academic referee — no more and no fewer
Reference letters must be attached within the application file; they cannot be sent directly to the Foundation
The application form must be filled out in one language only, either English or French
Attend the mandatory information sessions offered in the weeks of October 5 and October 12, 2026
Declare all additional sources of income each year, including other scholarships
scholarships.duration: Three-year program
scholarships.application_period: Applications open September 1, 2026 and close November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET. Two-step process: eligibility verification form must be submitted by October 2, 2026; references received by October 30, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET; mandatory information sessions in the weeks of October 5 and October 12, 2026.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are assessed on academic excellence, the clear alignment of the research project with the Foundation's mission and four founding themes, the rigour of the research proposal, and the ability to share knowledge for the benefit of society. Only applications meeting the programme's eligibility criteria are assessed. Applicants who pass review are notified by email; all other applicants are informed at the end of the application review period. Applicants shortlisted in the selection process are invited to group meetings and individual interviews, conducted in French or English depending on the applicant's preference. Final decisions are approved by the Board of Directors. The application form is removed from the portal once the competition ends; the confirmation email is the only proof of receipt.
