scholarships.title: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2027 - Research Students (Embassy Recommendation)
scholarships.description: The MEXT Scholarship research-student route funds postgraduate research study at a Japanese graduate school: it exempts tuition, pays a monthly scholarship of ¥143,000-¥145,000, and provides round-trip travel expenses (airfare). Recipients are selected by the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their country after sitting that mission's Japanese and English qualifying examinations, and are then placed at a graduate school. This record covers the Embassy Recommendation route for the 2027 cohort; the separate University Recommendation route is administered by individual Japanese universities.
scholarships.deadline: No central deadline is published. MEXT states that all procedures for the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarships are conducted through Japanese embassies, consulates in your countries, or institutions of higher education in Japan; candidates should contact the Japanese embassy (or consulate general) in their own country for the application date, and the Study in Japan page states that the type and field of application may vary from country to country and that applicants should check with the Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission for any openings.
scholarships.deadline_display: No central deadline is published. MEXT states that all procedures for the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarships are conducted through Japanese embassies, consulates in your countries, or institutions of higher education in Japan; candidates should contact the Japanese embassy (or consulate general) in their own country for the application date, and the Study in Japan page states that the type and field of application may vary from country to country and that applicants should check with the Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission for any openings.
eligibility: Research students: You must be under 35 years of age and be eligible for admission to a master's program or a doctoral program (first or second stage) at a Japanese graduate school.
Embassy Recommendation: scholarship recipients are recruited and initially screened by a Japanese embassy (or consulate general, depending on the country).

The type and field of application may vary from country to country. Please check with the Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission in your country to see if there are any openings in the type and field you wish to apply for.
All required documents and interviews will be conducted by the Japanese embassy or other diplomatic mission abroad in your country.
benefits: Preliminary training of Japanese etc. of 6 months for those who need this training, where offered by the institution
Placement into a Japanese graduate school at no application cost

scholarships.application_period: Applications for the 2027 cycle are handled at embassy/consulate level. MEXT lists the 2027 Embassy Recommendation Research Student recruitment under "募集中のプログラム" (programmes currently being recruited). No central opening or closing date is published; embassies set and publish their own deadlines and sit their own qualifying examinations.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applicants are recruited and initially screened by the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their country, which sits its own qualifying examinations (Japanese and English for research students), conducts the interview and collects all required documents; MEXT then selects the scholarship students and allocates them to host graduate schools, subject to the host university's acceptance.

scholarships.title: Young Leaders' Program (YLP) - Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship, GRIPS School of Government and School of Local Governance
scholarships.description: The Young Leaders Program (YLP) at GRIPS is a special one-year master's degree program in Public Policy, taught entirely in English, for exceptionally promising young government officials. It was introduced by the Japanese Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology in 2001 to foster future national leaders in designated countries, build comprehensive human networks among the leaders of nations, establish friendly relationships among the countries involved, and improve the quality of policymaking in the participating countries. scholarships.deadline: No central deadline is published. GRIPS publishes the application window as a historical reference only: application acceptance period (last year's result) July to October, with results announced the following April.
scholarships.deadline_display: No central deadline is published. GRIPS publishes the application window as a historical reference only: application acceptance period (last year's result) July to October, with results announced the following April.
eligibility: Young Leaders Program (YLP) students: You must be under 40 years of age (in principle), and university or college graduates who have practical work experience, young public administrators, etc. who are expected to play active role in Asia and other countries.

Study in Japan: 'Young Leaders Program (YLP) students' - Embassy recommendation: No; University recommendation: No. Recommendations come from official overseas recommending organizations (footnote 2).

GRIPS: 'Students will be admitted on the basis of an appraisal of their potential to become future leaders at home, to play important roles in their countries' development, and to maintain the lasting friendship and trust of Japan and other countries around the world.'
benefits: Monthly scholarship of ¥242,000
Tuition exempted
Round-trip travel expenses (airfare) provided

Candidates are recommended through official overseas recommending organizations; GRIPS publishes a country-by-country list of recommending authorities for the School of Government and the School of Local Governance.

scholarships.application_period: GRIPS publishes that for the cycle it runs, application acceptance runs July to October (last year's result), enrolment is in October and graduation the following September, with results announced the following April. GRIPS has published the YLP Brochure for 2027-2028. The nominating authority in the applicant's own country sets the operative date; no central deadline exists.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are handled at country level through the nominating authority, which is the institution listed for the applicant's country on the GRIPS page; MEXT's embassy/consulate route completes the scholarship process. GRIPS states admission is based on an appraisal of the applicant's potential to become a future leader at home, to play an important role in their country's development, and to maintain lasting friendship and trust between Japan and other countries. Selection method and review stages are not published on the pages read and are left unconfirmed.

scholarships.title: ICSSR Financial Assistance for Data Collection Abroad
scholarships.degree: Doctoral, Postdoctoral, Research (faculty and Ph.D/PDF scholars)
scholarships.description: The ICSSR provides financial assistance to Indian social science scholars who need to travel abroad for data collection or to consult archival material in connection with their research. It is aimed at scholars who proposed fieldwork abroad in their original approved ICSSR fellowship or project proposal and have made substantial progress, or at independent scholars for whom data collection abroad is academically justified and the research is at an advance stage. The total expenditure on the foreign visit, including economy class airfare, visa fee, travel insurance, local conveyance and maintenance, is supported within the prescribed norms of Government notifications.
scholarships.deadline: Applications are received online throughout the year.
scholarships.deadline_display: Applications are received online throughout the year.
eligibility: Serving Indian Faculty members in ICSSR research institute/ICSSR recognized institutes/institutions of national importance as defined by the Ministry of Education/university/deemed university/colleges recognized by the UGC and having 12b status with Ph.D degree are eligible to apply.
Ph.D/PDF Indian scholars are also eligible to apply.
benefits: The sanctioned maintenance amount is released before the commencement of the visit on submission of the copy of passport, visa procured, ticket and an undertaking.

Where the scholar receives air fare from any other source, 75 percent of the maintenance grant is given in advance and the remaining 25 percent after satisfactory submission of the relevant documents including the Statement of Expenditure.
requirements: Data collection abroad must have been proposed in the scholar's original approved ICSSR fellowship or project proposal, with substantial progress in the research, or be academically justified for research at an advance stage.
The visit must be realistic and not more than of two weeks duration.
After submitting the online application, a hard copy of the same along with all enclosures must be sent to the In-charge, IC Division, ICSSR, Aruna Asaf Ali Marg, New Delhi 110067.
Expenditure is reimbursed on submission of the statement of expenditure and the full documentary set; the ICSSR may ask for a copy of the tickets booked and the visa obtained before departure.
Where air fare is received from another source, only 75 percent of the maintenance grant is released in advance and the balance after the statement of expenditure is submitted.
ICSSR funding must be duly acknowledged in any publication (monograph or book) brought out from the material collected under the scheme, with a copy sent to ICSSR.
scholarships.duration: The visit under this Scheme should be realistic and not more than of two weeks duration
scholarships.application_period: Rolling - applications are received online throughout the year.
scholarships.selection_notes: Not published on the scheme page. The scheme page states the eligibility conditions and the objective of assisting scholars who have proposed fieldwork abroad in their original approved fellowship or project proposal and made substantial progress, or independent scholars whose research is at an advance stage; the evaluation and sanction procedure is not spelled out on the page and is listed under institution_check_required.
scholarships.program_type: Government research fieldwork grant
scholarships.name: ICSSR Financial Assistance for Data Collection Abroad

scholarships.title: University of Sharjah Research Assistant (RA) and Teaching Assistant (TA) Scholarship for Master's Students
scholarships.description: The University of Sharjah offers work-based Research Assistant and Teaching Assistant scholarships to eligible master's students, who must commit 20 hours per week at the University and may not be employed elsewhere during the scholarship period. The award is awarded by the concerned academic department based on its academic and research needs and available opportunities. The official page read does not publish the benefit amount, whether tuition is waived, or any list of expenses the scholarship covers, so this record is deliberately left unquantified rather than assumed to be full funding.
scholarships.deadline: Applications for Master's programs will be open from 5 October 2026 to 12 November 2026.
scholarships.deadline_display: Applications for Master's programs will be open from 5 October 2026 to 12 November 2026.
eligibility: Hold a Bachelor's degree with a minimum CGPA of 3.20 out of 4.00 (or equivalent) for UAE national students, and 3.60 out of 4.00 (or equivalent) for non-national students.
Be committed to working 20 hours per week at the University as part of the scholarship requirements.
Not be employed outside the University during the scholarship period.
Meet any additional requirements established by the concerned academic department and the University.

Regular master's admission also requires a bachelor's degree or equivalent from a university recognized by the UAE Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research (MoHESR), a minimum CGPA of 3.00 out of 4.00, and a bachelor's degree in a field relevant to the intended master's program.
requirements: Scholarship eligibility and continuation are subject to the bylaws and regulations of the University of Sharjah.
Remedial courses are not covered by the scholarship.
Meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not guarantee the award of a scholarship; selection is subject to departmental evaluation, availability, and approval.
The concerned academic department reserves the right to select eligible candidates based on its academic and research needs and the applicable selection criteria.
Applicants to Master's programs taught in English must obtain TOEFL iBT 79, TOEFL PBT 550, or IELTS Academic 6.0.
The University does not accept Home Edition or other online home-based English language proficiency examinations.
AED 500 non-refundable application fee.

Applicants nominated for admission must reserve their seat by paying AED 10,000 within the specified deadline; the amount paid is applied toward tuition fees upon enrollment, and on withdrawal or non-enrollment AED 5,000 is non-refundable.
scholarships.duration: Tied to enrolment in a full master's degree programme; continuation is subject to the bylaws and regulations of the University of Sharjah. No scholarship duration is published.
scholarships.application_period: Master's applications are open 5 October 2026 to 12 November 2026 for the published 2026/2027 intake. The University publishes no separate RA/TA scholarship application window; it states that meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not guarantee a scholarship and that selection is subject to departmental evaluation, availability and approval.
scholarships.selection_notes: The concerned academic department reserves the right to select eligible candidates based on its academic and research needs and the applicable selection criteria. Selection is subject to departmental evaluation, availability, and approval; meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not guarantee the award of a scholarship.
scholarships.program_type: University scholarship
scholarships.name: University of Sharjah Research Assistant (RA) and Teaching Assistant (TA) Scholarship for Master's Students

scholarships.title: Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) Program
scholarships.description: The Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) is a capacity building programme of the African Development Bank and the Government of Japan that offers high-achieving African students a two-year scholarship to pursue post-graduate study at master's level in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability and engineering. AfDB states it covers tuition for the 24-month study programme, a monthly living stipend, air travel between the scholar's home country and the host university at the start and end of the scholarship period, and health insurance usually obtained through the university, plus an additional six months for advance preparatory study or internships after graduation. It is not complete funding in AfDB's own terms: the Bank publishes an explicit exclusion list covering visa application costs, family members, extra-curricular courses, additional travel during the study programme, supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars, internships and educational equipment such as computers. AfDB publishes no stipend figure and no central call date, so the amount and the closing date must both be confirmed with the chosen partner university and the JADS Secretariat.
scholarships.deadline: The African Development Bank publishes no central JADS call opening or closing date, so there is no central deadline to quote. Applications go only through the partner universities, and the AfDB's own "List of Universities" page publishes each partner's intake and application window: Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University - "Application Deadlines are as following: April Enrollment: October / September Enrollment: April"; Hiroshima University Graduate School of Advanced Science and Engineering - "Month of Intake: April - Preliminary Survey: Oct 18-29 - Application period: Nov 8-19 - Exam. Period: Nov 29-Dec 8" and, for its second course, "Preliminary Evaluation for Apr. Oct 4-8, Preliminary Evaluation for Oct.: Mar. 7-11, Application Period for Apr.: Nov 4-15, Application Period for Oct.: Apr. 4-22"; The University of Tokyo Graduate School of Frontier Sciences - "Month of Intake: April or October / Examination: Schedule A (application period: mid June) Schedule B (application period: mid November)"; Sophia University - "Month of Intake: September / Deadline of Application: Web entry: Mid of March ~ Early April; Application: Mid of April". Kyoto University and Kogakuin University are listed with "Please refer to the program website".
scholarships.deadline_display: The African Development Bank publishes no central JADS call opening or closing date, so there is no central deadline to quote. Applications go only through the partner universities, and the AfDB's own "List of Universities" page publishes each partner's intake and application window: Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University - "Application Deadlines are as following: April Enrollment: October / September Enrollment: April"; Hiroshima University Graduate School of Advanced Science and Engineering - "Month of Intake: April - Preliminary Survey: Oct 18-29 - Application period: Nov 8-19 - Exam. Period: Nov 29-Dec 8" and, for its second course, "Preliminary Evaluation for Apr. Oct 4-8, Preliminary Evaluation for Oct.: Mar. 7-11, Application Period for Apr.: Nov 4-15, Application Period for Oct.: Apr. 4-22"; The University of Tokyo Graduate School of Frontier Sciences - "Month of Intake: April or October / Examination: Schedule A (application period: mid June) Schedule B (application period: mid November)"; Sophia University - "Month of Intake: September / Deadline of Application: Web entry: Mid of March ~ Early April; Application: Mid of April". Kyoto University and Kogakuin University are listed with "Please refer to the program website".
eligibility: Should have a minimum of a Bachelor's degree or its equivalent in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability, engineering studies or related areas; and have excellent academic records and relevant professional experience, and a history of supporting their countries' development efforts.

Applicants should have at least 1 year of paid employment in their home country or in other African countries after receiving their Bachelors (or equivalent university) degree within the past 3 years.
Candidates should be 35 years old or younger, and in good health.

Candidates should gain admission to an approved master's degree course at a Japanese or African partner university - application for admission to be done directly through the partner universities (Refer to list of universities and approved courses).
Candidates should not be enrolled in another graduate degree programs - the program does not support applicants who are already enrolled in graduate degree programs.
Must be a citizen of one of the African Development Bank's regional member countries.

Applicants must not be an Executive Director, his/her alternate, and/or staff of all types of appointments of the African Development Bank Group or a close relative of the aforementioned by blood or adoption with the term "close relative" defined as: Mother, Father, Sister, Half-sister, Brother, Half-brother, Son, Daughter, Aunt, Uncle, Niece, or Nephew.

Note published on the AfDB eligibility page: "All eligibility criteria are strictly adhered to unless otherwise communicated. Eligibility criteria will not change during an open call for applications. However, this information is subject to change between the close of one application process and the opening of the next."
benefits: Economy class air travel between a recipient's home country and the host university at the start of the study program and immediately following the end of the scholarship period
Tuition for a graduate program and the cost of basic medical insurance, usually obtained through the university
A monthly subsistence allowance to cover living expenses, including books
For scholars engaged in research, a special grant may be available for research and thesis preparation
In special circumstances, computer literacy, preparatory language and other similar courses may be covered under the scholarship
requirements: All applications should go through the partner universities, no separate application to the African Development Bank is necessary.
Only candidates who have been offered admission and endorsed by the university will be considered for the JADS Program.

Admission by the JADS partner university does not mean that you have been accepted for scholarship support; you should not take any action with respect to your current employment or otherwise, until you have been informed by the African Development Bank that you have been awarded the scholarship.
Request information and application forms and procedures from the chosen JADS partner university using the provided contacts.
The candidate completes and submits application for admission.
The university evaluates and selects applicants and gives them a provisional offer letter.

University sends list of selected candidates to the African Development Bank and the Bank further shares the list with the JADS Program Implementation Unit (PIU) to evaluate the applications based on a set criteria.
After the evaluation, the African Development Bank contacts the successful candidates and informs the universities.
Read information posted on the JADS website and review eligibility criteria carefully.

Begin gathering required documentation for the scholarship application, including: your current curriculum vitae, proof of employment for each record of employment since earning a Bachelor's degree, and certified copy of the certificate of your most advanced university degree earned.
Identify two professional references.
Prepare your research plan and proposal.
Take TOEFL iBT, TOEC test for English proficiency.
scholarships.duration: Two-year scholarship; "the scholarship only covers the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less"
scholarships.application_period: Annual partner-university admissions cycle. As published by AfDB on 2026-10-01, the next windows relative to that date are: Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University April-intake deadline in October 2026; Hiroshima University preliminary survey 18-29 October 2026 and application period 8-19 November 2026; Hiroshima University second course preliminary evaluation 4-8 October 2026; The University of Tokyo Schedule B application period in mid November 2026. AfDB states there is no separate application to the Bank and no central JADS window.
scholarships.selection_notes: All eligible applications are comparatively evaluated by the Program Implementation Unit hired by the African Development Bank, and the final selection is approved by the JADS Secretariat. Evaluation focuses on educational and professional excellence, commitment to home country development priorities, the quality of the statement of purpose, financial status and geographic diversity of awardees. The Bank's management decision and approval of the finalist also takes into consideration geographical diversity, gender balance, equity and inclusiveness (unusual circumstances or hardships when assessing employment experience), financial needs (applicants are financially constrained), and special consideration for applicants with special needs.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship (multilateral - African Development Bank and the Government of Japan)
scholarships.name: Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) Program

scholarships.title: Mandela Washington Fellowship for Young African Leaders (2027 Fellowship)
scholarships.degree: Non-degree (six-week executive-style exchange programme; no degree is awarded)
scholarships.description: The Mandela Washington Fellowship for Young African Leaders is the exchange component of the U.S. Government's Young African Leaders Initiative (YALI), a program of the U.S. Department of State with funding provided by the U.S. Government and administered by IREX. It brings up to 550 accomplished young African leaders to the United States for a comprehensive executive-style program: a six-week institute at a U.S. college or university combining academic coursework, professional site visits, structured networking, community service, and cultural activities in one of three tracks (Business and Trade, Emerging Technologies, or Governance and Security), plus an optional four-week Professional Development Experience for up to 50 Fellows and ongoing alumni opportunities.
scholarships.deadline: "APPLICATION DEADLINE: 16:00/4:00 PM GMT on Tuesday, October 13, 2026" and "The deadline for applications for the Mandela Washington Fellowship is 16:00/4:00 PM GMT on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. Applications must be submitted using the online application system at apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org." "There is no fee to apply for the Mandela Washington Fellowship."
scholarships.deadline_display: "APPLICATION DEADLINE: 16:00/4:00 PM GMT on Tuesday, October 13, 2026" and "The deadline for applications for the Mandela Washington Fellowship is 16:00/4:00 PM GMT on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. Applications must be submitted using the online application system at apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org." "There is no fee to apply for the Mandela Washington Fellowship."
eligibility: Are between the ages of 25 and 35 as of the application deadline (October 13, 2026), although exceptional applicants ages 21-24 may be considered
Are not U.S. citizens or permanent residents of the United States
Are eligible to receive a United States J-1 visa
Are not employees or immediate family members (spouses, parents, children, or siblings) of employees of the U.S. Government (including a U.S. embassy or consulate or other U.S. Government entity)
Are proficient in reading, writing, and speaking English (applicants who are deaf should refer to the English Language instructions in the application instructions)

Are citizens of one of the following countries: Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Cabo Verde, Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Republic of the Congo, Cote d'Ivoire, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Eritrea, Eswatini, Ethiopia, Gabon, The Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Niger, Nigeria, Rwanda, Sao Tome and Principe, Senegal, Seychelles, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Africa, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania, Togo, Uganda, Zambia, or Zimbabwe
Are residents of one of the above countries, and will be permanently residing there as of February 1, 2027, and at the beginning of the Fellowship in June 2027
Are not alumni or prior participants of the Mandela Washington Fellowship
benefits: There is no fee to apply for the Mandela Washington Fellowship
J-1 visa support

Round-trip travel from the Fellow's home city to the United States and domestic U.S. travel as required by the program. "Fellows must depart from their country of residence within an eligible Fellowship country in Africa to the United States"
A six-week institute
A limited accident and sickness benefit plan
Housing and meals during the program
An optional four-week Professional Development Experience (for up to 50 Fellows), which "will include support for housing, meals, and transportation for Fellows who are selected to participate"
Reasonable accommodations and support at no cost for Fellows with disabilities and chronic health conditions
requirements: Applications must be submitted using the online application system at apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org; "Applications and information submitted via email or other means will not be considered."
You must complete all fields marked with a red asterisk (*).
You must answer all application questions in English, and answers must reflect your own experiences and ideas.

You do not have to finish your application in one session. You may save your work and return as many times as necessary; however "Once you have submitted your application, however, you can no longer add any additional information or make any changes."
All answers in the application, including written responses to essays and optional PDE questions, must be your own original work, based on your own creativity and effort.

Your application will be disqualified if you copy language from other Fellowship applications (including those of other applicants or Fellowship alumni) or from other sources (including websites or blogs), as this is considered plagiarism.

Responsible use of technology is permitted with transparency: "If you use any technology (including AI) to help prepare your responses, you must disclose this where asked in the application, and you remain responsible for the content you submit."

In the online application system, after fully completing a section it will be marked as "Completed." When all required sections are marked as "Completed," click "Submit Application" at the bottom of the application dashboard; your application is not complete until you submit it.
If selected as a semi-finalist, you must provide a copy of your international passport (if available) or other government-issued photo identification at the interview.
If your technical eligibility for the Fellowship changes at any point, you must email MWFellowship@irex.org, as well as your local U.S. embassy or consulate, immediately.
The Fellowship Terms and Conditions require all Fellows to attend and fully participate in all required sessions and program activities scheduled by their institute.

All individuals who are selected for the Fellowship will be required to have a passport from an eligible Fellowship country that is valid through at least February 28, 2028, or through March 31, 2028, if selected for the Professional Development Experience.
scholarships.duration: "A six-week institute program" at a U.S. college or university, "from mid-June through early August 2027", plus an optional four-week Professional Development Experience, for a total of "approximately 10 weeks" for PDE Fellows
scholarships.application_period: Application opened 22 September 2026 and closes at 16:00/4:00 PM GMT on Tuesday 13 October 2026 for the 2027 Fellowship. Semi-finalists are interviewed by U.S. embassies and consulates from October 2026 to January 2027; applicants are notified of their status in February/March 2027; visa processing and pre-Fellowship activities for finalists run from March to May 2027; the Fellowship begins in the United States in June 2027, with institutes running from mid-June through early August 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: "The Fellowship selection process is a merit-based open competition." After the deadline, all eligible applications are reviewed and scored against the published criteria: proficiency speaking, reading and writing in English; a proven record of accomplishment in business, trade, emerging technologies, governance and/or security; a demonstrated and clear interest in building and maintaining partnerships with American organizations and businesses that advance shared goals; a commitment to return to Sub-Saharan Africa and contribute skills and talents; the ability to work cooperatively in groups and to respect others; strong social and communication skills; and demonstrated adaptability and the ability to lead effectively in varying and changing environments. Applicants who do not meet the technical eligibility requirements "will not be forwarded to the selection committee." Semi-finalists are then interviewed in person by the U.S. embassy or consulate in their home country between October 2026 and January 2027. Selected finalists must participate in mandatory Pre-Fellowship Orientation activities and a visa interview within Sub-Saharan Africa. The U.S. Department of State and IREX "reserve the right to verify all information included in the application", requiring documentation of age, citizenship and residency at the interview stage; any discrepancy or false information means "the application will be immediately declared invalid and the applicant ineligible." PDE applicants are assessed separately on the ability to work professionally in a U.S. organization, articulation of clear and specific learning goals, flexibility, alignment between professional background, institute track and potential U.S. organizations, interest in sustaining engagement with U.S. professionals, and strong English proficiency.

scholarships.title: African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS) Structured Master's Scholarship - January 2027 intake (South African applicants)

Applications run from 1 November 2026 to 30 April 2027 with a EUR 32 admission fee, and the standard length of study is tuition-free. The portal also advertises a separate national scholarship of EUR 5,000 per academic year for students in Slovakia.
scholarships.deadline: Apply the application for study 01.11.2026 - 30.04.2027
scholarships.deadline_display: Apply the application for study 01.11.2026 - 30.04.2027
eligibility: be a resident in Africa at the time of application*
be a citizen of any country in Africa

have completed a four-year undergraduate degree or a three-year undergraduate degree with an honours year by August (for the September intake) or December (for South African applicants in the January intake)
not have held a previous scholarship to study at an AIMS centre
benefits: Flights to and from South Africa
Airport transfers
Medical insurance
Tuition and research fees
Stipend of R2,200 per month
Accommodation on-site at AIMS (6 Melrose Road, Muizenberg)
Three meals a day at the AIMS canteen
requirements: Applications for the Structured Master's programme are completed online.
Choose the relevant stream: the Mathematical Sciences stream (apply.aims.ac.za) or the AI for Science stream (ai.aims.ac.za/apply).
Complete the online application form.
Upload your undergraduate and postgraduate transcripts, a CV, a cover letter and sample work.
Submit your application.
scholarships.duration: Structured Master's programme within AIMS's academic year, which "kicks off in September and runs through until the end of June"; the January intake begins in January and AIMS publishes no separate end date or programme length for it on this page
scholarships.application_period: Two published windows. September intake (African applicants): applications open January to March. January intake (South African applicants): applications open August to October of the preceding year. As at 2026-10-01 the only window still running is the January 2027 intake for South African applicants, open August to October 2026. The AI for Science stream is not part of this window because AIMS states: "For the AI for Science stream we only have the September intake with applications open from January to March."
scholarships.selection_notes: "Shortlisted candidates will be invited for an online interview before final selections are made." AIMS publishes no scoring criteria, no weighting, no shortlist size and no results date, so selection beyond the interview stage is not documented on its public pages.

scholarships.name: African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS) Structured Master's Scholarship - January 2027 intake (South African applicants)

scholarships.title: UNHCR Tertiary Refugee Scholarship Programme (DAFI) - Albert Einstein German Academic Refugee Initiative
scholarships.description: DAFI is UNHCR's dedicated tertiary scholarship programme for refugees and returnees, founded in 1992 and funded principally by the Government of Germany. The published scholarship package covers a range of costs including tuition and study materials, food, transportation and accommodation, and depending on the needs and capacity of the individual country operation or programme partner may also cover academic preparatory, language and ICT courses as well as psychosocial support. It funds ISCED 6 bachelor's or equivalent programmes and ISCED 5 short-cycle tertiary and TVET programmes of two years or more, and it explicitly does not cover master's studies. Applications are made through the DAFI Programme Management Platform, which was live and accepting registrations and submissions on 2026-10-01.
scholarships.deadline: No single global deadline is published. Deadlines are set per country operation and published on the UNHCR country help pages (published 2026/2027 examples: Rwanda 7 August 2026; Kyrgyzstan 21 August 2026; Slovakia 31 August 2026). Applicants must check their own country operation's call.
scholarships.deadline_display: No single global deadline is published. Deadlines are set per country operation and published on the UNHCR country help pages (published 2026/2027 examples: Rwanda 7 August 2026; Kyrgyzstan 21 August 2026; Slovakia 31 August 2026). Applicants must check their own country operation's call.
eligibility: UNHCR Tertiary Refugee Scholarship Programme (DAFI) offers qualified refugee and returnee (in selected countries*) students the possibility to earn an undergraduate degree in their country of asylum or home country

The applicant must be a recognized refugee or, where the country operation accepts them, an asylum seeker living in the country of asylum (published Rwanda wording: 'The applicant must be a recognized refugee or asylum seeker living in Rwanda')

Applicant should have been accepted to a university in the country of asylum; proof of admission must be submitted (published Rwanda wording: 'Applicant should have been accepted to a university in Rwanda. (You will have to submit proof of admission to a university.)')
Priority will be given to those who achieved excellent academic performance (published Rwanda wording)
Only one family member can apply/obtain DAFI scholarship to ensure that benefits allocated are equally given to other refugee students (published Rwanda wording)
Secondary selection criteria: female applicants and persons with special needs education are highly encouraged to apply (published Rwanda wording)
The DAFI Programme aims to provide equal opportunities for women and men (published Tajikistan wording)
benefits: The DAFI scholarship programme may also provide academic preparatory, language and information and communication technology (ICT) courses, as well as psychosocial support, depending on the needs and capacity of the individual country operation or programme partner
requirements: Apply through the DAFI Programme Management Platform at https://unhcr-dafi-tertiary.scholarshipsplatform.com/ - the platform instructs applicants to register an account, start the application (saved in-progress) and submit it for review
DAFI Scholarship programme application is free of charge

The final status of the application is notified by email from the DAFI platform (published Azerbaijan instructions wording: 'Submit your application for review and wait for notification from UNHCR about the final status of your application. The notification should come to your e-mail address from the DAFI platform.')
For any questions about the application process, contact the country office by email using the published country list, or your nearest UNHCR office or DAFI partner
scholarships.duration: Duration follows the degree programme enrolled in: ISCED 6 bachelor's or equivalent, or ISCED 5 short-cycle tertiary / TVET of two years or more
scholarships.application_period: Country-specific. The 2026/2027 cycle ran on country-published windows in July-August 2026 (Rwanda 15 July-7 August 2026; Kyrgyzstan 7 July-21 August 2026; Slovakia 1 July-31 August 2026). New country calls for the next cycle are announced on the relevant UNHCR country help page and applications are submitted through the DAFI Programme Management Platform.
scholarships.selection_notes: The published Rwanda call states that priority will be given to applicants who achieved excellent academic performance, that only one family member may hold a DAFI scholarship, and that female applicants and persons with special needs education are highly encouraged to apply. It also states that only qualified candidates duly registered with UNHCR are invited to interviews, that names of shortlisted candidates are posted at the respective offices, and that academic documents are verified with the relevant authorities (the last two statements are published in the Windle International Kenya DAFI scholarship instructions, not on the UNHCR Rwanda call). The UNHCR programme page states that UNHCR and its education partners closely monitor scholars' academic progress and well-being through regular engagement with students and their institutions.
scholarships.program_type: UN agency scholarship
scholarships.name: UNHCR Tertiary Refugee Scholarship Programme (DAFI) - Albert Einstein German Academic Refugee Initiative

scholarships.title: Postgraduate Sanctuary Scholarship - University of Westminster
scholarships.description: The University of Westminster offers two Postgraduate Sanctuary Scholarships to students who are seeking asylum in the United Kingdom. Each covers full tuition costs for a full-time master's course starting January 2027, plus a maintenance grant of £1,000 per month for up to 12 months, published on the University's central scholarship listing as 'Full tuition fee plus up to £12,000'. Applications are made by returning the completed application form with required evidence as PDF attachments to scholarships@westminster.ac.uk by 5pm on Monday 2 November 2026.
scholarships.deadline: Monday 02 November 2026 5pm.
scholarships.deadline_display: Monday 02 November 2026 5pm.
eligibility: You must have an offer from the University of Westminster for a place on a full-time master's course starting in January 2027
You must be resident in the UK

You must hold one of the following eligible immigration statuses before submitting your application: UK asylum seeker; UK discretionary leave to remain (as a result of an asylum application); UK limited leave to remain (as a result of an asylum application)

scholarships.title: University of Glasgow Sanctuary Scholarship
scholarships.description: The Staff Exchanges action of the Marie Sklodowska-Curie Actions "funds short-term international and inter-sectoral exchanges of staff members involved in research and innovation activities of participating organisations", with the aim of developing "sustainable collaborative projects between different organisations from the academic and non-academic sectors (in particular SMEs), based in Europe and beyond." Exchanged staff benefit from new knowledge, skills and career development perspectives while participating organisations increase their research and innovation capacities. Grants are awarded to international consortia, not to individuals: a consortium "needs to include at least three organisations in three different countries, two of which need to be located in a different EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country", must include both academic and non-academic sectors, and "participation of organisations from non-associated third countries is strongly encouraged". Projects can last up to four years and fund secondments of one month to one year. Seconded staff receive "a top-up allowance (for travel, accommodation, subsistence costs), which is on top of the salary paid by their organisation", plus a special needs allowance where applicable, alongside funding for research, training and networking activities and for management and indirect costs. The current call is closed; the 2027 call opens on 15 December 2026.

scholarships.title: Ernst Mach Grant – worldwide
scholarships.description: The Ernst Mach Grant – worldwide finances short research stays in Austria for young researchers from all disciplines and all countries except Austria. The published grant benefit is a supplementary monthly grant of EUR 1,300, together with assistance in arranging accommodation and health insurance, but scholarship holders pay the costs of accommodation and insurance themselves and must show own funds. Tuition fees at Austrian public universities and universities of applied sciences do not have to be paid by grant holders, and may be waived upon request to the rectorate, but this does not apply to private universities and private colleges. Holders from listed non-European developing countries also receive a travel costs subsidy of up to EUR 1,200 upon submission of original travel invoices.
scholarships.deadline: Closing date for applications: 01.12.2026. Online application is possible from September to December 1st; the application deadline for this grant is December 1st, 2026, 23:59 (CET) for all applications for stays during the academic year 2027/28.
scholarships.deadline_display: Closing date for applications: 01.12.2026. Online application is possible from September to December 1st; the application deadline for this grant is December 1st, 2026, 23:59 (CET) for all applications for stays during the academic year 2027/28.
eligibility: Eligible for application are: a. Postgraduates pursuing a doctoral/PhD programme outside of Austria; b. Postgraduates and postdocs wishing to pursue research in Austria with a view to an academic career and who completed their studies (at a university outside of Austria) after 30 September 2025; c. Postdocs who are working as researchers at a university outside of Austria
Applicants must not have lived/studied/pursued research/pursued academic work in Austria in the last six months before taking up the grant
Applicants who have completed their academic education mainly in Austria (does not apply to applications by Postdocs) or who are already permanently residing in Austria are not eligible to apply
Maximum age: 35 years (born on or after 01 October 1991)
Country of origin: all except Austria
Language skills: very good knowledge of English and/or German
Consent of a lecturer at the Austrian target university to supervise the applicant academically is a required document
The scholarship will only be granted for projects that can be completed within the scholarship period (max. 9 months)
benefits: Assistance in arranging accommodation (OeAD student housing may be applied for; availability is limited and a room cannot be guaranteed)
The OeAD can help with taking out health insurance accepted by the Austrian authorities
requirements: The documents have to be uploaded with the online application at www.scholarships.at
The use of generative AI must be indicated in the application
Applicants who seek admission to a university in Austria have to contact the institution of their choice directly
Grant holders must be continuously present at their place of study in Austria to study or conduct their research project

Scholarship holders are not allowed to engage in gainful employment. Exempt is marginal employment within research/the Arts at universities, universities of applied sciences and research institutions in compliance with residence laws and employment laws for foreign nationals (in 2026: 551.10 Euro per month)
The grant has to be consumed by the end of 2028
Scholarship holders are obliged to submit a final report at the end of their scholarship stay
It is strongly recommended that you take out adequate health, accident and repatriation insurance valid at your destination; the scholarship holder is responsible for taking out insurance
scholarships.duration: 1 to 9 months
scholarships.application_period: Online application open from September 2026 and closing 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET, for research stays during the Austrian academic year 2027/28 (starting September 2027). Expert evaluation takes place after the deadline; results are expected to be published at the beginning of July 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: The selection follows a multistage process: 1. Examination of the formal requirements; 2. Examination of the application's general plausibility; 3. Assessment and evaluation of the application by experts; 4. Final decision by the BMFWF. Incomplete applications and applications not complying with the application criteria will not be accepted for the further selection process. All formally valid applications are then evaluated by experts from the respective field and the selection committee awards the best applicants. The selection is competitive, i.e. there is no legal claim to a grant even if all application requirements are fulfilled; the number of grants awarded during one call depends on the quota and/or the available budget.

scholarships.title: Programa Portugal-Berkeley (Visiting Student Researchers at UC Berkeley)
scholarships.description: The Programa Portugal-Berkeley is an FCT call, run with FLAD and UC Berkeley, that supports doctoral students to spend a research stay as Visiting Student Researchers at UC Berkeley for up to six months. FCT launches the call to promote the internationalisation of Portuguese science and to foster research exchange between Portuguese universities and UC Berkeley in areas of mutual scientific interest. The selected candidate's home institution (CPS) is responsible for the administrative procedures to acquire the Visiting Student Researcher status and pays the University Services Fee, the DS-2019 visa processing fee and the Institute of European Studies administrative fees at UC Berkeley. The selected candidate must arrange and financially cover their own travel, accommodation and health insurance, and the call publishes no direct stipend or award figure.
scholarships.deadline: Applications are accepted on a continuous basis until 17:00 on 30 December 2027 (Portuguese Continental time), or until the maximum number of Visiting Student Researchers planned for each calendar year has been selected, whichever occurs first
scholarships.deadline_display: Applications are accepted on a continuous basis until 17:00 on 30 December 2027 (Portuguese Continental time), or until the maximum number of Visiting Student Researchers planned for each calendar year has been selected, whichever occurs first
eligibility: PhD candidates enrolled in Portuguese higher education institutions
Any scientific area
Candidates must identify and obtain the agreement of a UC Berkeley professor who can act as supervisor during the stay in UC Berkeley, before submitting the application
Applications must be submitted in English
benefits: Research stay of up to 6 months at UC Berkeley as a Visiting Student Researcher
Administrative handling of the Visiting Student Researcher status by the home institution (CPS)
Up to 8 candidates selected per year
requirements: Application submitted in English through the dedicated online form linked on the call page

Applications accepted on a continuous basis until 30 December 2027 at 17:00 (Portugal Continental time) or until the annual maximum number of Visiting Student Researchers is selected, whichever comes first
Prior identification and agreement of a UC Berkeley professor to act as supervisor
The candidate must indicate the expected arrival date, taking into account that arrival cannot occur before six months have elapsed since selection for the programme
For more information, consult the expression-of-interest call published with this initiative
scholarships.duration: Research stay of up to 6 months at UC Berkeley; arrival cannot occur earlier than six months after selection
scholarships.application_period: Opened 01 January 2026 at 09:00; closes 30 December 2027 at 17:00, or earlier once the annual quota of selected Visiting Student Researchers is filled. Assessment runs in quarterly windows, grouped by submission date (first window: applications received up to 31/03/2026; second window starting 30/06/2026; and so on until the call closes).
scholarships.selection_notes: Assessment is carried out by an academic committee appointed by FCT and FLAD. Criterion A: candidate's curriculum, considering academic grades, track record and scientific achievements including peer-reviewed publications, scholarships, prizes, conferences and project participation (40%). Criterion B: scientific quality, innovative character of the work plan and feasibility of the research activities to be developed (30%). Criterion C: motivation letter explaining the relevance of the stay and the work to be developed for the scientific ambition of the doctoral work plan, and the expected impact of the stay on the candidate's career (30%). Selection is based on the analysis of these criteria, producing a positive or negative opinion, with final classification CF = 0.4 A + 0.3 B + 0.3 C.

scholarships.title: Programa RESTART — 4ª Edição (FCT research funding after parental leave)
scholarships.description: RESTART is an FCT funding instrument that competitively finances individual R&D projects in all scientific domains for researchers who have recently taken a parental leave, including adoption leave. The award is a project grant of up to EUR 50,000 per project for a maximum of 18 months, drawn from a total budget allocation of EUR 1.6 million, and it is held by the beneficiary R&D unit rather than paid as a personal living stipend. Candidates must hold a doctorate, be an integrated doctoral member of an R&D unit or hold a contract with a State laboratory, and have taken a parental leave of at least 120 days (or at least 72 days in a shared leave, whether exclusive or shared) between 3 June 2025 and 1 October 2026 inclusive.

scholarships.deadline_display: Applications open 01 October 2026 at 14h and close 13 November 2026 at 17h (Portuguese time)

Be an integrated doctoral member of an R&D unit, or hold a contractual link with a State laboratory

Have benefited from a parental leave, including for adoption, of a duration equal to or greater than 120 days between 3 June 2025 and 1 October 2026 inclusive; in the case of a shared parental leave, including for adoption, the candidate must demonstrate having taken, exclusively or shared, at least 72 days of leave
The minimum number of days required (120 or 72) must be reached between 3 June 2025 and 1 October 2026 inclusive, regardless of the start or end date of the leave
Applications must be submitted with the commitment of the host institution

Researchers holding a scholarship contract may submit as proof of parental leave the statement of suspension of research activities funded by that scholarship, issued by the contracting institution, for an equivalent period; for FCT scholarships this may be replaced by simply indicating the relevant scholarship reference
Eligible applicants are national, foreign and stateless researchers

Gender and opportunity equality objective of the programme
Alignment with European Council and OECD recommendations on reconciling professional and family life for those working in R&D

Multiple applications sharing all or part of the work plan are not admitted, either within this notice or in different notices with overlapping application periods; in the case of multiple applications to different thematic notices with different application periods, a funding recommendation in one is a condition for exclusion from the others
scholarships.duration: Maximum 18 months of project development

scholarships.selection_notes: The RESTART programme's evaluation criteria are: i) scientific quality, innovative character and feasibility of the proposed research plan; ii) merit of the candidate and fit of their profile with the research plan; and iii) impact of the project's execution on the development of the researcher's career.

scholarships.title: CLP Future Conservationist Awards 2027
scholarships.degree: Not applicable - professional project grant, no degree awarded
scholarships.description: Annual CLP Future Conservationist Awards offer early-career conservationists a project grant of up to $15,000 as well as ongoing support through CLP's global Alumni Network, including funding, training and mentorship. For 2027 the process runs in two stages: a concept note first, then a full application from shortlisted concepts only.
scholarships.deadline: Stage 1 concept notes must be submitted by Friday, October 30, 2026 (23:59 GMT). Late, incomplete or ineligible submissions will not be considered.
scholarships.deadline_display: Stage 1 concept notes must be submitted by Friday, October 30, 2026 (23:59 GMT). Late, incomplete or ineligible submissions will not be considered.
eligibility: Proposed projects must deliver effective conservation interventions for globally important, at-risk habitats and species through both ecological research and conservation action

Projects must fall within one of these themes: a) climate impact and adaptation, b) biodiversity conservation, c) habitat restoration and/or management, d) social development and wellbeing, e) Indigenous community participation and/or community-led conservation, f) environmental policy, g) human-wildlife conflict, or h) environmental education and citizen science

'At-risk' species are those categorised by the IUCN Red List as globally threatened (Critically Endangered, Endangered, Vulnerable) or Data Deficient, or where there is information indicating the need for urgent local conservation action
All team members must be early in their careers (i.e. have no more than five years of professional conservation experience)
Project teams must include at least three people and explain how each team member will develop their capacity through the project
All team members must be nationals of the country in which the project will take place, although one team member can be a non-national if this is clearly justified
Projects must take place in an eligible country (see guidelines)
Project duration must be between six and 12 months
Proposed projects must go beyond academic research and this must be demonstrated in the application
The total funding request from CLP must not exceed US$15,000
CLP funding must cover at least 50% of the project budget

Ongoing support through CLP's global Alumni Network, including funding, training and mentorship

Follow the published guidelines on completing the concept note template, including the eligibility criteria
Meet all published eligibility criteria on the award page
Demonstrate that the project goes beyond academic research
Explain how each team member will develop their capacity through the project
Show that the total CLP request does not exceed US$15,000 and that CLP funding covers at least 50% of the project budget

scholarships.application_period: Stage 1: concept notes due 30 October 2026, 23:59 GMT. scholarships.selection_notes: Two-stage selection. Stage 1 concept notes are assessed against the published eligibility criteria and the eight eligible themes; only the highest-scoring (shortlisted) concept note applicants are notified and invited to submit a full application through the online portal. scholarships.title: Rufford Small Grants Programme
scholarships.description: The Rufford Small Grants Programme funds fieldwork costs for small-scale, pilot nature conservation projects run by early-career conservationists in developing and emerging economy countries. Funding is staged across four levels - 1st Rufford Small Grant up to GBP 7,000, 2nd Rufford Small Grant up to GBP 8,000, Booster Grant up to GBP 12,000 and Completion Grant up to GBP 18,000 - and the Foundation aims to provide between 50% and 100% of project costs, requiring evidence of co-funding where it is not the only funder. Only fieldwork costs are considered, and award holders must provide project updates and a final report that are posted on their Rufford webpage. There are no deadlines, so the programme was open on the verification date.
scholarships.deadline: There are no deadlines - applications can be submitted at any time of year. You can only make one funding application in any 12-month period; if an application is rejected you must wait 12 months before you can reapply; if you are funded you cannot apply for further support for at least 12 months.
scholarships.deadline_display: There are no deadlines - applications can be submitted at any time of year. You can only make one funding application in any 12-month period; if an application is rejected you must wait 12 months before you can reapply; if you are funded you cannot apply for further support for at least 12 months.
eligibility: Applicants should be in the early stages of their conservation careers; priority is given to those undertaking an MSc or PhD (or equivalent) or who graduated from such studies in the past 3 years
We do not fund undergraduate students studying for a BSc or equivalent
Projects must have a nature conservation focus
Applicants must be working in an eligible country
We support small-scale or pilot projects
Ideally the Foundation should provide between 50 and 100% of the costs of the project; where The Rufford Foundation is not the only funder, evidence of co-funding is required
Only fieldwork costs will be considered

For species-focused projects, the species must not be listed as Least Concern at a global level in the IUCN Red List; species not on the list because they have not been assessed but thought to be globally threatened are also considered
Projects can focus on particular species, threatened habitats, or issues such as human-wildlife conflict or community education
benefits: Staged funding pathway: 1st Rufford Small Grant, 2nd Rufford Small Grant, Booster Grant, Completion Grant
Project updates and a final report are published on the recipient's Rufford webpage
Access to a global network of Rufford grantees and conferences
requirements: Be in the early stages of a conservation career (current MSc or PhD student, or graduated from such studies in the past 3 years)
Have a project with a nature conservation focus
Be working in an eligible country
Submit a small-scale or pilot project proposal
Claim fieldwork costs only
Provide evidence of co-funding where The Rufford Foundation is not the only funder
For species projects, show that the species is not globally Least Concern
Make only one funding application in any 12-month period
scholarships.duration: Most projects last 12-18 months
scholarships.application_period: Rolling. Applications can be submitted at any time of year, with no published closing date. One application per 12-month period per applicant.
scholarships.selection_notes: The published criteria are the general criteria and general exclusions, project focus rules (including the IUCN Red List rule for species projects), the country eligibility list and the staged progression rules. The specific scoring method and decision process are not published on the pages read. Selection is effectively gated by the staged pathway: each further stage requires completion of the previous project, its updates and final report, and a minimum 12-month gap after payment, and for Booster and Completion Grants evidence of co-funding or sustainability planning.

scholarships.name: Rufford Small Grants Programme

scholarships.title: Whitley Awards 2027
scholarships.degree: Not applicable - professional project award, no degree awarded
scholarships.description: Awarded annually, Whitley Awards recognise grassroots conservation leaders, providing funding to support and scale up proven, science-based solutions that deliver lasting impact for both people and nature. Winning a Whitley Award can be a transformative moment in a conservation leader's career, bringing international recognition, communications and media support, and entry to a global community of more than 230 conservation leaders across over 80 countries.
scholarships.deadline: Applications for the 2027 Whitley Awards are now open and will close at 23:59 GMT on Friday, 30 October 2026.
scholarships.deadline_display: Applications for the 2027 Whitley Awards are now open and will close at 23:59 GMT on Friday, 30 October 2026.

Work based in at least one eligible country - countries not classified as a High-Income Economy by the World Bank, with some exceptions based on WFN's funding history; the full list of eligible countries is published by WFN

Wildlife conservation projects delivering measurable positive impacts for threatened ecosystems and biodiversity at the landscape or seascape level, while providing tangible benefits to Indigenous peoples and local communities
Applicants who work for a locally incorporated NGO, charity, not for profit, or university
Strong communicators who inspire others and collaborate effectively and share their learnings and results

Community-led conservation projects are encouraged, and all projects must demonstrate how they empower, engage and benefit the Indigenous peoples and communities with which they work
Grassroots, pragmatic conservation work that is realistic but ambitious, replicable or scalable
Actions that will have clear, measurable outcomes, with careful consideration of the indicators used to evidence impact
Sustainable projects that will continue well beyond the Whitley Award, demonstrating long-term planning
Projects that demonstrate value for money and an ability to manage funding at the Whitley Award level (GBP 50,000)
Projects for which a Whitley Award will make a significant difference; priority to applicants who can clearly demonstrate need
Work that would benefit from greater visibility, particularly projects that could gain momentum through media exposure and wider recognition
No invitation or nomination is needed to apply
benefits: GBP 50,000 in project funding over one year
International recognition and profile-raising opportunities
Professional communications and media support
Peer learning, training and collaboration opportunities
Eligibility for future Continuation Funding and the Whitley Gold Award
Membership of a global community of more than 230 conservation leaders working across over 80 countries

Be embedded in local communities and be backed by an experienced team or organisation demonstrating past success and an evidence-based approach
Work for a locally incorporated NGO, charity, not for profit, or university

Deliver a wildlife conservation project with measurable positive impacts for threatened ecosystems and biodiversity at the landscape or seascape level, with tangible benefits for Indigenous peoples and local communities
Be based in at least one eligible country (not a World Bank High-Income Economy, with WFN exceptions)

Register for a WFN account on the online application portal and complete the application form online

Download and use the current-year Microsoft Word template for the logical framework/timeline and the current-year Microsoft Excel template for the budget, then upload the completed versions to the portal
Nominate three referees and ensure they submit their references by the closing deadline
scholarships.duration: Each Whitley Award is worth GBP 50,000 in project funding over one year. Winners are announced at the annual Whitley Awards Ceremony in London in Spring 2027.
scholarships.application_period: Applications for the 2027 Whitley Awards are open and close at 23:59 GMT on Friday, 30 October 2026. Registered applicants can log in to the WFN application portal and complete the form at any time before the deadline. Winners will be announced during the annual Whitley Awards Ceremony in London in Spring 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: WFN publishes what it looks for rather than a scoring formula: strong communicators who collaborate and share learning; leadership and teamwork backed by an experienced organisation with an evidence-based approach; ecosystem-level projects (genuine flagship species projects accepted but not if results are purely species-specific); community-led projects that empower, engage and benefit Indigenous peoples and communities; pragmatic work that is realistic but ambitious and replicable or scalable; clear measurable outcomes with considered indicators; sustainability beyond the award with long-term planning; value for money and ability to manage GBP 50,000 of funding; a project to which the award will make a significant difference, with priority to demonstrated need; and work that would benefit from greater visibility. Practical process gates: three referees must be nominated and must submit their references by the deadline (the applicant's responsibility), and applications on out-of-date templates from previous years will not be considered. Winners are announced at the Whitley Awards Ceremony in London in Spring 2027.

Selected participants complete training modules on TEFConnect, submit a business plan, financial projection and pitch video, and then provide business registration, tax and banking documents before the seed capital is paid into their business account. Applications from applicants who have never benefitted from any of our previous programmes
Applications from applicants who have not previously applied in the same application window of the same year

scholarships.title: Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS)
scholarships.description: The DAAD EPOS programme funds individual scholarships for graduates from developing and newly industrialised countries to take a development-oriented postgraduate (mostly Master's) course at a state or state-recognised German university, and in exceptional cases a doctoral degree. The award is a monthly payment of EUR 992 for graduates or EUR 1,300 for doctoral candidates (EUR 1,400 from February 2026), plus payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance and a flat-rate travel allowance. Under certain circumstances scholarship holders may additionally receive a monthly rent subsidy and a monthly allowance for accompanying family members. Scholarships are awarded subject to funding being provided by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).
scholarships.deadline: Depending on chosen study programme; please check the DAAD list of application deadlines or the website of the chosen study programme. Applications are sent directly to the course, not to the DAAD.
scholarships.deadline_display: Depending on chosen study programme; please check the DAAD list of application deadlines or the website of the chosen study programme. Applications are sent directly to the course, not to the DAAD.

Bachelor degree (usually a four-year course) in an appropriate subject
Academic degree completed with far above average results (upper third)
At least two years of related professional experience after the first degree (bachelor) at the time of application
Academic degrees should normally not be more than six years old
Applicants who have been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline cannot be considered

Working context is normally a public authority or a state or private company in a developing country, in planning and executing directives and projects with development-policy emphasis in technological, economic or social areas
Proof of development-related motivation and an expectation of taking on social responsibility and initiating and supporting processes of change after the scholarship

The complete applications have to be submitted in English or German to be considered
Incomplete applications cannot be considered

If the motivation letter does not explain the specific courses and priority order, the application cannot be considered or an already awarded scholarship may be withdrawn
Applicants from the People's Republic of China are asked to submit an APS Certificate with their application documents

scholarships.application_period: Cycle-based: applicants apply directly to a listed EPOS postgraduate course for the published intake year (the current DAAD programme list is headed 'List of Application Deadlines for Intake 2027/2028'); the course's own committee then nominates candidates, who are invited to upload to the DAAD portal for the final selection.
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection is by independent, voluntary selection committees. It supports project-based research in all scientific domains and disciplines, giving full place to fundamental, exploratory or finalised research in an approach guided by researchers' curiosity, and mobilises five funding instruments from single-team to international collaboration.
