scholarships.title: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Standard Program)
scholarships.description: JSPS funds postdoctoral researchers from overseas to conduct collaborative research in Japan under the guidance of a Japanese host researcher at a university or other eligible research institution. Financial support is a maintenance allowance of JPY362,000 per month, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance of JPY200,000, and overseas travel insurance. A Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research for JSPS Research Fellows can also be applied for through the host institution to cover cooperative research-related expenses. Because this is a research appointment rather than a degree programme, there is no tuition to pay and the award is not presented as tuition funding.
scholarships.deadline: FY2027 2nd recruitment: April 23, 2027, 5 p.m. JST, submission from the Japanese host institution to JSPS. FY2027 1st recruitment closed on August 28, 2026.
scholarships.deadline_display: FY2027 2nd recruitment: April 23, 2027, 5 p.m. JST, submission from the Japanese host institution to JSPS. FY2027 1st recruitment closed on August 28, 2026.
eligibility: Be a citizen of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan (JSPS treats Taiwanese and Palestinian researchers in this manner)

As of April 1 of the fiscal year, have obtained a doctoral degree within six years of the date the fellowship goes into effect (on or after April 2, six years prior to the fiscal year), or who are expected to receive a Ph.D. by the start date of the fellowship period
Whether or not the candidate is employed in a full-time position is not considered
Researchers who obtained their PhD within six years minus time taken for maternity and/or parental leave (every four weeks of leave counted as one month)

Those who have previously been awarded and started a fellowship under the JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship Program for Research in Japan (Standard, and Pathway to University positions in Japan) are not eligible
Japanese citizens and foreigners with permanent residence status in Japan are not eligible
A selected fellow must submit an original copy of the doctoral degree certificate or diploma before the fellowship starting date
Host researcher must be a full-time researcher at a KAKENHI-eligible institution, eligible to apply for a KAKENHI grant, and each host researcher can submit up to three applications
benefits: Settling-in allowance and outbound airfare are not paid to a candidate who has been living in Japan with a mailing address before the fellowship start date
Fellows may spend part of the tenure at another research institution, including one located overseas, when recognised as necessary to advance their research
requirements: Applications must be submitted to JSPS by a host researcher in Japan via the head of their university or institution
Submit the application form using the JSPS Electronic Application System by the deadline designated by the host institution
The JSPS Electronic Application System becomes available approximately two months before the JSPS application period
The host institution must verify that the application is approved by the head of the institution and that the stated requirements will be carried out if approved
scholarships.duration: 12 to 24 months
scholarships.application_period: Two open calls per year. FY2027 1st: application deadline August 28, 2026 (5 p.m. JST), results late December 2026, arrival windows April 1 - September 30, 2027, 120 fellowships. FY2027 2nd: application deadline April 23, 2027 (5 p.m. JST), results early August 2027, arrival windows September 1 - November 30, 2027, 120 fellowships.
scholarships.selection_notes:
Document review by six examiners using a graduated 1 to 5 scale, followed by a panel review conducted by the JSPS International Program Committee
Marks are made on a comprehensive basis taking into account research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity, future potential of the research, and establishment of new research networks
That the applicant and candidate have established contact in advance and created a concrete research plan
That the applicant's institution has established a suitable place for the candidate to work and stay
That unbalance is avoided in the selectees' nationalities, host institutions and areas of specialization, allowing people from a wide diversity of countries to come to Japan
scholarships.program_type: Government research fellowship
scholarships.image_alt_text: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science
scholarships.name: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Standard Program)

scholarships.title: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Short-term Program for North American and European Researchers, PE)
scholarships.description: This programme brings PhD students and PhD researchers from North America and Europe to Japan to conduct collaborative research under the guidance of a Japanese host for between one and twelve months. Financial support is a maintenance allowance of JPY362,000 per month for PhD holders or JPY200,000 per month for non-PhD holders at the start of the research in Japan, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance of JPY200,000 for fellows with three or more months of tenure, and overseas travel insurance. A research support allowance for cooperative research-related expenses is applied for by the host researcher. The award is a research fellowship, not a degree scholarship, so no tuition is funded.
scholarships.deadline: FY2027 2nd recruitment: January 8, 2027, 5 p.m. JST, submission from the Japanese host institution to JSPS. FY2027 3rd recruitment: June 4, 2027, 5 p.m. JST. The FY2027 1st recruitment closed on September 25, 2026.
scholarships.deadline_display: FY2027 2nd recruitment: January 8, 2027, 5 p.m. JST, submission from the Japanese host institution to JSPS. FY2027 3rd recruitment: June 4, 2027, 5 p.m. JST. The FY2027 1st recruitment closed on September 25, 2026.
eligibility: Be a citizen or permanent resident of an eligible country, or have been engaged in research continuously for at least three years at a university or research institution in an eligible country (eligible countries: US, Canada, EU countries, UK, Switzerland, Norway and Russia); Taiwan and Palestine are also treated as eligible

Have obtained a doctoral degree from a foreign graduate school and, as of April 1 of the fiscal year, be within six years of having obtained that degree, or be currently enrolled in a doctoral course at a foreign graduate school and expect to receive a Ph.D. within two years from the start date of the fellowship period
Whether or not the candidate is employed in a full-time position is not considered

Researchers who have continuously carried out research for three or more years, or obtained their PhD within six years, minus time taken for maternity and/or parental leave (every four weeks counted as one month)
A person who has never engaged in research at universities etc. in Japan would be most preferable

Those who have previously been awarded and started a fellowship under the JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Standard (P), Short-term (PE), Short-term (PA), or Pathway to University positions in Japan (PU)) are not eligible
Those who have resident cards with mailing addresses in Japan at the application deadline set by JSPS are not eligible
A Japanese citizen who is also a permanent resident of an eligible country is not eligible
A selected fellow needs to submit an original copy of the doctoral degree certificate or diploma, or the prospect certificate if the degree is not yet obtained, before the fellowship starting date
The host researcher must be a full-time researcher at a KAKENHI-eligible institution and may submit up to three applications
benefits: The settling-in allowance applies only to fellows with three or more months of tenure
Airfare outbound and the settling-in allowance are not paid to a candidate who has been living in Japan with a mailing address before the fellowship start date
Three application periods a year give flexibility in timing
requirements: Applications must be submitted to JSPS by a host researcher in Japan via the head of their university or institution
Submit the application form using the JSPS Electronic Application System by the deadline designated by the host institution, which may be more than one month before the JSPS deadline
The JSPS Electronic Application System becomes available approximately two months before the application periods set by JSPS
The host institution must verify approval by the head of the institution and that the stated requirements will be carried out if approved
scholarships.duration: 1 to 12 months
scholarships.application_period: Three open calls per year. FY2027 2nd: application deadline January 8, 2027 (5 p.m. JST), results mid-May 2027, arrival August 1, 2027 - March 31, 2028, 20 fellowships. FY2027 3rd: application deadline June 4, 2027 (5 p.m. JST), results late September 2027, arrival December 1, 2027 - March 31, 2028, 20 fellowships. The JSPS Electronic Application System opens approximately two months before each period.
scholarships.selection_notes:
Selection is carried out by the JSPS International Program Committee, made up of Japan's frontline researchers, through document review in the first stage and panel review in the second
Document reviews are conducted by three examiners using a graduated scoring scale of 1 to 5, taking into account research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity and future potential
Selection policy: the fellowship contributes to promoting exchange between Japan and North America and Europe, and advances both the candidate's and the host's research work
Selection policy: the host and candidate have established close communication and devised a concrete research plan, and the host institution has adequately prepared a system for receiving the candidate
Selection policy: consideration is given to honing the research skills of pre-doctoral candidates, and preference is not given to host institution or field of specialization as much as possible
Any reviewer with a potential conflict of interest is removed from the Review Committee, and all members comply with confidentiality and non-disclosure obligations
scholarships.program_type: Government research fellowship
scholarships.image_alt_text: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science
scholarships.name: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Short-term Program for North American and European Researchers, PE)

scholarships.title: Apoyo Complementario SECIHTI-OEA 2026
scholarships.description: A complementary support awarded jointly by the OAS and Mexico's Secihti to students who already hold a Secihti National Scholarship for a full-time postgraduate programme in Mexico. The OAS contribution is a single payment of USD 1,200 for settling-in expenses in Mexico, paid in Mexican pesos at the official exchange rate on the day OAS deposits it, and the number of supports depends on OAS funds. Secihti adds its monthly support under the Secihti 2026 National Scholarship Scale plus ISSSTE medical service. The call does not establish tuition, travel or full living-cost coverage, so this is not full funding.

scholarships.deadline_display: Fecha de cierre del proceso: 30 de noviembre de 2026

Ser persona becaria nacional vigente en un programa de posgrado escolarizado.

Estar admitido e inscrito en las áreas de Física, Matemáticas y Ciencias de la Tierra, Biología y Química, Ingenierías, Medicina y Ciencias de la Salud (a excepción de la formación de especialidades y subespecialidades médicas), Biotecnología y Ciencias Agropecuarias.
benefits: The OAS portion is explicitly stated to be independent from the scholarship granted by Secihti.
requirements: The beneficiary must send the information and documentation that the OAS requests for formalisation and disbursement, on time and in full.

Under article 17-A of the Ley Federal de Procedimiento Administrativo, a failure to send that information triggers a single emailed prevención with a term of no fewer than five business days; if it is not corrected, the support may be cancelled and reassigned.
scholarships.duration: The support itself is a one-off contribution for settling-in expenses; the underlying Secihti scholarship runs for the postgraduate programme.
scholarships.application_period: Publicación de la convocatoria: 28 de agosto de 2026. The number of supports depends on the availability of OAS funds.

scholarships.title: KAUST Fellowship (Master's, Ph.D. and M.S./Ph.D. Pathway)
scholarships.description: The KAUST Fellowship is awarded automatically to admitted graduate students at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology in Thuwal, Saudi Arabia. The published package covers full tuition and bench fees (stated as worth up to USD $35,000 per year), a monthly stipend (stated as worth USD $20,000 per year for M.S. students and USD $25,000 to $30,000 per year for Ph.D. students depending on qualifications and academic progress), base on-campus accommodation, health insurance for students and eligible dependents living on campus, and relocation support covering visa, relocation and travel costs. KAUST states the total value of the Fellowship at between $70k and $80k per year depending on the student's situation.
scholarships.deadline: Fall 2027 Round 2 application deadline 3 January 2027 (Round 2 opened 28 September 2026); decisions released 14 February 2027

Masters degree in a subject relevant to the program being applied to, from a recognized higher education institution, for entry into Ph.D. programs; Professional Master's degrees are not regarded as directly equivalent and must be declared
At least 18 years of age on entry
Minimum permitted GPA of 3.0 on a 4-point scale (or equivalent); typically 90% of admitted applicants have a GPA above 3.3 and 75% above 3.5
Evidence of proficiency in the English language
benefits: Eligible students can request a housing upgrade, which will be subject to an additional fee

scholarships.title: MBZUAI Graduate Funding for M.Sc. and Ph.D. Students
scholarships.description: MBZUAI's graduate funding is not a single named scholarship but a University-and-faculty funding model under which funded M.Sc. and Ph.D. students receive free tuition fees, a monthly stipend, one return airfare each year to their home country, health insurance for the approved funding period, and a University-sponsored UAE residence visa and Emirates ID where eligible. Ph.D. Year 1 funding is centrally funded by the University while the student is matched with a faculty advisor, and funding moves to the faculty advisor's funding no later than the start of Year 2. M.Sc. students are fee-paying by default and funding is secured through a faculty advisor-sponsored research or teaching assistantship, or an approved government scholarship for UAE nationals, with merit-based funding considered during the admissions review process. The Master in Applied Artificial Intelligence is a fee-based programme and is not eligible for University or faculty-sponsored funding.

From an accredited university or college recognized by the UAE Ministry of Education (MoE)
Minimum CGPA of 3.0 or 3.5 (on a scale of 4.0) depending on the program

University-sponsored UAE residence visa and Emirates ID (where eligible)

scholarships.title: HBKU Graduate Tuition Waiver and Stipend
scholarships.description: HBKU graduate scholarships may include a tuition waiver applied to reduce tuition costs and a stipend paid directly to the student, and HBKU states that graduate students receiving a stipend would generally also be provided with a tuition waiver. Tuition waivers are standardised across HBKU and range from 100% for PhD STEM and PhD SHAPE and S.J.D. programmes down to 0% for LL.M. programmes, MS Economics and certificate programmes. Stipends are awarded to selected graduate students, with published monthly and annual rates for Qatari, international and local PhD and Master's students, over durations of 45 months for PhD and 21 months for Master's. Awards depend on the availability of funds, are not guaranteed, and are made on a merit or need basis only.

scholarships.title: MOFA Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs runs a scholarship programme for Emirati students to study a Bachelor's degree at one of the world's top universities approved by MOFA, specialising in fields that meet the needs of the UAE diplomatic corps. MOFA states in its FAQ that the programme covers all tuition costs in accordance with the programme's policies, and the applicant must already hold an unconditional direct academic acceptance from an approved university indicating the programme start and end dates and the total cost. The programme is not a general study-abroad scholarship: it carries a service obligation, requiring the holder to join the MOFA diplomatic corps for a period equivalent to the number of academic years covered by the scholarship and to join the Anwar Gargash Diplomatic Academy upon graduation.
scholarships.deadline: No application deadline is published on the program page; applications are registered through the online service and the review and final approval process typically takes between 3 to 5 months, with updates communicated by email or SMS

scholarships.title: Career Development Fellowship
scholarships.description: The Career Development Fellowship provides the most talented early career scientists from underrepresented groups in STEM with research funding and high-quality training opportunities to build a strong base for a successful research career. It is currently offered as a pilot with researchers from Black heritage backgrounds and, if successful, may be broadened to researchers from other underrepresented groups.
scholarships.deadline: 18 November 2026 (2027 round; opened 22 September 2026)
scholarships.deadline_display: 18 November 2026 (2027 round; opened 22 September 2026)
eligibility: You self-identify as being from a Black heritage, including mixed Black background.

You are a UK national or you have completed a part of your education in the UK through your Undergraduate, Master's or PhD degree studies or you hold/have held a postdoctoral researcher position in the UK.
You have a PhD, or will have one by the time the funding starts, but have less than 24 months post-doctoral experience.

Your research is within the Royal Society's remit of natural sciences, which includes but is not limited to, biological research and biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics.
Both UK and non-UK domiciled researchers who wish to conduct their research in the UK are eligible.
Applicants can be of any nationality and those requiring a visa are eligible to apply for a Global Talent Visa under the fast-track process of endorsement.

Directly allocated costs (at 80%)
Research expenses (at 100%)
Relocation and visa costs for the applicant and their dependants (partner and children), which can be requested in addition to the total grant cap of £703,800 over four years
Financial support for childcare costs arising from attending conferences, collaborative research visits or invited talks

Register interest in the scheme information session

Success rate for 2024/25 was 3% (233 eligible applications, 7 offers).

scholarships.title: Wellcome Early-Career Award
scholarships.description: The Wellcome Early-Career Award funds early-career researchers from any discipline who are ready to develop their research identity and lead their own independent research programme. The award provides the total cost of the grantholder's salary for the entire grant period, determined by the administering organisation, plus up to £400,000 for research expenses. Certain costs sit outside the £400,000 limit, including overheads, overseas allowances, adjustment support, and the cost of macaques purchased from the MRC Centre for Macaques. Staff salaries are funded up to the equivalent of a 36-month full-time post, and no studentships are provided on this award.
scholarships.deadline: There are no deadlines for applications to this scheme. Applications can be submitted at any time. Apply anytime - Applications are accepted year-round.
scholarships.deadline_display: There are no deadlines for applications to this scheme. Applications can be submitted at any time. Apply anytime - Applications are accepted year-round.
eligibility: You should be able to demonstrate the ability to conduct independent, original research that makes a meaningful contribution to knowledge, achieved through completion of a PhD or equivalent higher research degree (you must have passed your thesis defence by the date you submit your application), or through at least four years' research experience equivalent to a PhD.

Any periods of research undertaken during an undergraduate or Master's degree are not counted as equivalent research experience, and you must not have started a PhD or equivalent higher research degree if relying on the experience route.

You may have some postdoctoral experience in your proposed field of study, but no more than three years at the date of submission unless you can demonstrate how other factors have impacted on your research career.

You must be able to contribute at least 80% of your research time in support of the project proposed in the award, and should not spend more than 20% of your time on non-research related activities; if you are in a clinical craft speciality you may spend up to 40% of your time on clinical duties.

If you are a health professional and want to continue with clinical activities, you must be registered with, and be licensed by, the relevant professional regulator in the country you intend to work in.

Your administering organisation must be in the UK, the Republic of Ireland, or a low- or middle-income country apart from India and mainland China; the organisation must be not-for-profit and can be a higher education institution, research institute or healthcare organisation.

Your sponsor must be an individual at your administering organisation holding an established post (or an honorary academic appointment) for the duration of the award, and must guarantee the space and resources you will need from the start date to the end date of the award.
You should also identify a mentor for the period of your award with a track record in training and mentorship; your sponsor can also be your mentor. Sponsors and mentors are not paid for their input.
Coapplicants are not accepted.
You may only have one application under consideration as a lead applicant at any one time for the Early Career Award, Career Development Award and Discovery Award schemes.

Your research must fit within what Wellcome supports in Discovery Research and have the potential to improve human life, health and wellbeing; it can be in any discipline including STEM, experimental medicine, humanities and social science, clinical/allied health sciences and public health.
benefits: If, after two or more years from the activation date, your organisation awards you a permanent, open-ended or long-term rolling contract that includes your salary, you can keep the salary element of the award to use towards your remaining research costs
Award holders who need a visa to work in the UK may be eligible for a Global Talent Visa
The award may be held on a part-time basis, with the duration extended to reflect this; the application must still be costed at 1.0 (100%) full-time equivalent
Access to Wellcome's global talent, mentoring and community networks
requirements: Submit your application through Wellcome Funding, and only once all required sections and documents are complete
Obtain a sponsor statement from an individual at your administering organisation who holds an established post for the duration of the award
Identify a mentor with a track record in training and mentorship
If requesting overheads, provide a letter from your Finance Director stating how overhead costs were calculated, including confirmation of any externally validated rate and when it was last reviewed
You must check that your type of research project is within what Wellcome funds in Discovery Research before applying
scholarships.duration: Usually 5 years, but may be less for some disciplines, and may only be longer if held on a part-time basis
scholarships.application_period: Rolling, applications accepted year-round. Location eligibility changes on 29 October 2026: from that date applications are only accepted from lead applicants based at eligible administering organisations in the UK and low- and middle-income countries in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia. Applications submitted on or before 28 October 2026 are assessed under the current location eligibility requirements.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are assessed through Wellcome's shortlisting Advisory Groups and then peer review. The same project may be submitted for consideration a maximum of two times across all Wellcome funding schemes and themed funding calls, and resubmissions must include significant changes demonstrating clear development of the original proposal. If your application scores in the lowest levels at the shortlisting meeting you will not be permitted to resubmit. If unsuccessful with an Early-Career Award, you may submit one further application for the same project to any Wellcome scheme, provided you still meet the eligibility criteria.

scholarships.name: Wellcome Early-Career Award

scholarships.title: UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers' Fellowships Programme (UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships Programme) - Cycle 2026
scholarships.description: Under the 2026 cycle UNESCO and the Government of Japan award 10 fellowships to young researchers from Africa, Small Island Developing States, Ukraine and Turkiye to carry out postgraduate research in a Japanese university or research institution. Selected fellows may receive a fellowship grant of up to US$10,000, provided as a lump-sum contribution intended to cover costs directly related to the approved research stay in Japan. The grant may cover international and domestic travel for the approved itinerary, accommodation, medical insurance, personal subsistence in Japan including meals, local transportation and incidental expenses, and other research-related expenses where applicable. It is a research fellowship, not a degree programme: the grant does not cover tuition fees, and the page publishes no award figures beyond the US$10,000 ceiling.
scholarships.deadline: Deadline for candidate submission is now extended to 15 October 2026, midnight Paris time. scholarships.title: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP) 2027 - Application Window for Japanese Nationals
scholarships.description: This is the Japanese-nationals track of the Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program, which the World Bank states is fully funded by the Government of Japan. It funds up to two years for a limited number of Japanese mid-career professionals dedicated to the alleviation of poverty and enhanced shared prosperity in developing countries who have been admitted to or are currently enrolled in a master's or PhD programme outside Japan in a development-related field. Benefits include one economy class air travel to the host university and a $600 travel allowance at the start, one economy class return travel and a $600 travel allowance at the end, tuition, basic medical insurance obtainable through the university, and a monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus. The amount of the monthly subsistence allowance varies by host country and is not published on the page.
scholarships.deadline: The 2027 application window for Japanese nationals will open from February 15 to April 16, 2027. As from February 15, 2027, prospective candidates are invited to express their interest to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat with an email to scholarshipapplicants@worldbank.org. Winners are informed by mid-July, after the JJ/WBGSC approval. The 2026 application window for Japanese nationals closed on Friday 17 April 2026.
scholarships.deadline_display: The 2027 application window for Japanese nationals will open from February 15 to April 16, 2027. As from February 15, 2027, prospective candidates are invited to express their interest to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat with an email to scholarshipapplicants@worldbank.org. Winners are informed by mid-July, after the JJ/WBGSC approval. The 2026 application window for Japanese nationals closed on Friday 17 April 2026.
eligibility: Be a Japanese national

On or after the date the call for scholarship applications opens, not be an Executive Director, his/her alternate, and/or staff of any type of appointment (including temporary and consultant) of the World Bank Group (The World Bank, International Development Association, International Finance Corporation, Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, and International Center for Settlements of Investment Disputes), and not be a close relative of any of the aforementioned by blood or adoption (close relative defined as Mother, Father, Sister, Half-sister, Brother, Half-brother, Son, Daughter, Aunt, Uncle, Niece, or Nephew)
Hold a bachelor's degree (or equivalent university degree) earned at least three years before the date of the Application Deadline

On or after the date the JJ/WBGSP scholarship application process opens, not be employed (as a staff or any type of employment) by the Government of Japan or its related agencies, including JICA, local governments and the Central Bank

Have at least 3 years of paid development-related employment acquired since earning a bachelor's degree (or equivalent university degree) and acquired within the past six years from the date of the Application Deadline

At the time of the application submission, be either admitted unconditionally (except for financing) or currently enrolled full-time in a graduate program outside of Japan in an area of study related to development, or be currently employed full-time in development-related work pertaining directly to developing countries
benefits: The scholarship is fully funded by the Government of Japan
All JJ/WBGSP scholarships cover the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less
Two separate $600 travel allowances are payable, one at the start of the programme and one at the end
requirements: Register interest with the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat by emailing scholarshipapplicants@worldbank.org from February 15, 2027
Details on eligibility criteria for each call for applications are provided in that call's Application Guidelines, and those detailed criteria are strictly adhered to with no exceptions

Be admitted unconditionally (except for financing) to, or currently enrolled full-time in, a graduate program outside of Japan in an area of study related to development, or be currently employed full-time in development-related work pertaining directly to developing countries
Inform and document to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat any other sources of scholarship funds if notified of being a semi-finalist or awarded a scholarship
scholarships.duration: Up to two years; all JJ/WBGSP scholarships cover the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less
scholarships.application_period: A single application window for the 2027 cycle for Japanese nationals, from February 15 to April 16, 2027. From the opening date, prospective candidates are invited to register interest with the Secretariat by email. Results are communicated by mid-July 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: Two qualified assessors independently review each eligible application and score it on a scale of 1 to 10 on four factors: Quality of Academic Experience and Recommendation (20% weight), Quality of Professional Recommendations (20% weight), Quality of Professional Experience (20%), and Commitment to International Development Career (40% weight). The Secretariat uses the average score of the two assessors plus maintaining a reasonable distribution of awards across gender and giving scholarships to those applicants who, other things being equal, have limited access to financial resources for graduate studies abroad. Finalists are presented to the JJ/WBG Steering Committee, composed of members of the World Bank Board of Directors and World Bank management, for approval.

scholarships.title: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships (ESKAS)
scholarships.description: The Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships are awarded annually by the Swiss Confederation to encourage international exchange and research cooperation between Switzerland and more than 180 other countries. Recipients are selected by the Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students (FCS, also known as ESKAS), an independent decentralised federal body that is not bound by directives. The programme has two components: research scholarships for talented early career researchers from abroad who have already completed a Master's degree, and art scholarships for students from a limited number of countries wishing to pursue an initial Master's degree in an artistic field in Switzerland. Applicants are aged 35 or less and the scholarship pays CHF 2,450 per month.
scholarships.deadline: Applications are open from 20 August 2026. Applications are submitted to the applicant's Swiss diplomatic representation, and the deadline is set country by country: information on application deadlines and scholarship opportunities by country of origin is published by the Federal Commission in August each year.
scholarships.deadline_display: Applications are open from 20 August 2026. Applications are submitted to the applicant's Swiss diplomatic representation, and the deadline is set country by country: information on application deadlines and scholarship opportunities by country of origin is published by the Federal Commission in August each year.
eligibility: Maximum age 35 (date of birth after 31 December 1991 for the 2027-2028 cycle)
Master's degree or equivalent completed by 31 July 2027 (30 June 2027 for ETH Zurich)
Applicants from one of the 183 eligible countries of origin
For PhD scholarships at graduate schools only: confirmation of admission to a doctoral school must be submitted together with the application
Letter of support from an academic supervisor in Switzerland, with a short CV of that supervisor
Applicants already residing in Switzerland must have entered Switzerland no earlier than 1 August 2026, evidenced by the registration confirmation or residence permit
For art scholarships: initial Master's degree in an artistic field in Switzerland, and nationality of one of the limited number of eligible countries
benefits: CHF 2,450 per month to cover basic living expenses for one person
Official note that the scholarship is not a salary and must not be treated as equivalent to regular remuneration, financially or legally
PhD scholarships renewable twice for up to 36 months, subject to academic progress
requirements: Applications must be submitted to the Swiss diplomatic representation of the applicant's country of origin, within the country-specific deadline
Detailed research plan with a timeline specifying key milestones and activities
For PhD scholarships at graduate schools only: confirmation of admission to the doctoral school must be submitted with the application
The PhD scholarship application (with the supervisor letter) and the application for admission to a doctoral programme are two separate procedures
scholarships.duration: Research fellowships: maximum 12 months (minimum 6 months), no extension possible, start 1 September 2027. PhD scholarships: 12 months, renewable twice for up to 36 months subject to academic progress, start 1 September 2027.
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle. Applications open on 20 August 2026, country-specific deadlines apply between August and December 2026, and the Federal Commission announces its award decisions by the end of May at the latest for the following academic year.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are submitted to the applicant's Swiss diplomatic representation. The Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students assesses applications against three criteria: candidate profile, quality of the research project or artistic work, and synergies and potential for future research cooperation. Art scholarships are reviewed in consultation with the Federal Office of Culture.

scholarships.title: Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP)
scholarships.description: The Swiss-European Mobility Programme is Switzerland's national mobility programme for higher education and forms part of the Swiss solution to the EU's Erasmus+ programme. Funded by SERI and implemented by the Swiss agency Movetia, it enables officially accredited Swiss higher education institutions and colleges of higher education to send their students and staff abroad (outgoing) and to host students and staff from abroad (incoming). Students, including PhD students, spend one or two semesters at a partner higher education institution and keep their enrolment at home, earning ECTS credits; they do not pay study fees abroad and receive financial support for travelling and accommodation.
scholarships.deadline: There is no central student deadline. Participants apply through their home institution's International Relations Office and the deadline is set by that institution. For institutions, accreditation and funding applications can be submitted annually at the beginning of March and the funding period starts on 1 June of the year of application. Movetia currently states that the next application deadline is spring 2027, likely under Erasmus+.
scholarships.deadline_display: There is no central student deadline. Participants apply through their home institution's International Relations Office and the deadline is set by that institution. For institutions, accreditation and funding applications can be submitted annually at the beginning of March and the funding period starts on 1 June of the year of application. Movetia currently states that the next application deadline is spring 2027, likely under Erasmus+.
eligibility: Enrolled at a higher education institution (university, university of applied sciences, university of teacher education) or college of higher education in Switzerland or abroad; PhD students included
Stay lasting between 60 days and 12 months
Interinstitutional agreement between the home and host institutions
Follow courses at the host institution that count towards the student's degree (ECTS credits or equivalent)
For funding applicants: an officially recognised Swiss higher education institution, or a college of higher education with federally recognised courses at higher education level
Accreditation under the SEMP Charter or a European Charter for Higher Education (ECHE); partner institutions abroad must hold an ECHE or formally accept the SEMP quality principles
benefits: European mobility outgoing: CHF 1,430 to CHF 3,900 depending on duration
European mobility incoming: CHF 1,430 to CHF 4,500 depending on duration and country of origin
Worldwide mobility: CHF 1,750 to CHF 5,000 for incoming and outgoing mobility depending on duration
CHF 100 sustainable-mobility contribution included in European mobility grants when travelling sustainably
Special-needs grant of up to CHF 12,000 for individuals with disabilities or physical, mental or chronic illness
No study fees payable abroad during the mobility
requirements: Only Swiss institutions can apply for funding with Movetia; the institution must be an officially recognised higher education institution based in Switzerland or a college of higher education with federally recognised courses at higher education level
Accreditation under the SEMP Charter, or a European Charter for Higher Education (ECHE) for partners abroad
A learning agreement for study mobility, validated in advance by the sending and receiving institutions and the participant
The grant is always paid out by the Swiss home or host institution, never directly to the participant
scholarships.duration: 2 to 12 months per mobility (a stay must last between 60 days and 12 months); one or two semesters for study mobility
scholarships.application_period: Annual institutional cycle: applications from accredited institutions each March, funding period from 1 June. Student-level applications run year-round through the home institution's own deadlines. Movetia expects the next call to be launched under Erasmus+ following Switzerland's planned association from 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: Participants are selected by their home institution through fair and transparent selection procedures and criteria; each institution sets its own participation criteria, and some award SEMP grants only for mobilities within Europe. Institutions may also apply internal restrictions, for example no mobility to the applicant's country of origin for foreign nationals, language skills, or mobility duration.
scholarships.program_type: Government mobility programme (higher education), Swiss solution to Erasmus+
scholarships.name: Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP)

scholarships.title: Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP) - Incoming Mobility to Switzerland
scholarships.description: Incoming mobility to Switzerland is funded under the Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP), the higher education part of the Swiss Programme for Erasmus+ that Switzerland operates in place of Erasmus+ association. Students from abroad, including PhD students, can spend one or two semesters at a Swiss university or college of higher education, or do a traineeship in Switzerland, while remaining enrolled at their home institution and earning ECTS credits. They do not pay study fees at the Swiss host institution and receive a financial contribution towards travel and accommodation. Applications are coordinated by the international relations office of the Swiss host institution, which is the only party that can receive and pay out the grant.
scholarships.deadline: There is no central deadline for individual students: applications are handled by the international relations office of the Swiss host institution, which sets its own dates. At institutional level, accreditation and funding applications go to Movetia annually in early March for a funding period starting 1 June. Movetia currently states that the next application deadline is spring 2027, likely under Erasmus+.
scholarships.deadline_display: There is no central deadline for individual students: applications are handled by the international relations office of the Swiss host institution, which sets its own dates. At institutional level, accreditation and funding applications go to Movetia annually in early March for a funding period starting 1 June. Movetia currently states that the next application deadline is spring 2027, likely under Erasmus+.

Stay of between 60 days and 12 months
Interinstitutional agreement between the home institution and the Swiss host institution

scholarships.selection_notes: Selection is carried out by the home institution abroad (which runs the application and nominates the student) and then by the Swiss host institution, which coordinates the SEMP application and pays out the grant. scholarships.program_type: Government mobility programme (higher education), Swiss solution to Erasmus+ - incoming mobility
scholarships.name: Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP) - Incoming Mobility to Switzerland

scholarships.title: Türkiye Bursları (Türkiye Scholarships) - Turkish Government Scholarship
scholarships.description: Türkiye Bursları is the Republic of Türkiye's government-funded, competitive scholarship programme for international students, run under the coordination of the Presidency of Turks Abroad and Relatives of Overseas Citizens (YTB). It funds associate, bachelor's, master's, PhD and research places at the most prestigious Turkish universities and is distinctive in providing university and department placement rather than a fellowship to be spent at a chosen institution. The package covers tuition, a monthly stipend, health insurance, accommodation, a one-year Turkish language course, a once-off return flight ticket and free academic and cultural programmes. Applications are submitted online, free of charge, through the Türkiye Scholarships Application System (TBBS).

scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are received in one period each year, free of charge. Candidates are given the opportunity to select between 12 choices online, and the programme assigns university and department placement.

scholarships.title: Invest Your Talent in Italy (IYT) — MAECI / ICE / Uni-Italia scholarship programme
scholarships.description: Invest Your Talent in Italy is a MAECI scholarship programme run with the ICE Agency and Uni-Italia that pays a nine-month scholarship to foreign students from 22 partner countries to attend a Master's or Postgraduate course at a participating Italian university, combined with a compulsory internship at an Italian company or professional association. Courses are taught entirely in English, and the programme includes study of Italian language and culture plus a mandatory gender-equality and anti-gender-violence seminar or module. The winner receives an annual scholarship of EUR 10,800, paid quarterly into an Italian bank account in the holder's name, and is exempt from enrolment fees and university contributions, but must still pay the regional right-to-education tax, stamp duty, accident and civil liability insurance and health insurance. The scholarship explicitly does not cover travel expenses and does not include accommodation, and the recipient must independently arrange health insurance.

scholarships.deadline_display: 11 May 2026, 6:00 pm Italian time (11th edition, now closed)

scholarships.title: Boren Scholarships and Fellowships (National Security Education Program)
scholarships.description: The National Security Education Program awards Boren Scholarships and Fellowships to U.S. undergraduate and graduate students committed to long-term overseas study and to federal service. Boren Scholarships fund study abroad by U.S. undergraduates and Boren Fellowships fund research and language study proposals by U.S. graduate students, in world regions critical to U.S. interests. Maximum awards are determined by duration abroad: $25,000 for 25-52 weeks (preferred), $12,500 for 12-24 weeks, and $8,000 for 8-11 weeks for STEM majors under the Scholarships programme. There are no minimum language requirements except French and Spanish, which require intermediate high [1+] proficiency for advanced study programs in Africa and Latin America. The Boren Awards are an initiative of the Defense Language and National Security Education Office.
scholarships.deadline: National deadlines for the 2027 Boren Awards: Boren Fellowships January 20, 2027; Boren Scholarships January 27, 2027. 2027-28 Boren Awards funding may be applied to programs starting as early as June 2027 or as late as March 1, 2028. Applicants are notified of selection in mid-to-late April.

Commit to long-term overseas study in a world region critical to U.S. interests
Pursue a career with the federal government and accept the one-year federal service requirement
For Boren Scholarships studying STEM, satisfy the additional criteria for the shorter 8-11 week award tier

scholarships.selection_notes: The homepage directs applicants to review the official selection criteria, and frames professional goals as critical: the Boren Awards invest in linguistic and cultural knowledge for aspiring federal government employees, so the national security implications of the study and career opportunities matter to a successful application.

scholarships.title: Kyushu University Friendship Scholarship
scholarships.degree: Undergraduate, Master's, PhD (exchange, special auditing, special research or double degree enrolment at Kyushu University)
scholarships.description: Kyushu University's own support programme for privately financed international students who come to Kyushu University on exchange, special auditing, special research or double degree status and who cannot afford to study in Japan solely at their own expense. It pays a monthly stipend of JPY 80,000, and the total of all scholarships held by the grantee may not exceed that amount. Applicants apply through their prospective host department at Kyushu University, not directly to the university centre. There are two recruitment periods per fiscal year: Period I around February for students who will study from April to September, and Period II around May for students who will study from October to March. The period of stay must be 3 months, 5 months (one semester) or 11 months (two semesters).

scholarships.title: EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships
scholarships.description: EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships support excellent postdoctoral researchers throughout Europe and the world for a period of up to two years. International mobility is a key requirement, and the fellowship includes a salary or stipend, a relocation allowance and support for fellows with children.
scholarships.deadline: Friday 22 January 2027, 14:00 CET
scholarships.deadline_display: Friday 22 January 2027, 14:00 CET
eligibility: Applicants must hold a doctorate or equivalent at the start of the fellowship
Applicants who already hold a PhD at the time of application are eligible only if they obtained it during the two years prior to the date the application is submitted
Applicants must have at least one first author publication (research paper) accepted in or published in an international peer reviewed journal at the time of application
A first author preprint with public in-depth peer reviews obtained from an independent peer review service is also sufficient for eligibility
All applications must involve movement between countries
Applications to go to the country in which the PhD was obtained will not be considered
Applications to return to a laboratory where the candidate worked for more than six months in total will not be considered
Applications to work in the laboratory, institute or department where the candidate worked to obtain the PhD, or again with the candidate's PhD supervisor, will not be considered
Candidates who have already started working in the host laboratory may apply only if they have been living in the host country for less than six months at the time the application is submitted
Candidates can submit only one application for one project at one host laboratory at each round of selection
Projects that are a direct continuation of the PhD work are not eligible
benefits: Salary or stipend for the postdoctoral position (host-institution employment contract in EMBC Member States)
Travel and relocation allowance as a lump sum
Child daycare allowance up to EUR 2,500 per fellowship year per child for children under six (non-EMBC fellows only)
Dependent child allowance for children under 18 (non-EMBC fellows only, value depends on country visited)
Free attendance at an EMBO Laboratory Leadership Course
Travel and accommodation for the two-day EMBO workshop for journalist fellows is not part of this scheme
requirements: At least one first-author publication in an international peer-reviewed journal, or a first-author preprint with public in-depth peer reviews from an independent peer review service
PhD obtained within the two years preceding the application submission date
Cross-country mobility between the country of the PhD and the host country
Doctoral supervisor's support and a host laboratory in a host institution
Agreement with the host institution that the EMBO grant is used to fund an employment contract for the fellow
scholarships.duration: Up to two years; minimum one year; maximum combined full-time and part-time duration 36 months
scholarships.application_period: Rolling applications; evaluation rounds with hard cutoffs (next cutoff 22 January 2027, 14:00 CET)
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are assessed on the excellence of the research project, the applicant's track record and the international mobility of the project. Effective from the Autumn 2026 selection round a host laboratory may support a maximum of one candidate per selection round. Effective from the Autumn 2027 selection round (applications submitted after 22 January 2027, 14:00 CET) re-applications will no longer be permitted.
scholarships.program_type: Research fellowship (life sciences)
scholarships.name: EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships

scholarships.title: Maria Leptin | EMBO Science Journalism Fellowships
scholarships.description: The Maria Leptin | EMBO Science Journalism Fellowships support science journalism by providing journalists with funded placements at research institutions to deepen and broaden their knowledge of the life and associated sciences, and researchers wishing to transition full time into journalism with funded placements in media newsrooms. The scheme was made possible by a private donation from Professor Maria Leptin.
scholarships.deadline: 30 October each year, 23:59 Central European Summer Time (applications may be submitted at any time but must be registered by this deadline)
scholarships.deadline_display: 30 October each year, 23:59 Central European Summer Time (applications may be submitted at any time but must be registered by this deadline)
eligibility: Applicants must reside in an EMBC Member State
The placement or placements must also occur in an EMBC Member State
Placements must be in person; virtual placements are not eligible
If Fellows undertake two or more placements, at least one must be in a different EMBC Member State than the others
Applicants are not subject to any age restriction
Journalists must demonstrate relevant experience of working as an employed or freelance journalist as their main occupation
Journalists must provide samples of their published or broadcast work
Journalists must show a genuine desire to broaden and deepen their knowledge of science, not a search for immediate publication opportunities
Life scientists seeking to transition to full-time journalism must hold a master's degree or higher, preferably in a life sciences discipline
Life scientists must demonstrate a genuine intention to move into journalism as a profession, with evidence of prior reporting on the life sciences or associated disciplines
Personal blog posts, social media postings, or commentary and review articles in academic journals are not accepted as evidence of prior journalism
Fellows are expected not to undertake other work during the fellowship and must not report on their host research institution during the fellowship term
benefits: Daily subsistence stipend sized to the cost of living in the host country
Living expenses
Travel costs connected with the placement
requirements: Proposal in English of a maximum of three pages
For journalists: nomination of the research institution and specific learning and knowledge outcomes
For researchers: nomination of the newsroom and confirmation that the placement will be a full-time internship producing published or broadcast science journalism
Curriculum vitae in English with permanent residential address, email and mobile phone number
Samples of previous journalism work, which may be in any language
Prior discussion of the proposal with the proposed host, although formal written acceptance is not required at application stage
For journalists: confirmation that the sabbatical is focused on individual learning and long-term development and that the fellow will not report from the host institution
scholarships.duration: Journalists: minimum three months, maximum six months. Researchers transitioning to journalism: minimum three months, maximum twelve months.
scholarships.application_period: Applications can be submitted at any time; selection takes place once a year and fully completed applications must be registered in the EMBO portal by 23:59 CEST on 30 October each year. Applicants are notified by mid-November.
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection takes place once a year, with outcomes notified by email by mid-November. Applicants are judged by the EMBO advisory board on the genuine desire to broaden science knowledge or to move into journalism, the quality of the proposal and the learning outcomes set. The scheme was made possible by a private donation from Professor Maria Leptin.
scholarships.program_type: Science journalism fellowship
scholarships.name: Maria Leptin | EMBO Science Journalism Fellowships

scholarships.title: UM NL Global Studies Scholarship
scholarships.description: Maastricht University awards one full-coverage scholarship per academic year to a bachelor student who has been admitted to its Global Studies bachelor's programme. For 2027-2028 the award covers tuition fees at cost plus a living-expense stipend of EUR 20,150 per academic year, and includes a mandatory two-week UM Pre-Academic Training in the first week of August 2027. Applications are open from 1 October 2026 to 1 February 2027, and the bachelor's programme application in Studielink must be complete by 10 December 2026.
scholarships.deadline: 1 February 2027, 23:59 CET
scholarships.deadline_display: 1 February 2027, 23:59 CET
eligibility: Nationality of an OECD DAC-eligible country, Surinam excluded
No dual nationality with an EU/EEA country, Switzerland or Surinam
Able to obtain an entry visa and residence permit for the Netherlands
Applicant to the Global Studies bachelor's programme at Maastricht University for 2027-2028, file complete before 10 December 2026
Meets the specific admission requirements of the bachelor programme applied to
Does not hold a diploma from a higher education institution and has not completed a bachelor-equivalent degree
Not older than 35 on 1 September 2027
benefits: EUR 20,150 per academic year for living expenses, broken down by Maastricht as housing EUR 960, groceries and personal hygiene EUR 160, telephone EUR 60, travel EUR 100, books and study materials EUR 90, clothing, hobbies and going out EUR 125, miscellaneous EUR 55
A UM room allocated to the scholar until 16 July 2028
Two-week mandatory UM Pre-Academic Training in the first week of August 2027
Participation in the International Student Ambassador Programme
requirements: Apply for the Global Studies bachelor's programme at Maastricht University via Studielink and receive a UM student ID before applying for the scholarship
Complete all registration requirements by 1 February 2027, except legal residence, tuition payment and a hard copy of the diploma
Pay any programme handling fee yourself by 10 December 2026; the scholarship does not cover it
Sign and return the award letter to the UM International Services Desk to accept the scholarship
Agree to act as an active Global Studies and UM ambassador during and after the studies, including at least one information session
scholarships.duration: 36 months (the full three-year Global Studies bachelor's programme)
scholarships.application_period: 1 October 2026 - 1 February 2027 (scholarship form); bachelor programme application in Studielink by 10 December 2026
scholarships.selection_notes: The UM International Services Desk checks application completeness after 1 February 2027; the Global Studies admission office ranks files on the UM scholarship selection criteria and proposes a top five to the Global Studies Scholarship selection committee in March 2027; the top five are interviewed online; candidates are informed of their status in April 2027, with selected, waitlisted or rejected status final by the beginning of June 2027.
scholarships.program_type: University scholarship
scholarships.name: UM NL Global Studies Scholarship

scholarships.title: Latvian State Scholarship for Foreign Students (Scholarship for Studies in Latvia)
scholarships.description: The Latvian state scholarship for studies pays a monthly stipend to students from more than 30 partner countries who are enrolled in a bachelor's, master's or doctoral programme at a Latvian higher education institution. It is worth EUR 500 per month for bachelor's and master's students and EUR 700 per month for doctoral students, awarded for up to 10 months (11 months for doctoral students). The annual call runs from 1 February to 1 April through the VIAA online application system, so the next window opens on 1 February 2027.
scholarships.deadline: 1 April 2027
scholarships.deadline_display: 1 April 2027
eligibility: Nationality of one of Latvia's partner countries (39 eligible countries are listed by VIAA)
Bachelor's applicants must have completed at least one academic year at any higher education institution
Master's or PhD applicants may apply from any previous higher education institution
Must have chosen a study programme at a Latvian higher education institution and obtained a confirmation letter from the designated institutional contact person before applying
Cannot be awarded concurrently with other grants
Must be present in Latvia for the scholarship to be paid; no scholarship is provided for presence of under 15 calendar days
benefits: EUR 500 monthly stipend for bachelor's and master's students
EUR 700 monthly stipend for doctoral students
A separate strand funds participation in approved summer schools in Latvia, with funds transferred to the organisers rather than to the participant
requirements: Submit the application online in the VIAA electronic application system
Fill in the application form according to the published quality evaluation criteria; incomplete or incorrect applications are not assessed
Attach all required documents translated into Latvian or English
Use the unified HEI confirmation letter template, signed and submitted by the institutional contact person
Register a profile with a unique login and password in the VIAA system
scholarships.duration: Up to 10 months for bachelor's and master's students; up to 11 months for doctoral students; maximum two terms within one study cycle
scholarships.application_period: 1 February - 1 April annually
scholarships.selection_notes: All applications are evaluated against the published quality evaluation criteria and the final decision on granting scholarships is made by the VIAA evaluation committee. Candidates receive an official decision by email in June, also visible in their profile in the electronic application system.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship
scholarships.name: Latvian State Scholarship for Foreign Students (Scholarship for Studies in Latvia)

scholarships.title: International Excellence Entrance Scholarship
scholarships.description: The University of Manitoba awards one International Excellence Entrance Scholarship valued at $25,000 and two valued at $10,000 each to international high school graduates entering University 1 or any faculty, college or school with a direct entry option. The $25,000 award requires a minimum admission average of 90% across five senior level high school courses, while the two $10,000 awards require only the minimum admission requirements for the programme. Short-listed applicants are ranked first, second and third place using the award application and the admissions application. This is a separate application from the admissions application, although both must be completed.
scholarships.deadline: December 1 (2027/28 cycle)
scholarships.deadline_display: December 1 (2027/28 cycle)
eligibility: Are international students
Are enrolled full-time (minimum 80% course load) in the first year of study in University 1 or any faculty, college or school at the University of Manitoba with a direct entry option

For the $25,000 award: have achieved a minimum admission average of 90% across five of the following senior level high school courses: Math, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Computer Sciences, English, First Language Literature, Geography, History, Music and Visual Arts
For the $10,000 awards: have achieved the minimum admission requirements for University 1 or any faculty, college or school with a direct entry option
Have demonstrated strong leadership qualities and sustained, meaningful community involvement
Have completed a University of Manitoba application for admission by December 1, including payment of the application fee
benefits: One award valued at $25,000
Two awards valued at $10,000 each
Separate funding recognition from the general entrance award pool, which runs on a different deadline
requirements: Submit a separate award application in addition to the admission application
Nominate one recommender who is a current teacher or principal
Ensure the recommender submits their letter by the December 1 deadline
scholarships.duration: Entrance award for the first year of study
scholarships.application_period: Application for the 2027/28 International Excellence Entrance Scholarship is open now; the complete application and all required documentation must be received by December 1.
scholarships.selection_notes: Short-listed applicants are ranked in first, second and third place based on the results from the award application and the admissions application.
scholarships.program_type: University merit entrance scholarship
scholarships.name: International Excellence Entrance Scholarship

scholarships.title: Killam Predoctoral Scholarship Level 2 (Doctoral)
scholarships.description: The Faculty of Graduate Studies at Dalhousie University awards Killam Predoctoral Scholarships competitively to outstanding doctoral students across all disciplines, with a base value of $42,000 per year ($14,000 per term) for up to three years. The scholarship is open to both Canadian and international students in a full-time PhD at Dalhousie, and international recipients may only use the funds for study and research in Canada. Applicants who are not eligible to apply for a Tri-agency CGRS-D through Dalhousie in the current competition apply through the Faculty of Graduate Studies scholarship platform. The scholarship is supported by the Killam Trusts.
scholarships.deadline: Round one: October 16, 2026 at midnight AT. Round two: opens January 5, 2027, submissions due February 28, 2027 at midnight AT
scholarships.deadline_display: Round one: October 16, 2026 at midnight AT. Round two: opens January 5, 2027, submissions due February 28, 2027 at midnight AT
eligibility: Enrolled in a full-time doctoral (PhD) degree at Dalhousie University
Canadian or international student
Demonstrates exceptional academic achievement, strong research potential and a clear likelihood of contributing to the advancement of learning in their field
Award taken up no later than the 7th term in the PhD program

Has spent less than six terms (24 months) in the PhD as of May 1 of the award year; for students who transferred or intend to transfer from a Master's to a PhD without completing the Master's, time-in-program begins at the transfer date
benefits: Base value $42,000 per year ($14,000 per term) for up to three years
If a Tri-agency CGRS-D is awarded, the CGRS-D value of $40,000 per year is topped up to $48,000 per year ($16,000 per term) while both awards are held concurrently
If the CGRS-D expires before the end of the award holder's fourth year in the PhD, Killam funding is extended into the remaining terms of the fourth year at $14,000 per term
Relocation allowance reimbursing travel to Nova Scotia, not exceeding the lowest cost airfare available by the most direct route
Paid parental leave benefits for predoctoral Killam scholars without access to other paid parental leave support
Non-paid interruption of the award for up to 12 months for an approved leave of absence, with the end date extended by the leave duration
requirements: Submit the application and all accompanying materials by the stated round deadline, after which the application closes

Non-Tri-agency applicants create an application in the Faculty of Graduate Studies Scholarship Management Platform under Major Scholarship Competitions 2026/2027 and the category Major Scholarship Application for Non-Tri-Agency Applicants
Dalhousie students with a NetID access the platform using their Dalhousie NetID
Complete an annual report and submit it to fgs.slo@dal.ca by July 31 of each year the award is held
Apply for a Tri-agency CGRS-D within the first two years of holding the Killam award
Participate in Killam scholar initiatives and events whenever possible
scholarships.duration: Up to three years
scholarships.application_period: Round one is open now and closes October 16, 2026 at midnight Atlantic Time; round two opens January 5, 2027 and closes February 28, 2027 at midnight AT. These rounds are stated for non-Tri-agency applicants.
scholarships.selection_notes: Awards are made competitively on the basis of exceptional academic achievement, strong research potential and a clear likelihood of contributing to the advancement of learning in the field; considerations beyond academic excellence include character, ethical conduct and contributions to a respectful and inclusive community.
scholarships.program_type: University doctoral scholarship
scholarships.name: Killam Predoctoral Scholarship Level 2 (Doctoral)

scholarships.title: Dalhousie Research Excellence Scholarship (DRES)
scholarships.description: Established in 2024, the Dalhousie Research Excellence Scholarship attracts and supports exceptional new PhD students at Dalhousie University and is valued at $35,000 per year for up to four years. Of the total, $28,000 is provided by Graduate Studies and the remaining $7,000 by the supervisor and/or programme of study. Applicants must intend to start a PhD at Dalhousie between January 2027 and January 2028, and funds are only administered after admission to and registration in the intended programme. Applicants who apply for a Tri-agency CGRS-D through Dalhousie in the current cycle are considered automatically for DRES funding.
scholarships.deadline: Round one: October 16, 2026 at midnight AT. Round two: opens January 5, 2027, submissions due February 28, 2027 at midnight AT
scholarships.deadline_display: Round one: October 16, 2026 at midnight AT. Round two: opens January 5, 2027, submissions due February 28, 2027 at midnight AT
eligibility: Intent to start, meaning enrol in or transfer to, a PhD programme at Dalhousie between January 2027 and January 2028
Outstanding research achievement
Exceptional leadership potential
Capacity to generate significant regional, national or international impact through their research
Scholarship funds are only administered after admission to and registration in the intended programme of study
benefits: $35,000 per year for up to four years, maintained while the award holder stays eligible
Automatic top-up to $42,000 per year while a Killam Predoctoral Scholarship is held concurrently
Possibility of additional funding beyond the award value through stipends or other sources negotiated with the supervisor or programme of study
requirements: Submit the application and all accompanying materials by the round deadline, after which the application form closes

Non-Tri-agency applicants create an application in the Faculty of Graduate Studies Scholarship Management Platform under Major Scholarship Competitions 2026/2027 and the category Major Scholarship Application for Non-Tri-Agency Applicants
Dalhousie students access the platform using their Dalhousie NetID
Complete an annual report and submit it to fgs.slo@dal.ca by July 31 of each year the award is held
Apply to the Tri-agency CGRS-D competition within the first two years of the PhD programme
Students planning to transfer from a master's to a PhD must apply for a doctoral scholarship before officially transferring into the doctoral programme
scholarships.duration: Up to 48 months, and not past the end of the fourth year in the programme
scholarships.application_period: Round one of the non-Tri-agency competition is open until October 16, 2026 at midnight Atlantic Time; round two opens January 5, 2027 and closes February 28, 2027 at midnight AT. Intended PhD start must fall between January 2027 and January 2028.
scholarships.selection_notes: The award targets applicants demonstrating outstanding research achievement, exceptional leadership potential, and the capacity to generate significant regional, national or international impact through their research. Recipients are expected to contribute innovative research with potential for significant impact.
scholarships.program_type: University doctoral entrance scholarship
scholarships.name: Dalhousie Research Excellence Scholarship (DRES)

scholarships.title: National Humanities Center Residential Fellowship
scholarships.degree: PhD (terminal degree required; postdoctoral researchers and doctoral candidates are not eligible)
scholarships.description: The National Humanities Center is a private, nonprofit organization and the only independent institute dedicated exclusively to advanced study in all areas of the humanities. Its Residential Fellowship offers scholars the time, space and support to pursue their work and the opportunity to take part in the Center's intellectual community.
scholarships.deadline: Applications open July 1; deadline October 1; letters of recommendation due October 8
scholarships.deadline_display: Applications open July 1; deadline October 1; letters of recommendation due October 8
eligibility: The applicant holds a PhD or relevant terminal degree for their primary discipline (for example an MFA for research-based non-fiction writers).

The PhD or requisite terminal degree was received at least five years prior to 1 October 2027, that is no later than 30 September 2022; or the applicant meets the requirements for the Geiss-Hsu or Philip L. Quinn fellowships.
The applicant has published at least one scholarly monograph, for book-focused fields, or the equivalent in peer-reviewed scholarship for article-focused fields.
The applicant is working on a project beyond the dissertation and is engaged in humanities research that will result in publication.
The proposed project is at an advanced stage, meaning that most of the research is done and the applicant is already writing.
The applicant plans to spend the full term, one or two semesters, in residence at the Center; extended time away including trips for field research is not permitted.
The applicant speaks and reads English fluently; it is not required that the primary project publication be written in English.
benefits: Individually determined stipend (the Center seeks to provide about half of the Fellow's salary)
Round-trip travel to Durham, North Carolina and back for the Fellow and immediate family living with the Fellow
requirements: 1,000-word project proposal
Short bibliography
Brief curriculum vitae (maximum four pages)
One-page tentative outline of the project structure
Three letters of recommendation (due October 8)
scholarships.duration: Academic year (September-May), or fall semester (September-December) or spring semester (January-May)
scholarships.application_period: Opens July 1, closes October 1 (letters of recommendation October 8)
scholarships.selection_notes: Applicants are informed by email in February; the fellowship class is typically announced in early April; all applicants receive final notification by the end of March. Alternates are offered fellowships by telephone.
scholarships.program_type: Independent humanities institute research fellowship (private nonprofit)
scholarships.name: National Humanities Center Residential Fellowship

scholarships.title: Horatio Alger Association National Scholarship
scholarships.description: The Horatio Alger Association is a US non-profit organisation dedicated to helping high-school students who face significant financial obstacles and demonstrating that a college education is attainable through scholarships, mentoring and other programs. This scholarship programme supports US high-school juniors who can demonstrate strong academic potential, perseverance in overcoming adversity and service to their community, aiming to help them attend a US college or university.
scholarships.deadline: Applications open 1 December and close 1 March (next cycle: 1 December 2026 - 1 March 2027)
scholarships.deadline_display: Applications open 1 December and close 1 March (next cycle: 1 December 2026 - 1 March 2027)
eligibility: Enrolled full time as a high school junior in the United States
Strong commitment to pursue and complete a bachelor's degree at an accredited non-profit public or private institution in the United States immediately after high school graduation
Demonstrates financial need: USD 100,000 or lower adjusted gross family income is required
Involved in co-curricular and community service activities
Displays integrity and perseverance in overcoming adversity
Minimum grade point average of 2.0
United States citizen
benefits: USD 25,000 scholarship award used towards undergraduate tuition and education costs at a US accredited institution
requirements: Complete the online Horatio Alger application during the published application period
Write essay responses describing the Horatio Alger story and the American Dream experience
Provide a high school transcript that includes fall grades
Provide income verification, most often the parents' tax form
Provide your school counselor's email so the counselor can submit the Counselor Certification Form
Provide the email of an adult over 21 who is not related to you and is familiar with the adversity described, who then reviews and confirms the adversity section

scholarships.selection_notes: The Association states that while most other scholarships focus exclusively on academic achievement or leadership potential, Horatio Alger Scholarships are also intended for promising students who have critical financial need, demonstrate integrity and perseverance in overcoming adversity, and are determined to succeed. scholarships.program_type: Need-based scholarship from a non-governmental organisation
scholarships.name: Horatio Alger Association National Scholarship

scholarships.deadline_display: August 1, November 1, February 1 at 11:59 p.m. EST

Enrolled in or applying to full-time or part-time post-secondary study
Studying in college, university, a skilled trade, an apprenticeship or a technology programme
Certificate or diploma programmes of one month to four years duration are eligible for the Skilled Trades stream

Certificate, diploma, college and university study costs

scholarships.application_period: For the September 2026 to August 2027 academic year, with deadlines on 1 August, 1 November and 1 February at 11:59 p.m. EST. The next applicable deadline after 2026-10-04 is 1 November 2026.
