scholarships.name: Building Brighter Futures: Bursaries and Scholarships (Indspire)

scholarships.title: Perimeter Institute PhD Residency Program Award
scholarships.funding: Doctoral funding package (university salary plus Perimeter top-up)
scholarships.description: Perimeter Institute awards a PhD Residency Program Award to doctoral students admitted to a partner Canadian university and supervised by a Perimeter faculty member, associate faculty member or senior researcher. The official page states that resident PhD students are financially supported through their home university, typically for four years or twelve academic terms, and that the Residency Award adds top-up funding up to $30,000 per year, calculated after fees and tuition, on a September to August academic year, until Term 12. Benefits also include a dedicated desk in a shared workspace, access to Perimeter facilities, a 50% discount at the on-site Black Hole Bistro, and a technology grant of up to $2,000.
eligibility: Apply to a PhD programme at a Perimeter partner university
Secure a supervisor who holds a Perimeter faculty, associate faculty or senior researcher appointment
Submit a separate Expression of Interest to the Perimeter PhD Residency Program Award
Upload the partner-university offer letter to the Expression of Interest application
Current PhD students may apply by indicating their university, term and supervisor
benefits: Top-up funding to $30,000 per year after fees and tuition until Term 12
Dedicated desk in a shared workspace at Perimeter Institute
Access to Perimeter Institute facilities, resources and scientific activities
50% discount at the on-site Black Hole Bistro
Technology grant of up to $2,000 for research-supporting technology
Mentorship from other PhD students and postdocs, and the opportunity to mentor an MSc student
Support and accommodations throughout the application process for applicants with disabilities
requirements: One Expression of Interest listing up to five Perimeter Faculty or Senior Researchers

scholarships.title: Mauritius-Africa Scholarship Scheme (MASS)
scholarships.description: The Mauritius-Africa Scholarship Scheme is the Government of Mauritius scholarship for African students, run by the Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science and Research and open to resident citizens of African Union member states and African Commonwealth countries. The 2026 edition funds Diploma, Bachelor's, MPhil and PhD study at public higher education institutions in Mauritius, paying tuition and course-related costs up to a published cap, a monthly living allowance of MUR 16,500 and a return airfare, while requiring awardees to have already secured or applied for a place at a listed Mauritian public institution. Applications are routed through a nominating agency in the applicant's own country, so the Ministry does not accept direct applications.
scholarships.deadline: No central date is published: each nominating agency sets its own deadline and communicates it to prospective applicants. For the 2026 edition the Mauritian public universities opened their own application windows from October 2025 and closed them between February and March 2026, so the next edition is expected to follow the same annual cycle.
scholarships.deadline_display: No central date is published: each nominating agency sets its own deadline and communicates it to prospective applicants. For the 2026 edition the Mauritian public universities opened their own application windows from October 2025 and closed them between February and March 2026, so the next edition is expected to follow the same annual cycle.
eligibility: Be a resident citizen of an African Union member state or an African Commonwealth country
For undergraduate programmes, be above 18 and not yet 26 on 1 January of the intake year
For MPhil, MPhil/PhD and PhD programmes, not yet 40 on 1 January of the intake year
Have already applied for a full-time on-campus Diploma, Degree, MPhil or PhD programme at a listed public higher education institution in Mauritius for the intake year
Hold a qualifying examination result with an overall average of about 60% or 12/20, or the A-level equivalent, or an equivalent qualification
Provide TOEFL 550 (paper), 213 (computer) or 79 (internet), or IELTS 5.5, where the language of instruction in the qualifying examination was not English
Not already hold an undergraduate degree when applying for an undergraduate programme
Not be a self-financing African student already studying in Mauritius applying for the same programme level
benefits: Annual payment of fees and study-related costs up to MUR 100,000 for beneficiaries from SADC countries and MUR 160,000 for beneficiaries from non-SADC countries
Monthly living allowance of MUR 16,500 credited monthly against evidence of attendance from the institution
Return airfare from the country of origin to Mauritius and back after successful completion of the scholarship period
Student visa and provisional entry permit arranged by the host institution
Refunded university application fee for successful applicants
requirements: Submit the application through the nominating agency in your own country; applications not processed through a nominating agency are not considered
Obtain either a conditional offer from your chosen Mauritian public institution or proof of having paid its application fee
Produce original educational certificates in Mauritius within two weeks of arrival
Undergo a medical check-up in a Mauritian public hospital within one month of arrival
Not interrupt studies to take up employment, which terminates the award and requires refund of the whole amount paid
Inform the institution and the Ministry at least two weeks before any travel out of Mauritius
Ensure the host institution submits quarterly attendance and progress reports to support continued disbursement
scholarships.duration: Diploma up to three years, Bachelor's up to four years, MPhil up to two years plus six months for thesis defence, MPhil/PhD up to three years plus six months for the transfer report plus one year plus six months for the thesis defence, PhD up to three years plus six months
scholarships.application_period: Annual edition published by the Ministry, with applications made through the nominating agency in the applicant's country and in parallel with the chosen Mauritian public university's admission window
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection is on merit, after all attached conditions are satisfied and the host institution confirms a seat has been offered. Applications without endorsement from a nominating agency, or from the Ministry of Education where no agency exists, are not considered. Candidates not informed of selection within six months of the application deadline should consider themselves not selected, and the Ministry does not respond to individual queries. The final and binding decision on award rests with the Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science and Research, and the Government reserves the right to offer no scholarship at all following a call.

scholarships.title: Fulbright-Garcia Robles Graduate Degree Program (COMEXUS, Mexico)

COMEXUS will fund up to two academic years for a master's and up to three academic years for a PhD, with an initial academic year of funding and continuation subject to academic performance and availability of funds. Financial support comprises monthly maintenance, one round-trip international air ticket for the grantee, a Fulbright medical benefit plan, COMEXUS assistance with visa paperwork, and up to 50,000 pesos per academic year to cover tuition. scholarships.title: Posse Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: The Posse Foundation awards a full-tuition scholarship to each Posse Scholar to attend one of its partner colleges or universities in the United States. Students cannot apply directly: they must be nominated by their high school or a community-based organisation in one of Posse's more than 20 recruitment cities, and they take part in Posse's Dynamic Assessment Process nomination programme. Posse describes the scholarship as neither a minority nor a need-based award, and states that it is open to students of all backgrounds. Beyond tuition, Posse runs a Pre-Collegiate Training programme before college, a Campus Program with staff and faculty mentors once enrolled, Posse Plus retreats, a Career Program and a Fellowship Program for alumni.

HEC awards fully funded places to Bangladeshi citizens to study medicine, engineering, computer science, business administration, mass communication, media studies, and basic and social sciences at Pakistani public and private universities, across Bachelor's, Master's and PhD levels. scholarships.title: HKUST Global Learners Scholarship
scholarships.description: The Global Learners Scholarship was established by HKUST to support the University's strategic objective of enhancing the diversity of its student community. Applicants do not apply for it: all undergraduate programme applicants from underrepresented nationalities are considered automatically, and the decision is normally communicated with the offer of admission. Awardees receive a full tuition waiver that is renewable for the normal duration of the study, subject to satisfactory academic performance, and a School or Programme Office may add a top-up as long as the combined limit of full tuition fee plus an HK$60,000 annual allowance is not exceeded. The University opened its online application system for 2027/28 entry in early October 2026, with a Priority Round deadline of 25 November 2026.

scholarships.title: ITB International Undergraduate Scholarship
scholarships.description: The ITB International Undergraduate Scholarship is a fully funded grant run through Institut Teknologi Bandung's financial aid office for selected young applicants from partner countries in ASEAN, the Asia-Pacific and Africa who want to study at Indonesia's leading technological university. The published package covers the whole S1 degree: full exemption from tuition fees for all eight academic semesters, a monthly living allowance of IDR 4,700,000, a one-time arrival settlement of IDR 10,000,000 to secure private off-campus accommodation, a round-trip economy air ticket at cost to Jakarta, basic health insurance and visa fee coverage. Applicants must hold a 12-year high school diploma with a GPA of at least 3.00 out of 4.00 and IELTS 6.0 or an accepted equivalent, and the university provides no dormitory support.

scholarships.description: Curtin University's John Curtin Global Excellence Scholarship gives eligible international, fee-paying, non-sponsored students 40% off the tuition fee of their course, credited for up to four years of an undergraduate degree or two years of a Master's by coursework. Applicants need a Course-Weighted Average of 95% or equivalent in their most recent eligible study and must study at a Curtin Western Australian campus commencing in 2027 or 2028. No separate scholarship application is needed: all qualifying applications to Curtin are assessed automatically by Global Admissions.
scholarships.deadline: 1 October 2027 (applications opened 27 July 2026)
scholarships.deadline_display: 1 October 2027 (applications opened 27 July 2026)
eligibility: Be an international, fee-paying, non-sponsored student of any nationality except Australian
Be enrolled in a Curtin undergraduate degree course or a Master's degree by coursework
Will be studying at a Curtin Western Australian campus commencing in 2027 or 2028
Have achieved a Course-Weighted Average of 95% or equivalent scores in the most recent and eligible course of study, as determined by Curtin University
Not be enrolled in Not-for-Degree Exchange or Study Abroad, a campus transfer from a Curtin global campus, or a recognised joint program at a Curtin Transnational Partner Location outside Australia
Not be enrolled in one of the excluded courses
benefits: 40% tuition fee reduction for the duration of the scholarship term
requirements: Must maintain enrolment as an international full fee-paying, non-sponsored student during the scholarship
Must maintain 'Good Standing' academic status and a minimum CWA of 70% from the second study period onwards in every study period
Must maintain full-time enrolment in each study period; underloading does not extend the scholarship term
Must not be on Leave of Absence during the scholarship term
Must not be withdrawn or AWOL from Curtin
Must not receive, hold or be awarded any other Curtin or Australian government scholarship while in receipt of this one
Must pay the full Deposit amount set out in the Letter of Offer for the first study period to accept the scholarship offer
Must accept the Letter of Offer and enrol in the course by the specified date
scholarships.duration: Credited for up to 4 years for an undergraduate degree, or a maximum of 2 years for a Master's degree by coursework
scholarships.application_period: Applications open 27 July 2026 and close 1 October 2027, for study commencing 2027 or 2028 at a Curtin Western Australian campus.
scholarships.selection_notes: Merit based. The CWA threshold of 95% or equivalent is determined by Curtin University and may change without notice, as may the list of excluded courses. Curtin reserves the right to cease offering the scholarship if the offer is not accepted by the due date or all places are filled.
scholarships.program_type: University merit scholarship
scholarships.funding_type: Tuition Fee Waiver (40% of tuition fee for the scholarship term)
scholarships.name: John Curtin Global Excellence Scholarship (Curtin University)

scholarships.title: New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura Education Awards
scholarships.description: The Education Awards are an annual programme of sponsored grants from the New Zealand charitable trust New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura, supporting women returning to or continuing education. Awards are sized by qualification level, at NZD 1,000 for NZQCF levels 3-4, NZD 1,500 for levels 5-6 and NZD 3,000 for level 7. Targeted streams exist for refugee and migrant women, STEM degree students, trade and apprenticeship women, solo parents, and Pasifika women in Early Childhood or Primary Education.
scholarships.deadline: 11.59 pm, Tuesday 25 August 2026 (round now closed)
scholarships.deadline_display: 11.59 pm, Tuesday 25 August 2026 (round now closed)
eligibility: Be enrolled in an NZQA or Universities New Zealand approved tertiary qualification for study in 2027, in any field of study
Be a New Zealand citizen, or be ordinarily resident in New Zealand and either have lived here on a resident-class visa for at least three years, or be a refugee or protected person of New Zealand
Be studying at certificate level (NZQCF level 3-4), diploma level (NZQCF level 5-6) or degree level (NZQCF level 7)
Have not previously received a New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura award at the level of study being applied for
Not be enrolled in secondary school at the time of applying, unless enrolled as an adult student
benefits: A one-off grant of NZD 1,000 to NZD 3,000 depending on qualification level
Access to targeted award streams for refugee and migrant women, Pasifika women, STEM women, trade and apprenticeship women, and solo parents
Support for non-traditional study fields and for women who have shown community leadership
requirements: Successful applicants must provide certified evidence of their 2027 course enrolment and identity before receiving the money
Must not previously have received a Trust award at the same level of study
scholarships.duration: One-off award for a single qualification; a previous recipient cannot apply again at the same level of study
scholarships.application_period: The Trust's Education Awards page states 'Applications are CLOSED' and that all applications will receive a response in October 2026, for study in 2027. No next opening date is published on the Trust's own site.
scholarships.selection_notes: The Trust states it is not looking for perfect grades and instead values determination and potential to complete the programme. Selection emphasis is on academic potential and commitment to education, background information including reasons for returning to education and future study or employment goals, and the impact the award will have on the applicant's success.
scholarships.program_type: Charitable trust grant programme (women returning to education, with targeted streams for refugee, migrant, Pasifika, STEM, trade and solo-parent students)
scholarships.name: New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura Education Awards

scholarships.title: Sonja Davies Peace Award Fund
scholarships.description: The Sonja Davies Peace Award Fund promotes initiatives that advance peace in New Zealand and is open to a woman, or a group led by a woman, developing an initiative at home, school, the workplace or in the community. It commemorates Sonja Davies, a New Zealand women's rights campaigner and politician, and includes work on family violence, inter-group understanding, mediation and conflict resolution. Awards are worth up to NZD 4,000, and the Trust publishes the 2026 application window as 12 to 30 October.
scholarships.deadline: 30 October 2026
scholarships.deadline_display: 30 October 2026
eligibility: Be a woman, or be the project leader of a group where the leader is a woman
Be one of: an informal group with peace promotion among its stated aims, an individual enrolled at a tertiary institution, or a formal group
Be a New Zealand citizen, or hold a resident class visa, and currently live in New Zealand
Not have previously received a New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura Award
Be developing an initiative that will advance peace in New Zealand
benefits: Up to NZD 4,000 of project funding
Recognition as a Sonja Davies Peace Award recipient from a national women's charitable trust
Support for initiatives addressing family violence, inter-group understanding, mediation and conflict resolution
requirements: Must submit a project timeline and budget indicating how the funds will be spent
Must describe the initiative and how it will advance peace in New Zealand
Must demonstrate experience of and capability to conduct the initiative
Must not have previously received a New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura Award
scholarships.duration: One-off grant for a defined project with a submitted timeline and budget
scholarships.application_period: The Trust publishes that the application window is open from 12 to 30 October 2026. That window opens eight days after this verification date.
scholarships.selection_notes: The Trust's selection panel considers three things: experience of and demonstrated capability to conduct the initiative; a description of the initiative and how it will advance peace in New Zealand; and a project timeline and budget indicating how funds will be spent. Previous recipients of any New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura award are ineligible, so this cannot be combined with the Trust's Education, Research or Personal Growth awards.
scholarships.program_type: Charitable trust project grant (women-led peace and conflict-resolution initiatives, open to tertiary students)
scholarships.name: Sonja Davies Peace Award Fund

scholarships.title: ILSC Humanitarian Scholarship
scholarships.description: The ILSC Humanitarian Scholarship gives refugees living in Australia three sessions of English language study to overcome the language barrier that stops newly arrived refugees from entering tertiary education or employment. It covers 11 to 12 weeks of English tuition in groups, all learning materials and resources, and administrative fees, plus free Duolingo Premium for the placement. Two scholarships per campus are available every three sessions, and applications are open year-round.
scholarships.deadline: Rolling intake - applications are open year-round and no closing date is published
scholarships.deadline_display: Rolling intake - applications are open year-round and no closing date is published
eligibility: Hold, or be on a bridging visa for, one of the Australian humanitarian visa subclasses 200, 201, 202, 203, 204, 785, 790, 851 or 866
Be at least 18 years of age at the commencement of studies
Live within commuting distance of the ILSC-Adelaide, ILSC-Brisbane, ILSC-Melbourne, ILSC-Sydney or ILSC-Perth campus
Not have received a Centrelink Relocation Grant
Not have received the ILSC Humanitarian Scholarship before
benefits: Three sessions of English language study, structured as four-week sessions except in December
All learning materials and resources
Administrative fees covered
Free Duolingo Premium for the duration of the placement, sponsored by Duolingo
Access to free events and clubs on campus
Barista skills development through the Cafe Work Skills course
Access to other selective courses matched to the applicant's interests
requirements: Must be able to provide proof of an Australian humanitarian visa or the relevant bridging visa
Must complete the free ILSC Online English Placement Test, and must reach at least Pre-intermediate
Must not have received a Centrelink Relocation Grant
Must not have received the ILSC Humanitarian Scholarship previously
Must maintain a minimum attendance of 80 per cent during the programme
Must accept the scholarship offer within 48 hours, or it is withdrawn and offered to another candidate
Course selections and timetables are subject to availability on enrolment, and confirmed start dates cannot be deferred
scholarships.duration: Three sessions, with one session lasting four weeks except in December
scholarships.application_period: Applications are open year-round. Applicants receive a link to complete ILSC's Online English Placement Test, which must be completed by the deadline stated in that email, and successful candidates are offered the earliest available date.
scholarships.selection_notes: Scholarship candidates are selected by a committee of staff and teachers at the ILSC Australia schools. Successful candidates are offered the scholarship based on the earliest available date. ILSC states it does not discriminate on the basis of race, colour, national origin, disability, age, gender, sexual orientation or religion.
scholarships.program_type: Private education provider scholarship (refugees and asylum seekers on Australian humanitarian visas)
scholarships.name: ILSC Humanitarian Scholarship

scholarships.title: Government of Guyana Scholarships
scholarships.description: The Government of Guyana advertises and administers its national scholarship awards through the Ministry of Public Service, Government Efficiency and Implementation in three categories: undergraduate, technical and vocational education, and postgraduate, based on national workforce requirements. Beneficiaries receive full tuition plus allowances for books, outfit and travelling, and graduates are bonded by contract and guaranteed a public sector job after completing their studies. Each award is advertised separately with its own requirements, on the Ministry's website, in the newspapers and on the Ministry's social media pages.

Meet any language requirement named in the advertisement, for example fluency in Spanish for the Guyana to Chile scholarships

Administered by SAIA, n.o., it funds living costs for study, research or artistic stays abroad (outgoing track) or in Slovakia (incoming track), with a distance-based travel grant.

Outgoing track: hold permanent residence in Slovakia
Incoming track: be a foreign student, doctoral candidate, university teacher, researcher or artist invited to a Slovak higher education institution or research organisation
Have a selected foreign higher education institution or research workplace, or a Slovak host institution, for the proposed stay
Apply within the published round for the intended semester
benefits: Living costs during the study, research or artistic stay
Separate travel grant for eligible Slovak applicants

scholarships.title: Cost Sharing Overseas PhD Scholarships Scheme with Australian Universities (TSLS, Government of Fiji)
scholarships.description: The Cost Sharing Overseas PhD Scheme is a TSLS scholarship, revamped to partially support Fiji citizens undertaking full-time PhD study at ten eligible universities in Australia. Under the cost-sharing arrangement the tuition fee is borne by the partner university in Australia or New Zealand, while TSLS provides a living allowance, airfare, visa and health cover support and other allowances. Five awards are available for the 2026-2027 Financial Year.
eligibility: Be a Fiji citizen
Be ordinarily resident in Fiji for at least three (3) years before the award commencement date unless determined by the Service
Secure an offer letter or candidature based on the eligible university's requirements for full-time mode, unless determined otherwise by the Service or arranged with an employer
Demonstrate the direct and applied relevance of the research study towards Fiji's workforce needs and development
Be less than 50 years at the time of application
Not be an existing TSLS sponsored student or graduate on active bond service, or sponsored through any other agency
benefits: Living allowance at a minimum AUD/NZD of $32,000 or at a local market rate
Economy Class yearly return airfare
Visa Fees up to $3000 FJD
Overseas student health cover fee for sponsored students only
Establishment allowance, a one-off payment at the beginning of the programme, at a maximum rate of AUD/NZD $3500

Excess baggage allowance at a maximum rate of AUD/NZD $300, and a field grant of up to AUD/NZD $3,000 only if the student is required and approved to undertake field surveys for primary data collection
requirements: Register on the TSLS Apply portal, complete the online form and submit the application
Hold an offer letter or candidature from one of the 10 listed Australian universities
Frame the research around Fiji's workforce and development needs
scholarships.duration: Not published on the scheme page; the TSLS Scholarship Policies Handbook covers this
scholarships.application_period: TSLS published its 2027 Scholarship Policies Handbook in September 2026 and its TSLS Apply portal was live and linked as "Apply Now" on the scheme page when checked on 2026-10-04. TSLS does not publish a closing date on the scheme page.
scholarships.selection_notes: 39 awards are available under the scheme across twelve priority disciplines: Medical and Health Services; Engineering Services; Climate Change/Environmental Science; Marine Science; Forestry; Public Policy and Analysis; Economic Modelling and Policies; Public Financing; Inclusive Education; Information Technology Services; Social Science; Border Security. Eligible institutions are 10 Australian universities: CQ University Australia, Griffith, Monash, Queensland University of Technology, Swinburne, University of Newcastle, UNSW, University of Queensland, Western Sydney and RMIT.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship (Fiji Tertiary Scholarships and Loans Service statutory scheme)
scholarships.name: Cost Sharing Overseas PhD Scholarships Scheme with Australian Universities (TSLS, Government of Fiji)

scholarships.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at The American University in Cairo
scholarships.description: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at AUC is a fully packaged graduate fellowship for African students, starting with the Spring 2027 cohort, under which AUC intends to award fellowships to 300 graduate students in fields that promote African economic development. It targets academically talented young Africans with leadership potential who face the highest economic and social barriers. The award is granted for the total study period of the degree on full-time enrolment, subject to review every semester for satisfactory academic performance, and it covers tuition, a stipend, a laptop, health insurance, university accommodation, local transport and, for fellows who do not already reside in Egypt, roundtrip airfare. Application requires two separate steps: the AUC graduate application and a dedicated Mastercard Foundation Scholars application.

Bachelor's degree with a minimum overall GPA of 3.2 on a 4.0 scale or equivalent
Showcase financial need
Women, forcibly displaced people and/or people living with disabilities are highly encouraged to apply
benefits: Tuition fees for nine credits per semester
Stipend during the fall and spring semesters
One laptop is provided
Student services and activities fees
Medical service and health insurance fees
Accommodation in university dorms/residence
AUC bus subscription (or travel allowance)
May cover remedial English modules or intensive English courses
Roundtrip airfare provided for fellows not residing in Egypt
Some candidates may be eligible for additional funding to cover research, publication fees and conference attendance
Special software subscriptions or IT purchases for those with disabilities
requirements: Must maintain full-time status
Must maintain a minimum GPA of 3.2
Fellows are assigned 12 hours per week of related academic work
A teaching assistantship mandatory training must be completed per University requirements if the fellow is involved in teaching assistantship duties

Date of birth after 31 December 1991
Detailed research plan with timeline specifying key milestones and activities

If already in Switzerland: date of entry must not be earlier than 1 August 2026
Art Master's: Bachelor's degree completed by 31 July 2027; must not already hold a Master's degree
Art Master's: Admission letter or proof of application from Swiss University of the Arts or Music
